egor.title: BUTTERFLIES, KNIVES
egor.text:
ran together ran apart amicably
you know show me someone without sin
makes no difference I'll take anyone down
words hearts butterflies knives

undress forget like a poet's blade
across skin like across the September sky
because if it was fun then this
cannot be a war cri—

I don't eat don't drink don't fuck and I don't play
the fool at cards for money
out of spite I don't ask how you are
though of course I know you're not okay

I'd serve myself up on a saucer a slice a spoon
you're a girl I'm a boy heh heh heh
I love you so much how long can this go on
what will you do to me I'm in another poem

egor.title: TOMORROW
egor.text:
Like a hard candy pressed against the gum
and disappearing.
We're still here together, but we're already gone.
I was so busy,

so very busy that I couldn't tell you,
but you know ---
I fell in love with you for the naked eyes
of other people's fires.

They bring the bill --- and once again fifteen hundred
thins down to two hundred.
The thing no little cross worn on the chest
can guard or save you from.

It darts and howls, pressing its face
to doors and to the word.
The thing you can't outrun near Kherson
or in Barcelona.

I was so busy that I forgot to tell you.
I'll send it on a postcard:
how the world tightens its time zones
around a suicide bomber.

Put on a song for us, we'll stare at the dawn,
a prayer-mantra.
We're still here together, but we're already gone.
We're already in tomorrow.

We're already where there are no incoming strikes or bangs,
no fallen pawns.
And with us is a swarm of poem-fireflies
all lit up and crazed.

We're already in tomorrow, as if without sins
or dimensions.
When I go to meet you, I'll pick an armful of poems
and daisies.

egor.title: PICK-ME
egor.text:
Sick karma and berry gum from childhood.
Big Pharma in Uncle Paracelsus's nightmares.
If you spot a wounded man --- take more careful aim.
Keep away from liberals and the lit-process.

Stay closer to the one who gives you freedom for free
in a routine scorched like a field near Soledar.
Brains liquefied by TikTok and Telegram.
Lie down, I'll lick your juices with filigree precision.

Your parents were God and a night star.
My parents were naked when they conceived me.
Don't come near me, don't touch me, darling.
The Motherland inside me sobs as wildly as a sick woman.

I've grown handsome, like a ronin in line for fugu.
I have strength left for one last dash and one seppuku.
Strength left for one last line (it goes in circles).
But disgusting is the man who prays out of fright.

Of two evils I always chose sharpened pikes,
while the girls of TikTok decided who was more pick-me,
while the boys spun the casino under the shadow of a FAB bomb
and vanished like cringe and hype when vibe arrived.

Poet women in fearless poses made me fall for them,
and permanent Russian snow (even when it was pink).
I drank and sang like a sick man, dreamed in word and deed
of loving people --- in a trench, in a church, or in a brothel.

Loving people through carrion, gloss, and mother-of-pearl.
Going to the shore, standing there, crying tears inward.
Spending half a life building my monastery out of an italic line,
only to set it alight after the tonsure, like Mishima.

Being a bare wire, striking without meaning or message.
Pouring LED colors into the darkness of Khrushchev blocks.
Second: it hurts. First: it is beautiful.
Wherever we arrive, there will be a feat and there will be a feast.

egor.title: CAT
egor.text:
A cat looks at me. Neither wild nor domestic.
Three thousand and thirty-three yellow-eyed nights.
Stuck somewhere in the middle of his ninth life,
breathing easily.
Something unsaid hangs in the air,
something premature in the pack of cigarettes.
We're alike, yes. I'm almost the same, really.
No longer an animal. Still far from a soul.

Still far, little brother? How much longer?
Am I prey or the one who feeds?
Am I in the fire or am I master of all the fire?
The world has been left on an ellipsis.
In the middle of the ninth life,
with such perfect concentration,
the cat looks at me.

With malice and tenderness, my mysterious little friend.
I look the same way at the cold sky
that will receive me,
as the cat looks at me ---
his leap is no more frightening than mine.

The only frightening thing is if one of us doesn't make the jump.

egor.title: PROPHETIC
egor.text:
May the address always be right, and the text prophetic.
In a letter about love as real as the view from the window,
with Admiralty shipyards and children's things,
and the neighbor's cat staring huge-eyed from the sky.

May it not exactly happen, but be simpler:
as if you dreamed your whole life and suddenly cried in the morning
from happiness that is everywhere, like salt or air:
in the kitchen, in the hospital, inside you, at your parents' dacha.

And here, where the night ends, carrying away so much
of what seemed not to be a dream and glittered like claws.
The heavenly cat will quietly jump onto the bed,
and as soon as you stroke her, rising on one elbow ---

the doctor is already laughing with the keys to paradise,
the male nurses laugh brightly, broad-shouldered and warm-hearted,
and your god laughs, taking the whole world away from you,
and of course you don't hold petty things against him.

egor.title: WHEN THE CHERRY TREES BLOOM
egor.text:
When the cherry trees bloom, I'll sweep out of the corners
all the death, spiders, skeletons, and commas.
Poems that seemed immortal and holy,
their letters tangled, will become dust on the tongue,
a residue of prayer, tiny soundless grains of powder.
When the cherry trees bloom, punching a hole through my ceiling,
when the cherry trees bloom, you'll call me,
you'll call me --- and we'll go
skipping through gardens, springing out through little windows.
From one branch, yes, nothing but pits beneath the flesh.
With one silly girl, under a little tree,
hiding from the storm.
In spring, in the morning, on a staircase,
talking, complaining, crying.
When they bloom, when the cherry trees bloom,
tell me something good (speak more quietly),
tell me something unasked-for, tell me too much,
tell me everything --- don't be petty, tell me everything.
Those miserable Februaries must have existed for something.
Death must have existed for something,
and with it --- spiders, skeletons, and commas.
They must have been there for something.

egor.title: THE LAST DANCE
egor.text:
Who grew up here with everything handed to him, everything flashy.
Who hunched his back here with cattle, beasts, rabble.
Who was bewitched by the Motherland, who was hammered by it.
Who was cuckolded by the Motherland, spat on, sold.

Who sang here like a quail, shone like a deal.
Drank shot after shot, delighted like a child.
Who was torn apart by time, who was made sturdy,
and for that was depicted on its icons.

Who survived here by a miracle, who chewed the living.
Walked himself like crooked-legged undead.
Who listened here to every bark and howl,
the rumble of third-class train cars, grinding, wheezing, snoring.

Who spent the day in chores and the evening in poisons.
Who pulled the load, who drove flags in like crosses.
For yet another new world-disorder,
suddenly exploding into fanfares and fronts.

Who twisted the necks of pocket-sized tits until they crunched.
Licked condensed milk from the breasts of ladybirds.
Trenches lay across the Russian language like scars.
But it isn't our first time driving devils under the bunk.

Fall in love every day like a holy half-wit.
Become Cyrillic in poems, in cracks in asphalt.
Take my hand, everyone who has remained here.
Everyone who has not accepted the smallness of being human.

egor.title: TODAY I FEEL ALMOST SICK, BUT I DON'T TRUST PHARMACIES
egor.text:
Today I feel almost sick, but I don't trust pharmacies.
Come stand by the river with a black coffee to go.
By accident we invented a new Silver Age for them ---
when all we wanted was to remain ourselves in perdition.

So everything that wakes us and howls would get the hell out of here.
Look there: the hard sign is abolished, the yat is abolished.
Today I feel almost alive and almost happy.
Come stand by the river, just stand there for no reason.

egor.title: CREED
egor.text:
You believe in me as if in Sochi; before your eyes you see a symbol of luck.
The dandy is flawless and damned, a corkscrew driven under the heart as into sangria.
When I come to you at night, come to you alone at night and cry,
hold me close, let the number of ribs feel even, feel equal.

The amount of pain, the amount of dark rum --- the amount of death.
A pirate bay on the gray Gulf of Finland.
The amount of life --- barely visible, the number of lines in an envelope.
The guitar is badly tuned and the guests sing off-key.

You think I keep silent like a scout, like someone in a long captivity without end or limit ---
but I'm only trying not to die at the beginning.
I'm a black pawn on a square (remind the war that White didn't start it).
And those standing beside me are eaten bones and all.

But you believe in me. And believe you see a symbol of luck with your own eyes.
I'll keep writing to you as long as you breathe.
When I come to you at night, come to you alone at night and cry ---
find the right word out of thousands upon thousands.

Everything is mixed in you: mother, father, the one and only friend-comandante,
and a love for which it would be a sin not to raise a revolver.
We stand at the station, Petersburg all around us, and the eyes ask: “Where are you going?”
My symbol of faith, my symbol of faith, my creed.

egor.title: SKETCHES
egor.text:
This is not us, only sketches. Not us, only
sketches. A child's palm, a lifeline.
This is not me and not you. Sinless
is our path, bloodless, undecided.
Like the distance between an easel and a raised pencil.

This is not me and not you. For now, only
inside an envelope --- a letter without a word. A letter in an envelope.

There is so much good around us here, look:
nothing but love, solid love --- and a little death.

The soul is a stone that asks to go into the sea beneath the tide.
Only a stone on the shore above the damp sand.
If there is stone and darkness --- you become a reef.
If there is stone and light --- you become a lighthouse.

But until the choice is made, the sea turns you however it wants.
All life is a long preface, an entr'acte.
Nothing but love. Solid love. And a little death.

Still not us, only sketches, only sketches.

egor.title: OUTSKIRTS OF ROME
egor.text:
Our time has come. To catch theorems behind numbers.
The second is simple-hearted, worthy, and properly prima.

The boy Remus fell asleep on the she-wolf. And Remus dreamed
of future people building the outskirts of Rome.

Our time --- is now. This joy --- perhaps it is blind.
And let it be: gratitude need not hide from “Grazie.”

The boy Romulus, pressed against his brother, watched as he fell asleep
how trains were set flying to outlying stations.

Here there are flower-people and percentage-people.
Here they walk and stare. Or hurry to the checkpoint.
We stand, and above us Latin letters glow fluorescent.
And beneath us high-voltage lines hum.

I ask you, as Romulus asked Remus, for forgiveness
for the empire's coming glory, the senate's wisdom.
Our time will end. The joy and devotion of a puppy ---
are boundless, like the map of an ever-growing city.

Our time has come. To love --- as one loves a mother or brother.
To tell apart --- victory from a banner, a wound from makeup.

We stand here together, and behind us --- the outskirts of Rome.

egor.title: BEAUTIFUL PRINCES
egor.text:
Beautiful princes fell from white horses to the bottom
of a dirty pit of serotonin syndrome (read: sadness).
Each time they thought it was the basement level, but
it always turned out someone was knocking from below.

To tear one's lower eyelid away from what is above ---
no easy task, a mission the color of the nation.
Man is Duke Franz Ferdinand to man,
slowly approaching firing range.

Oh open, open, open the eyes of newspapers,
monitors, sisters, neighbors, soldiers, and judges.
Alphabets lose their voice on “I” and “Z,”
leaving room for activity, essentially.

But the Principle is merciless, a step backward is ruinous.
The heavens cannot hear complaints like “advance pay” and “runny nose.”
So beautiful princes would fall in their eyes,
would fall ringing in their eyes, smashing themselves to death.

egor.title: EVERYTHING
egor.text:
A step left, a step right, an attempt to escape.
Where can I go from here, toward what stars?
I was carried out in someone's arms from a burning house while still an infant
by teenage soldiers drafted for Grozny.

I looked at chewing-gum wrappers, into my mother's eyes,
and through the window overlooking the zoo and the dark distance.
My father sold abroad, whole trainloads at a time,
timber. Cases were opened, then he was acquitted.

Where can I go from here, toward what stars?
As a child I learned that Kursk was a submarine.
That pain is called Beslan or Nord-Ost.
Pain, not a city. Not a musical on Dubrovka.

Where can I go from here, where grandmothers fed
their grandchildren their fill of white bread with butter and sugar?
Where, looking from the roof of a prefab block at the city and sky,
at sixteen I imagined myself the son of the Lord?

Not a step left, not a step right. Complete stillness.
Everyone is equal before a succession of alarm clocks and sunsets.
It was I who stood on Bolotnaya Square. I don't remember on which
side --- the batons or the placards.

It was I, accused of graphomania and of drinking
this and that in such-and-such a place, seeing no difference between “zdravstvuyte” and “salaam,”
---
it was I singing along with Ramazanova at Closing:
“We scatter apart, the world breaks in half.”

It was I who said it wasn't too late to believe in people.
Even if you're running with a wheel beneath your soles.
Where can I go from here, toward what stars?

I watch you sleeping. I watch you sleeping --- and that's all.

egor.title: PRAYER
egor.text:
Ran and ran, never spared my breath.
Lowered the pain threshold.
From the tempting knife to the lines worn against the body.
Spring --- no vice, hysteria --- no vice.
It will all end crosswise in a bed.
You knew that in advance.

Was bad, but didn't die. Took it as a lesson.
Stepped bloodlessly off the crooked high-speed roads.
A hungry sheet, a breath against the ceiling.
A cold interstellar breath against the ceiling.

Here is God, here is the threshold. Here is dust and its prophet.
A raspberry-red mouth. A prayer in reverse.

egor.title: FREE VERSE No. 2
egor.text:
Love is a multiplier.

Every time I leave the house,
I weave through the morning like a fresh centipede,
dodging the feet of Buddhist monks.

Every poem in my phone is a forty-day prayer for the dead;
if it's about you, if not --- it goes into recursion,
white noise into the great springtime Petersburg
sky, soaking up, like a sponge, people like me

or this woman --- forty-five, yet as if seventeen,
or this woman --- seventeen, like forty-five.

And love is a multiplier.
Without going into subtleties ---
I want to divide myself, and subtract you.

Every time I leave the house, I watch
emptiness scatter in panic
like a crowd of Buddhist monks from beneath my
rhymed and pulsing footsteps.

egor.title: PSALM 227
egor.text:
He comes to me.
*Shrapnel wound* --- he says, --- *to the head; if you can --- take it out.*
But my hands treacherously bog down in white, viscous light.
Into broken pixels, bitterness, and black earth
the seams come apart.
He inhales,
and for a second the darkness thickens in the cigarette.

*What is it like to be dead?* --- I ask.
*What is it like to be alive?* ---
he asks, and we fall silent,
not knowing how to answer one another.

They say God has no dead.
There are variables in formulas, but no dead.
There are oscillations in waves, but no dead.
There is gravity, chemistry, euphoria,
an innate fear of insects and fangs,
futurology, ethics, mythologems of Judgment Day
or the Third Rome,
serotonin receptors,
monoamino acids and polygamy ---

but there are no dead,
no dead person,
no emptiness and nonbeing.

God, they say, drives emptiness and nonbeing away deftly and precisely,
like an ice-cream seller swatting wasps away
from children by the kiosk on sunny days in May.

He comes to me all the time.
*To the head* --- he says, --- *shrapnel wound.*
*Help me* --- he says, --- *take it out.*

And I embrace him.

egor.title: ETERNAL RETURN
egor.text:
I fall in love mercilessly, broadcast it into every chat.
I burst, desperate as Admiral Kolchak,
into the measured pace of March.
My sorrow --- an imperial map from the West to Kamchatka.

It was me singing you little hopes, rocking you in my arms,
reviving you with tea, charming your pale throats,
drying your runny, roaring eyelids,
hoping with you for *the resurrection of the dead
and the life of the world to come*.

It was me weaving you ornate midnight talk,
saying daisies would grow on the scars of Khrushchev blocks,
that separation is only a dot in the atmosphere
or above a letter of the Old Russian alphabet,
that Suzume would one day close the doors
and kiss a stormtrooper,
and a hot head would drop to two-dimensional knees.

It was me preaching to you about continuity between generations,
embracing a monument to Lenin
in a crumbling, wretched city-bottom,
believing, believing, believing in the Kingdom of God on Earth,
watching corporate glass towers
screw themselves into the sky.
And we walk on, so beautiful,
so ridiculous, forgiving everything.

We walk hand in hand, walk beyond the river,
walk to the Arctic, walk to Africa,
wherever our huge Horde-like anime eyes
happen to look,
through passports and residence registrations and sinful souls ---

because everything will be resharpened, undesired,
everything will melt in March soap, in red water.

But we will not end,
we end nowhere.

egor.title: COLD SNAP
egor.text:
A cold snap. A kitten and a ball of yarn.
Tour guides dream of warm Bermuda.
Remember me as everything I failed to do
(well, let me have failed --- nothing will come of it).

Remember me like a veil,
when you're both sleeping and feverish, half-seeing,
and someone strokes you with an everyday “there, there,”
and dissolves like vitamin C in something hot.

Someday I'll become slender and holy,
but I'll sprout inside you so crookedly and absurdly.
That day an acrylic sky will crash
onto Petersburg's enormous umbrellas.

Whether to flee vodka or escape the beasts.
One endless line into soldiers and Sesames.
Not our bright handsome sons.
Not our daughters with almond-shaped eyes.

egor.title: VICTORY OVER THE SUN
egor.text:
In ninety-four Mom laughed
when Dad called a pistol a “volyna.”
The country decomposed into gas and nickel.
The working man's eye was pleased only by a glossy woman
and Romantsev's Spartak.

The dorm windows looked onto a zoo
without a single animal (unless you count the guard);
blood and syringes on the stairwells --- all that happened.

All that happened,
and all of it --- means nothing.

Then I saw a solar eclipse.
At the very beginning of autumn, on the dorm steps,
Dad smoked and took pictures, repeating:
this happens once every three thousand years.

A drunken freak on the screen babbled nonsense,
old women carried their pensions to MMM,
the streets carried death, and Mom laughed.
In ninety-four Mom always laughed.
When she cried, I was already fast asleep.

And in my sleep I saw
that I was a solar eclipse,
happening once every three thousand years.

egor.title: THOSE YOU USED TO SNORT WITH
egor.text:
Those you used to snort with leave one by one,
feet first out of rented modest burrows,
out of the windows of Khrushchev blocks, neon new builds,
caught off guard by treacherous March.

Searching for caches, on comedowns and desynchronizations
with the forest park that has chewed them up.
Leaving old age, sorrow, and little wings stitched from lies
to the tough guys, doctors, sergeants who worried about them.
Let the stigmatized one put fingers into the stigmata,
but for every clean one --- may there be neither feather nor fluff.

Those you used to snort with lie in graves; those you used to snort with
have dried into naked moss, into toothless linden honey.
Even that gray-eyed girl, even that
same-sex dancer, bodily as a salamander.
Here are the city and Tuesday, the sober pallor of the frame.
God or conscience --- who can tell in the morning.
But one more day, one more impenetrable battle,
one more dust and ashes, shining through and burning.
Those you used to snort with are watching over you
from eternal November.

egor.title: ENHEDUANNA
egor.text:
Yesterday the neighbors were making noise through the walls again.
They drank in the evening; trouble came in the morning.
Sister, what can you do, you know, these Sumerians ---
forever from nowhere and into nowhere.

Our new language, somewhere between cawing and murmuring,
flickers on a floe, the one burning inside.
Soon it will embrace everyone with March and Petersburg,
like radium against Saint Marie Curie's breast.

The century will spin: God has a soft paw.
Ask to get out --- and you'll emerge at dot com,
because the first poet in history was a woman,
not the man who compared her to a flower.

It was long ago, it was, I swear, just recently.
We're dust underfoot, puddles, so be it.
Love me, but don't kiss me, Enheduanna.
If you kiss me, I'll wake up.

egor.title: THIS IS HOW THE STEPPE BURNS
egor.text:
Look how dawn sparkles in your steppe in summer.
They set the whole world on fire, and it smoldered and zoned out online.
Don't blame me, don't accuse me, I'm like fourteen years old ---
I'm vanilla, vinyl, velvet, and the trump jack.

You're hard as progress, as an execution, as a black queen.
And inside you --- an apostle begun and a bastard finished.
And a war there's no escaping, even if you climb the walls,
and poems against which every one of us will be worn down.

So watch these steppes burn --- like a matchstick hell,
like marketable oil in a Carthaginian, Baghdad massacre.
And walk an entire life with me, the way a soldier *marches* ---
one-two, one-two into the light, my *Shagane*, my *Shagane*.

Be with me everywhere like sorrow, sing a lullaby.
I'll barely feel the blade --- as if a Gillette
purred against an inflamed cheek with incorruptible earth.
As if a lullaby angel sat down on a bulletproof vest.

egor.title: 10TN
egor.text:
the time of cheap flour and múkka
catching the Pokémon of mental anguish
a pink tail

neon chills like girls' hands
and the voice smokes the bros idiots
post a clip

long before pride and offense
stoned Conor against Khabib
who are you for

I'm only a phantom among prefab blocks
and it drags along sticky spreading
its tongue

all a children's fairy tale kind of whatever
like a blade hiding behind the cheek
without sky or bottom

poetry is gentle and seamless
and there are no masks no mask-shows
and somewhere there is war

egor.title: SPARROW SONG
egor.text:
I'll throw a white night over your shoulders,
and someone's knife will freeze, deprived of its blade,
and in the morning news ---
one less dismemberment.

April in Petrograd: every sick person's symptoms flare.
An oil depot spits, hit hard in the gut.
The imperial flag
flutters on a thin little pole.

There aren't enough workers' foreheads to repaint the country.
At the zoo the Pallas's cat still can't find love.
If the connection goes down ---
come over, I've got Chianti here.

From my window to the river --- a hundred meters and zero roads.
And poems so good that damn if anyone else could do that.
And such a spring,
sparrow-like --- just look.

zavadsky.title: SWALLOWS
zavadsky.text:
And still --- at times, as before,
you and I again lie gently to each other.
“Everything is fine,” you'll say almost inaudibly, while I ---
will simply keep quiet, losing the tone.
If I happened to be beside you --- no, this time
let's not lie ---
I merely ended up a meter higher, closer to the ceiling.
And the light bulb and the chair, as soldiers say,
may still be swaying, but long since not the same way.
I'll wake with you, fall asleep with you,
but the degree of that heat
is not what it was before --- a year ago, two years ago.
I'm still --- a boy with shard-eyes,
among steep snowdrifts, plaster, and glass.
I worry about how I'll return home,
back --- all right,
your photos and words were beside me all the time,
the ones I knew by heart, with the occasional furtive glance ---
and repeated,
and repeated, trying not to go insane.
A nest of two swallows in a long-empty barracks
will remain a nest as long as someone there is alive and waiting.
I saw only what could be seen there plainly ---
and only for the one
to whom the poem was not dedicated.
Go on, try to let go of the memory of an entire company,
all the cold of the Far East ---
it will not be as frightening as the cold of your eyes.
Yes, let somewhere far away
a mortar still thunder --- and
I'll write a letter to the one sleeping under its blasts.
I can still hear the grinding of rails,
those screams --- though truly
there it no longer matters who is a soldier and who an officer.
I only wanted to tell everything,
but the new day will remind me with a shell
of that last trailer --- left underloaded by that brigade.
Let there be neither rhyme nor meter here ---
I hadn't written for a long time,
and now --- I'm already tired even of poems.
Your eyes will truly leave me,
and I'll write about what I never wanted to see again.
Yes, I was wrong --- and I suppose I'll remain so.
I simply forgot everything, but I couldn't forget those two.
And I'll have to lie stupidly,
saying I got confused, but --- I know
that now, this time --- I was speaking only of love.
Someone will give me a hint with a hook under the ceiling,
with the soldier's belt
I gave to the one I love ---
I'll simply go on living --- long since a little tired,
but I'll gather my strength, and no, I won't repeat my path again.

zavadsky.title: MORNING, APRIL, RUSSIA
zavadsky.text:
Morning, April, Russia,
so many knocked-off latches,
for one person through the peephole ---
a worn-out ID,
for another --- something else,
and no more mercy is needed.
The stairwell is a needle-filled taiga,
where an intentionally
knocked-off front sight
of a shortened AK led the way.
That night everyone hung beautifully,
some in a club and some ---
like a lantern on a pole.
Morning, April, Russia,
and what awaits us now?

zavadsky.title: LAKERS
zavadsky.text:
Don't linger by the fence,
a worn “Lakers” logo
hides the balaclava. The needle of a mohawk
sticks up straight. And meanwhile,
it seemed so awkwardly
the lacing had changed;
behind me --- a sports bag, of course,
not a backpack and a rifle. Clothing
changed over the years.

I wipe the sweat from my forehead with my hand,
and over the fence, like Corrado,
a corrida will begin --- but who needs that?
I got twisted,
knocked completely out. And everywhere
it irritated, flickered --- stripes, swings,
other little things. The stars that night
were much brighter and sharper,
the letter --- “Blue,”
I keep seeing the devil everywhere:
penicillin, kerosene, or the FSIN.

Lord, have mercy and, please,
let me go.

zavadsky.title: SHE --- LOOKED AT THE STARS
zavadsky.text:
She --- looked at the stars,
looked and softly sang along.
I, looking like a beast,
ached
by the window.
The dancing ended long ago,
there is no ball,
the music
has finished playing,
and only one star remained.

zavadsky.title: ZH. Z. (HOSPITAL ROMANCE)
zavadsky.text:
--- I still have nothing to write to you,
like one who sees between moths --- A and O,
my gaze is pressed to the back of my head, as before I'm out of place,
and from under the brow they stare --- either me or him.
For half a year the reflection in blue tile
has reminded me who shared the ward with you --- hardly
anything remained of the sky but linen canvas
and a whetstone driven firmly into the temple.
Across the corridor, in the opposite window, he flickers while I
lie --- now slightly curled, now bent ---
shaved bare, bracing my feet against the floor,
asking you to forget me or leave me for more than a little while.

On the stair landing I scratched a couple of words
across the whole wall, filing through a metal pin.
From there looks not the one I'd wanted beside me;
by the radiator, on the floor, knees drawn up --- only you
hammered nails by touch beneath your eyelids,
silently clenched, tightened a tourniquet around your neck,
and --- grinned at yourself, as I did on all fours,
so the word might lie across the cross of my arms ---
I'll unbraid and cut a strand from my wrist,
it's time to hide myself from others --- the same kind.
Tonight I can no longer raise my hand;
kerosene waits for the throat, pliers for the nails.

I dug and rummaged, crushing the dot of an eye into a lump,
finding nothing, tearing window hinges out unevenly,
while I dive like a white feather
above the edges of snow, far away, over the platform ---
there, having left the ward, ruling lines across the wallpaper,
and left wordless everything I had decided ---
I'll say: you didn't exactly kill yourself,
you simply decided not to live.
You'll lie down, one of our own through and through, swaying a little,
leaving your finger bones in an aspen doorjamb,
and were you right when you left the one
who never asked anyone for anything?

zavadsky.title: BLANK
zavadsky.text:
Look at me, please,
you know I'm sick too.
Onto your shoulders, in the heat of your furs,
I will fall --- sharper than stakes
there my word will seem ---
drive it into a corner, tear it with your teeth,
the one who froze dead in memory
froze for a moment in the lens.

Beneath the lowered lid like a matchbox
I hid a field of red poppies;
there was close-up, there was long shot,
three hundred gazes from the ceiling ---
I saw no faces, but kissed them,
and seemed to know each one;
crumpling cellophane in the restroom,
powder stained a broken nose.

Tears slid down; sweat from the brow
was wiped only by the coolness of hands.
It wasn't tobacco that got the stairwell high,
incense had smoked out the apartment,
and plastic melted on clothes,
a sail of smoke trailed along the walls,
and what I don't regret --- the same thing
was entrusted to me by a fan of open fingers.

On the dance floor I asked for help ---
silence --- coughing blood.
In front of you the blue spread
across the crosses on the fuselage;
then the glare of spotlights scraped,
the rasp and roar of high frequencies.
I look at a spill of ink
forming the pattern of a thistle flower.

Arm in arm into the night an aperitif
leads with a Picasso stroke,
and when I stopped being able to walk,
I still didn't lean on the railing,
palm raised --- sliding down
the corner of a cedar bar counter.
Was revelry left, or risk ---
and help is not needed for free.

If only to feel for an earlobe, to find
the one who was beside me, who was near,
to the tune of an old song ---
nostrils alone are to blame for everything.
I would wipe the flowers from your eyes
beneath mascara, saying once:
on the white tablecloth --- not you;
dawn lay there, the cotton reddened.

zavadsky.title: S.
zavadsky.text:
She circles the room,
paying attention to nothing,
her eyes shining like spears,
almost completely out of her mind.
She stretched upward on tiptoe,
but couldn't reach the lamp there.
You can no longer hear it,
I kept repeating farther into the thaw.

She stretched higher, and ---
a fur coat bristles over the naked body ---
eyes burned as if by a strobe
in a blurred landscape.
If only to fence oneself off from the world,
cover the balcony with an old blanket,
and --- beating out rhythms ---
the sky lay at your feet.

She freezes --- doesn't move ---
lifting the hooks of her wrists upward,
setting the height of her face
like a stern above a shipyard.
And stitched a vein to match,
pupils flashed somewhere higher.
You seemed to appear ---
no, you didn't seem to, if only you had!

zavadsky.title: KPZ '82
zavadsky.text:
No, wait! I'm not ready yet,
the voice --- is wrong, the words --- are wrong.
Now I have to answer for
what I myself never wanted.
If only I could earn forgiveness --- from start to finish ---
in the faces of others, but at the exit (here you go!)
the unbroken ice of my words
is the Gulf of Finland this March.

“Je ne sais pas! Pardon, mon cher,”
I repeat, gripping a cut-off piece of pipe,
and just as on wet eyes
a Soviet ruble no longer rusts,
so she will settle into my arms
with a razor sewn into her collar ---
no, not a lighthouse and not a pendulum, but
the thing that will swing them both ways.

She --- that spark and that branch
that beat Morse-code buckshot against the windows,
mangled by your hand ---
and the fingers froze through,
as after the blow of a hammer
the whiteness of the palm is obvious.
Something other than stale alcohol, Mom,
is hardly likely to remain.

A drop of Clicquot runs down
as the final word. Like an anchor,
a name remained beneath the lip,
but I was not in that name.
At night it broke me as it was,
trying to keep silent, and still ---
I remember, Mom, you can't get off the needle
by snapping it beneath the skin.

zavadsky.title: SOME WILLINGLY LAY DOWN UNDER TRAINS
zavadsky.text:
Some willingly lay down
under trains,
others ---
fell headlong into dugouts
and painted the pillbox green.
Whoever wanted to live
with a conscience ---
it wasn't you, was it,
who saw in barbed wire
strings and sheets of music,

and as if for the first time
you had to answer
for it,
to the rattle of zinc
and the uneven crash of crowbars.
In the Russian word --- a backswing,
a blow,
and a dislocation;
everyone --- for himself,
and God will be against everyone.

The time of the flank
and flask,
from now on ---
you can trust only
gauze, a Finnish knife, a high-explosive charge.
Now, instead of ropes ---
soap the cables
of veins,
and --- in farewell one may
hear: “Hello!”

zavadsky.title: PANKOPTICUM
zavadsky.text:
I wager for cutting off
my index finger:
everyone needs poison --- outside,
and I'd give a year of life under slate
to never again hold
a weapon in my hands.

And not from cold
the palms will tremble --- on their own,
gently, like a raid by the Cheka, while I
write for those to whom flowers will remain ---
a snowdrop, a little rose,
a tulip.

And I lived as if
God had given me a head start,
nervously tearing and crumpling by example
protocol, eros, chronicle,
like a monologue
with a bicycle chain
around the throat.

With a gust of wind
I froze as if stunned,
and it isn't the flag that changes color but the flagpole.
I would so much like
to apologize to you,
but I can't understand for what.

And across the way will stand ---
a PR-73 baton --- the stretch
between the one who sat down and the one who got off,
while corrugated sheet metal
keeps rustling
like the tight uniform
of an SS soldier.

We dropped out of schools,
blocked roads, stormed museums,
seized power plants,
wandered between detention centers
and contempt,
while this world
is soon completely fucked.

zavadsky.title: MOSCOW
zavadsky.text:
--- I hate this city, ---
Danil said, ---
it's a freak, with its law
turned
inside out.

--- Amen. Amen.

There, beyond the window --- cool autumn
spreads leaves over squares,
and here --- only a draft
carries the curtains screaming,
as if a horse groans in a pit.

--- I'm not coming back here, I've had enough! ---
he kept repeating, ---
music was playing,
get out of bed
and go off the balcony.

He wrote about the first snow,
about the hospital,
then wrote something else:
“a guest flew in the window frame,
lay there --- at rest...”

--- One last thing I'll tell you, ---
he started up again, ---
I compress dignity like a spring
always for amusement.

And with poems
about a Prima cigarette butt,
to stand by another square ---
an inconspicuous one ---
some need a coat, some would
become different people,
and I'd just like to make it calmly
to the tobacco shop.

zavadsky.title: PASSACAGLIA
zavadsky.text:
“Brother, look back!” --- there was no room left for doubt,
tightening belts, bells reared up,
in every row before me, as before the door of a church,
crosses were leaned against the walls like oil,
only behind us she cracked into fragments
and the truck beds swayed.

All eight spurs driven beneath the elbow,
two steps to a meter --- like a pole, he sees.
Falling down in tears, leaving hum and murmur,
ruffling the snow with a broken fist:
“I was born!” --- tearing open the collar of his pea coat,
snow struck his face, left far behind.

Before me --- from clangs and chimes ---
rifle stocks held ready beat against bayonets,
and someone's gesture born from the frost,
the final sweep of an unshaking hand,
reminded me that in the beginning was the word
and only --- a lie, contrary to Love.

Yes, I stood there, all for different reasons,
while behind the door someone inside was speaking.
She was there --- now on the palm, now on the fingers ---
my country between crooked railings.
I knew everything had not happened in vain
and recited “Left March” from memory.

I interrupted their words --- out of rhythm, tired,
always off-key --- but only let me remind you:
“You remember that tear with its metallic echo,
you remember, brother, but even it was different.”
Only noise remained --- two steps --- he called out,
and that was me, the one who failed to recognize love.

After me, please, leave as a keepsake
at the feet --- a decayed pair of torn-off shoulder boards.
Closing my eyes, I stubbornly continued
my conversation not “with someone” but “about someone.”
“And he remembers without envy, because always
I stubbornly continued the conversation.”

“Brother, look back!” --- bent over, they set the back upright,
and only --- he himself --- barely whole,
I remembered only half my poem
and accepted my lot exactly like a White officer,
and however much snow again fell past me,
the cross of snowflakes did not melt from my face.

zavadsky.title: RAUSCHKOR
zavadsky.text:
I.

There were times I drank so much,
however much was poured ---
in a shard of pupil
a gram was indistinguishable from a liter.
Everything I groaned out again,
hear it while
I still have enough voice, and words
still remain.
I haven't yet traded them all away.
Straightening my back,
I climb toward the chandelier, and they
will not take me down anymore ---
from its curves, neck, lines,
and my poems
driven into the corner, drowning out
swearing and abuse.

II.

Falling to the floor, her necklace
strokes my hand,
like glue staining a bag,
childishly and out of place,
leaving only a handful of syllables ---
please, listen,
how a dog's tail in a sheepskin coat
is always chopped off up to its ears.
One more thing I ask, no matter who ---
say goodbye, and if later
you tattoo my name
onto yourself,
forget it --- rearrange the letters,
multiply it by grief,
burn the ink from your hands with a soldering iron,
wash it down with a Negroni.

III.

And white smoke rose
from the gangster chain,
and together with my passport
the trash bin by the police station
burned ---
and even at full height, just right for me,
the curb was not enough,
and somehow that already familiar
window blinked.
It will blink from the shoulder of a tunic
with a bright swarm of stars,
playing with me head-on
either blind man's bluff
or hide-and-seek ---
deal them innocently into the suit,
and now --- the chip fires,
night is already smearing a palette knife ---
only for appearances.

IV.

I stood up without breaking off the clatter
and, a little gloomy,
assembling a puzzle of broken glass
from officers' shot glasses,
I drank then without feeling,
my throat burning with rum ---
and died not for the first time,
like Remus and Romulus.
I asked, into the pattern on the glass
of roses and lilies,
before anyone had yet driven
a file into my chest like that ---
please! --- let me be tipsy and
finished off by others ---
let only the date remain,
the time, perhaps --- the name.

zavadsky.title: 1931, LIAONING PROVINCE
zavadsky.text:
gather into the palm
the last tobacco
before the siege of Shenyang ---

and carry it through the years,
no matter what becomes of us.

flags are unfurling.
I regret that there was so much
I never said aloud.

the assault begins, the sound of wind,
hair gets into my eyes.

the escalade gives way to a wedge,
sweat drips together with blood.

in a tear spilled by accident
the reflection of the sea
will cover everything.
to the right
the tremolo of volleys and clanging can be heard.

a blow to the temple with a gas pipe ---
and none of this ever happened.

before me once again you
appeared in the chiming of a monisto necklace

with cartridges of different calibers,
like a deafening shot.

while in the port the sailors
quietly crumble dry rice
into jidan'e,
leave on me with your own hand
as many hieroglyphs as possible.

the ramrod of the horizon
had been set straight by someone,
later ---
something hit the back of my head,
and only stains remained of the sky.

in every face flashing past
I tried to recognize myself, but alas ---

I begin the count. one... two... cut...

zavadsky.title: POEM OF PERMANENT NOISE (PPSH)
zavadsky.text:
--- No, leave him! Leave him, he --- too,
pressing the AKM grip painfully
into a burned-through sleeve, ---
I repeated, hair disheveled,
only clenching a couple of words in my mouth, ---
clenching, fuck, every word,
like the broken cross of reinforcing bars,
and let the cold of a crowbar bend it,
a little piece of reforged rail,
the sharp stake of rafters ---
all of them stopped,
you --- multiply the roof's chipped slate,
like the groans of steel beneath the eaves
and a bayonet-knife broken in the throat.
And like shrapnel, just multiply it
by the lice of a worn greatcoat, and --- here
only rusty crumbs of wire
and the trampled ground of former paths.

A rifle stock point-blank, wind mows the snowdrift,
the muzzle brake is removed, and only --- she,
that February blue of lashes frozen together,
remained whole in the breast pocket.
The overpass roars with metal and thaw patches,
the uneven hurried stamp of boots ---
you heard it, you were there,
and as soon as debris covers the body,
you'll remember how another person's gaze went dark;
he --- the ringing of fragments roaring in the ears,
flying like swan down,
the weight of laid sleepers never lifted.
And snow and rain, as though the sky were punctured ---
like Blok's moth-like manteau,
with the warmth of a soldier's collar lining
I kept every word about him.

A vein in stone, he --- a shadow in a cave,
window light --- he keeps appearing,
carefully rising, baring his teeth with strain,
he squeezes the trigger all the way down,
a brass belt flies off whistling,
he is like a misfire roaring in the ear.
I'm afraid --- door, wall, the same low ceiling,
and the face in the reflection preserves the noise ---
and that noise, brother, will stay with you for a long time ---
it will stay with you --- that noise.
With the same belt taken from a pile,
I myself will retie the loop around his neck.

He --- Gaer, Yulaev, Joseph, Barabbas,
Volnovakha and Novocherkassk ---
and no, there is no need at all for forgiveness,
while they can still hear the command half-whispered
where the landscape roughens,
whether maple or willow,
for the two-hundreds, three-hundreds --- the October rain
of the pine forest narrowed its eyes,
like sails facing the waves ---
pressing the whole body in, leaning slightly,
I brace the window with my sole ---
wait! --- someone repeated three times,
gripping the handguard instead of the frame,
and with the rolling choirs of a mortar,
the pin from a tripwire flies like a motor,
I sit silently, remembering someone,
and the conductor's hand no longer trembles.

--- I've lived more than once, and I won't live again
as long as I'm alive! --- the poet said, arguing, ---
No, I won't return! I repent, I repent, I repent,
but instead of words there are only tracks of tank treads.
There the temperature --- zero, a frame of railway spikes,
and farther down from the hills, I remember, a narrow-gauge line poured
point-blank into the face of the one who fell, and even that is not enough,
for one --- a jack, for another --- a Welt.
A turbine blade, so many kinds of lace,
dew runs in a drop down an unshaven cheek,
now it will no longer go into the rack of standing rifles ---
into formation, in ranks.
Left.
One. Two!
And now --- silence, it has already worn everyone out.
I stand motionless myself, as if it were precisely me,
while knees knocked against the bunks,
nervously scratching dates and names into the arches with a nail.

zavadsky.title: EVENING, I LIE SILENTLY AND STARE AT THE CEILING
zavadsky.text:
Evening, I lie silently and stare at the ceiling;
every day is another binge and it remains
the same ---
everyone has scattered,
like an infantry regiment from a garrison.
“Either you're an attesting witness,
or you'll be detained” ---

that's what one man told me,
with only a hint that,
well, whatever is yours remains, so take it ---
and don't hesitate.
I'll say a couple of words,
let them be about something else:
either you're an attesting witness, or you'll be detained.

violetta.title: WANT ME TO STEAL A CITY FOR YOU
violetta.text:
Want me to steal a city for you
from the meanest Tatar-Mongols in the world?
And if you want, I won't hide a thing
about how I'll become a little animal chasing
moths across a field.
I'll measure you in yurts and bitcoins,
glow, grief-glow,
the whole reverse side:
want me to become your
soundtrack to history
in post-punk style?
While the days are such
that for some reason you know your way around flowcharts.
You'll laugh, but you know ---
I'm still the Kremlin.
And want me to be not red
but pink,
to believe in fairy tales?
Just don't cancel me then, like Husky.
Just love me
like a child with spikes around the neck,
fold me into a little figure
and, like a soldier,
launch me as springtime ships
through April trenches
so that all the little monkeys are happy in their zoos.
Just love me
through all the room tours
and the scrambled letters of Karakorum,
in heat, in cold, and in a storm.
Want me to steal a city for you
from the meanest Tatar-Mongols in the world ---
and let that be our excuse
to meet in February.

violetta.title: AND PEOPLE GROW INTO DOMES WITH THEIR VOICES
violetta.text:
And people grow into domes with their voices,
and that voice quietly says
that you are for me --- a form in which to pronounce words,
and proof that graves are going wild.
God came, but was always alone,
like the running of a lame young man across a field.
I'll tell everything, I'll tell everything,
but I'll hide
that you are for me --- a surrogate for prayers.
Freeze.
I'm dying of longing,
from the feeling of chthonic excess.
Here is August.
We were the ones who burned it
and took photos against it for fun.
I'm horny and unable to whine.
I accept bombs and cashless payments.
You are for me --- something like the weight of evidence
that no one ever collected.
Like a white man dying in darkness
and holiness simply torn from the hands,
you are something wild and herd-like in me,
as if it were one of the arts.
When you held me so, so tightly,
and in the outflow of pink blood
we looked at the world through the eyes of radicals,
through the eyes of summer, snow, and love.

violetta.title: REMEMBER, WE SURVIVED THE WORLD
violetta.text:
Remember, we survived the world
and made it to the final,
while football
set all the clerks' chats against one another many times over.
While August sneered
and kept going on and on
about the innocence of the storm
and summer's noninvolvement.
I zigzagged, kept zigzagging through words
and kissed dogs;
we shot at apples
as if shooting at a greyhound's legs.
If all this is out of love,
then love as an act
will never die
in this necrosis of wars.
I carried mercury in my belly
and wanted to press
against your scratches the hail
that smashed everything here.
I wanted to live very, very quietly,
but by chance
was born into the loudest of times.
Breathe in the restless twilight --- that's us,
and fear falls,
bitter as wormwood.
While Elektrostal burns down to embers
and warehouses burn
with dried flowers ordered for you.
Look into the restless days ---
yes, that's us too.
While drops fell
straight into an oil rainbow,
and the sunset was beautiful to the point of breakdown,
we grabbed each other's hands,
and like mourning moths
poured kerosene into it.

violetta.title: WE TALKED ABOUT PALMYRA AND TEHRAN
violetta.text:
We talked
about Palmyra and Tehran.
Smoked rhymes
at Telegram's wake.
And we got blocked for nothing.
And it's half past one.
How do I prove that I,
that I'm not a robot,
twisting like a snake
under total surveillance?
How do I explain to tech support
that in summer people feel like kissing?
An obsessive feeling, like an ad.
And I no longer trust faces in avatars.
All chats are written off like days.
I loved you, loved you,
but you --- are AI.

violetta.title: I'LL TAKE AN ASSAULT RIFLE AND START SHOOTING
violetta.text:
I'll take an assault rifle and start shooting
at memory --- as at maps.
I'll keep beneath my skin a cherry orchard
scorched by last March.
And when the dirt is over and the pogrom has passed,
I'll breathe in a quiet home.
And timidly
beneath my rib will bloom
a colored tattoo.

violetta.title: GRANDMA ALWAYS SCOLDED THE CAT
violetta.text:
Grandma always scolded the cat
for being a little bastard who drank the milk,
and for some reason it smelled strongly of grass,
something like hardy steppe wormwood.
I look out the window and there is God himself,
wagging a finger at me: tut-tut ---
as if this poem were all wrong,
as if this poem weren't about a cat.
As if Grandma had been right back then
and had thrashed the kitty for good reason,
because she really was a little bastard ---
as if life were nothing but nonsense
and just like milk
could fit into three sinewy laps.
On the table, creamy lemon balm,
fragrant tea
already drunk a little ---
less and less often do I fall asleep at night,
more and more often I wake at night
hearing neither Grandma nor the cat arguing.

violetta.title: THESE ARE THE DREAMS SQUIRREL KITS HAVE NOW
violetta.text:
These are the dreams squirrel kits have now ---
that for some reason I wake them and cry
with a tear flowing into a July snowfall.
At least I mean something in it.
Who is to blame,
tell me, who is to blame
that I haven't slept for three years,
three winters?
Look, there we are,
standing --- two dashing pines,
and on our cedar memory
thrushes and drones
race each other.
And whatever warmth there is, it isn't mine,
while the whole earth, season by season,
sheds human sons.
Want everything?
Want us not to die?
Want us to be pines no longer,
but bears ---
the ones in the sky, the Dipper,
lying in the fork ---
and God saw it:
Shishkin and Savitsky painted us.
The bear-days going away ---
we smell of smoke, the blade of metal,
and beatifically, as if Ruskeala
were letting springs beneath our skin.
But that's not us.
Let's not imagine it.
Everything here is as before again: the years
become churches and cathedrals beneath a chevron,
and in every person --- minus two.
The simple arithmetic of the living.
What did you stop breathing for and chase?
In every reel --- I simply mistook someone:
like --- unfollow,
scrolling backward by name.
Look how picturesque a Russian grave is,
how deep its dark eyes.
Love, run, love, love, run,
without stepping on the smiles of mines.
I am clay, clay, clay...
And you,
perhaps as the most tenacious dahlia,
will save this Norway of ruins?
For now the world
looks at us and growls.
Let's embrace, let them gossip:
none of this is shameful,
like the dreams of squirrel kits,
like the fact that we wake them,
the fact that we cry.

violetta.title: BLACKCURRANTS BLOOMED IN THE DON SHELTERBELTS
violetta.text:
In the Don shelterbelts
blackcurrants bloomed
on the lips.
Resin, rumor;
midnight ambers.
So that we might pass
for sunflowers until morning ---
speak to me, woman,
speak.
Speak of how bread is leavened,
how hand-to-hand the forest is
on the wing of whirlwinds,
in the partridge-ness of the sky.
Grow evening with me, woman,
grow evening.
As evening falls, remember:
how in April
the legs are haymaking,
the scythe is innocent.
How straw-like the field is, broken,
and mined
among feather-grass nuts.
Do not be afraid, woman,
do not be afraid.
Of the evil cloud
on the fishing line of day,
where the village has settled,
where from A to Z
I fell in love with everything one-day,
everything twenty-first.
Where in the Don shelterbelts
blackcurrants bloomed,
the net was uncatching,
and beneath the fires
the motherland gave birth
so fleetingly.
Fear became a herd.
And the woman ran, ran
with a little boy in her arms.

violetta.title: TO LOOK INTO YOUR METEORITE EYES
violetta.text:
To look into your meteorite eyes,
to strip the copper from them
with ammonia solution.
To wander through galaxies --- not grow earthly,
to guess your zodiac sign.
And I wish,
to the beat of orbits, listening to wounds,
I could rush away with you into dreadlocked distance.
Watch dinosaurs fall asleep.
To eternal Lil Peep and Tentacion.
There we are mean.
Mean, yes.
Since wherever we happen to be ---
we dance death.
From the front end and the rear.
Mean, yes,
like, God forgive us,
all of Russian rap.
It happened and happened.
We always dress in black --- whose night are we?
I'm a drunk, drunk sunstroke.
You --- maybe Mars, more likely --- his daughter.
In a Thrasher shirt, you text me bye.
--- bye
--- bye
God simply mixed up the cosmos here.
Hello, rocket, this is me --- Earth.
And the sky smells of a tear and diesel fuel.
The world is watching us, and I'm shooting at you,
my half-native little alien.

violetta.title: AND PEOPLE ARE LIKE ANIMALS
violetta.text:
And people are like animals.
And the sky --- a trap.
The twenties --- the two-hundreds,
February's flammability.
The twenties --- the two-hundreds:
oaks without their hundreds,
a wounded field,
an epidemic of army boots.
The rifles are diligent
and bedsores in the eyes.
The twenties --- the two-hundreds,
the Lord at the frontiers.
A cackling morning
and the resettled south.
The twenties --- the two-hundreds,
and I love you.

violetta.title: I'LL SLEEP UNTIL NOON IN THE AUL (1)
violetta.text:
I'll sleep until noon in the aul,
so Aunt Ragmeda
can break off a walnut branch
and whip my legs with it.
For now I dream of a country
with a flock of cornflowers
and revelations of a fly,
sounding like hymns to evil.
And whoever hasn't had enough of it?
For them it's probably easier
to hide away. Not to go.
We are a sheep-like life
on the approaches to iftar.
And suns beneath the snow,
and the Caspian locked up.
And still the shepherds can't sleep,
so early in the morning,
playing karakan.
Oh my spring,
herd-like, driven in droves,
do not fall asleep.
I dream of candies from overseas
and of the sea itself,
people with undercoats of grief,
mourning toward the lighthouse.
In the Khunzakh aul
I dream of a Russian mother ---
perhaps not even mine.
I dream of a wedding. Someone else's.
Everyone stares and says nothing,
and I can't understand:
why do your cats
ghek and ok at me?
I know no one. I don't fit
the type of mica.
The indecomposability of life,
the laggability of bombs.
If May doesn't come,
then the February beetle
failed to love.
Well, or one of them
is definitely lying to you.
I'll roll onto my stomach,
agree to the deadliness of the day,
because I'm allowed,
because I dream of a great sky
and a heart so large
that it truly seems
the most human-sized thing of all.
And Aunt Ragmeda --- a foolish woman.
She simply didn't know, simply didn't know,
that death, so improper and
so unwilling to show itself,
drives two-legged dragonflies somewhere.
While in the Khunzakh aul
I seem to dream the whole world at once ---
all its godliness,
all its flesh and bone.

violetta.title: I'LL SLEEP UNTIL NOON IN THE AUL (2)
violetta.text:
I'll sleep until noon in the aul,
so Aunt Ragmeda
can break off a walnut branch
and whip my legs with it.
For now I dream of a country
with a flock of cornflowers
and revelations of a fly,
sounding like hymns to evil.

violetta.title: I'M OK. YOU'RE OK
violetta.text:
I'm OK.
You're OK.
A nuclear chuckle rang out.
Step back, and quickly.
Bone on bone --- the beat is heard.
In the wasteland I plant
a radioactive poppy.
What remains of the screen?
A person sits by the church.
A dragonfly flies past:
we danced it through to the end.
Where there is nothing --- God will be there:
the darkness of heads lit up,
invisible people beneath the rubble ---
poisons of an angelic sting.
I am a stranger to him. A stranger.
You stand the other way round.
Go on, look for yourself:
you have --- an entrance at the entrance,
I have --- a single line
stretched across all three.
Bone on bone --- a pulse is heard.
A person said: I'll return.
Didn't return. So be it.
I am alone. Of a hundred arts.
I come out of darkness.
Nothing. And the beat is heard.
Sapling. Core. Wasteland.
Radioactive poppy.

violetta.title: INTO DEAD WINDOWS
violetta.text:
Into dead windows
I press a cigarette butt so it won't smolder.
At five years old
people also pray and see someone off onto a little cloud.
Life --- vodka,
God --- a greedy bastard,
the sky covered in abrasions:
that was me throwing plum stones at it.
To the sound of draining water I heard families and states fall apart.
Give me love and protest.
I like tearing your skin at the hangnails.
And gluing sparrows to resin in spring.
I can surely do something greater, since I can't do something smaller.
Running a hand over oilcloth,
not getting ready for summer,
watching people lose teeth, people, and hope.
Cutting bread only halfway through.
The loops in the toilet look like lifebuoys.
I'll take all the candy and run away from home
toward the smell of other people's apartments
for lack of a home.
Is it even possible to want anything among a hundred and forty million?
A roll-up cigarette. Insomnia.
Scooter riders and stairwells.
A scooter.
Yandex Lavka.
Delivery
of draft summons.
This is my love --- spring with its throat torn open,
paralytic laughter, this is sin --- for lack of a word.
This is my citizenship --- to be guilty of something.
This is my country --- great Russian defiance.
These are dead, dead windows.
I lie on my stomach, close my eyes --- that's how I play hide-and-seek.
Grown-up women and men
pour boiling water, drink boiling water, beat boiling water.
I remember the hiss of a bag. And what they brought me in the evening:
a couple of little loaves, and the tears of the world,
permanent distrust,
a two-second truce,
and generally I don't give a damn.
Cathedrals burn too
in the space of metamodernism.
I am an ellipsis.
I'm five,
and I'll trade everything for cheap
cola-flavored Bubble Gum.
To chew it and throw stones
at dead, dead windows.

violetta.title: REMEMBER HOW WE TURNED THE LIGHT ON EVERYWHERE
violetta.text:
Remember how we turned the light on everywhere
so you'd stop being afraid of the blizzard,
and the lamp lit up, as in the window
a bullfinch froze, the crossing stiffened.
And with him the female bullfinch in the ring
hid her chilled beak beneath the branches.
February keeps trying to make the snow meaner,
the northern winds chirp and chirrup.
While someone's daily life flickers in the distance:
someone else's grubby childhood,
pots, dust, forgotten neighborliness,
the cobbledness of streets we will not get to live.
Deception all around and blackmail in retinues,
so that once more, through all these hassles,
we are already full of the courtesy of spring.
On some dreary Monday or other.
You'll say to me: let's go pour some tea,
take a piece of dried-up cookie ---
and of course, of course I'll go,
to chew nothing but pronouns with you.
And then an armful of firewood is coming,
and winter can be started over again.
I step outside --- barely dark. Into the hoarse courtyard,
and you accidentally stuff a mitten into my pocket.

violetta.title: THE BLACK BERRY HAS RIPENED
violetta.text:
The black berry has ripened.
Everyone left in need,
the reckless apple tree laughed,
God denied people.
As an old woman milks the apple tree,
do not look into the well
where the black berry pours,
oh Nicholas the Wonderworker.
How beautiful the black berry is,
how majestic,
how did it fade so,
how did it go wild?
Roots and tops all froze out,
grew older.
How did they all die out like that
and turn beastly?
A floor of wormwood, bitterness --- is blazing;
from now on I am to writhe here
with poems.
Like an echo of quartz,
thunder, and cradle,
I am to remain here
as a gravestone of pronouns.
Like over a baptismal font,
water haystacks,
I am still to carry
lines to graves.

violetta.title: AMÉLIE
violetta.text:
Amélie,
I will never wake up,
I will never wake up,
and let it be.
Lilies bloomed.
I bet on wars and pandemics.
Amélie,
want me to bring you the sun from Syria?
There are bruises on the cloud.
I stood death up.
Because death is nothing.
You are a hundred times wider:
nothing, nothing, nothing.
So what?
I fell into people and their grief.
Love is when it goes through-us-through.
The night was --- fatherless.
I choked on wretchedness
and beauty.
Forgave everyone.
And was help-less.
Amélie,
I believed in God,
but it's true, I broke butterflies' spines
and looked down angels' throats.
And you?

violetta.title: WITH THE SMILE OF A WILD ANIMAL
violetta.text:
With the smile of a wild animal,
with the gait of a porcupine,
with blueberry eyes ---
you were ugly.
And you taught me to kiss
on my fingers.
I lost count.
And counted again.
The earth embraced me and intently
searched in me for the son of man.
And I, like an idiot, meowed ---
the way you taught me.
The hills, little loaves,
jays and mockingbirds made faces.
People in general --- are sinners
with beef-like tenderness.
For some reason they tried to drown the sun ---
and it squealed.
Death became domesticated.
You went wild.
Thawed Indigirka,
tired ears of grain.
Your hair
stretches along the Trans-Siberian Railway.
And strawberry tears burn
on the shelterbelts.
Stripped before everyone,
swinging your heels,
they scolded you, but stubborn,
you threw wounds into your backpack,
wondered ---
whom cockroaches pray to
and who will get me.
You closed your eyes,
kept running,
like one cut open,
not knowing ---
whether there would be another May.
I don't know either.
I just listen,
listen, listen,
to steel barking,
and answer it:
meow, meow.

violetta.title: THE SUNSET OF MY YOUTH
violetta.text:
The sunset of my youth.
Escalators, escalation.
Nowhere left to descend.
Second day without sleep.
Who is the killer?
It's hard to draw a body in beige
so that a person looks like a person.
If you place a triangle
on top of a square,
you get a house
or a rocket.
Pa-ra-pam-pam.
The rocket cried and flew,
you cried and wrote
sobbing.
Then fires,
harvest posts.
You feel sorry for everyone again ---
stop whining.
People --- hydrangeas,
only covered in little crosses.
Allergic to flowers.
The lifeline through the minefield
stretches to you.
Explosion.
A domesticated butterfly
grieves:
who will feed it now?
Whom am I supposed to love now?
Shift change of feelings.
You're silent --- so I'm silent too.
I'm running --- so you run too.
You know yourself
why you're saying all this.
Please, don't burn out.
Give me
your wounds --- I'll kiss them.
Spring in handcuffs.
They say spring is forbidden.
But I'll fall asleep on it.
Touch me
with every line,
with every rhyme.
I was told
that God had died,
but I don't believe them.
One step closer ---
I'm allowed to breathe,
but the cold still won't let up.
You are my heart --- a chestnut.
Plant it when you return.

violetta.title: ALTARS WILL RISE TO US FROM THE EAST
violetta.text:
Altars will rise to us from the east.
God preserve my holy ghetto.
Everyone is silent here: no one speaks,
words run back into the person.
And the nights are long --- but lives are short;
extend them another half-minute.
Foreignburgs wither from longing:
I live by Cyrillic --- don't hold it against me.
And beauty --- is the final act.
I have nothing to say to this spring.
You will not die until you cease
to be what death does not possess.
The earth will take me and this poem.
Hearts escaped from the Kunstkamera are beating.
I fall asleep in your arms
to dream with open eyes.
And still no one speaks.
On Khokhloma, tulips bloom in crowds,
and my great Russia still stands.
I ruled a whole alphabet across it ---
thirty-two capitals came up missing.
Only
its own
name remains.

violetta.title: I'M ALIVE, I'M ALIVE, I'M ALIVE
violetta.text:
I'm alive, I'm alive, I'm alive.
How many times must I repeat it
for you to believe?
I'm mute. I'm mute. I'm mute.
How many times must I stay silent
for it to become clear?
There is some kind of noise in my heart
and FM interference.
I decompose into classes and student construction brigades.
I am the twenty-first century;
a chrism appears on me,
two chrysanthemums --- for Mother and the Tsar ---
inside me a Decembrist song blossoms.
I say --- Revolution, I address you as “I.”
I myself, I myself, I myself
protest for myself.
Beside me are my guardian angel and May.
I am war, therefore I exist
somewhere beyond online,
where angry children swear.
While somewhere in the wombs of fields the world is dying,
I so wanted to become a bullet in a pistol
to live inside you, to live inside you,
to live.
But we won't stay here long;
we hold on, hold on, and break through into hell.
What's wrong, my magnificent rebel?
Today your soldier died too.
There will now be fireworks in his honor
and a ceremonial march.
Only his mother cries,
remembering how he
as a boy in childhood
he released balloons
into the sky
for no reason at all.

violetta.title: ROADS ARE BEING BUILT --- THE TRAM RUNS
violetta.text:
Roads are being built --- the tram runs,
runs until the line snaps.
My city loves May and robberies
and panoramas of Lenin avenues.
They've run up against churches; any moment now
Voroshilov bullets will whirl them into a dance.
My city remembers caravans and Berlin
and how factories rebelled against the streets.
I walked to you --- stole the neighbors' lilies
while they bent their backs over melon patches.
I walked to you --- I wasn't allowed through
past the bags lined up for the dachas.
Try it yourself! Slogans and shouts
that divided and stole our youth.
I'm small-time.
And my city --- is markets.
On cardboard I undress at the outskirts.
Knives mutter something in thieves' argot to me.
Love will make it from home to the den.
My city --- is a monument and a life.
One hundred and forty million look into me.
Before death I don't count the days.
I know the city kills on command.
But winters will end, and the sun will shelter
my homeless Volgograd August.

violetta.title: AND LIFE FIT INTO THE PALM, THE WAY
violetta.text:
And life fit into the palm, the way
I placed you among the hills of Jerusalem.
Ah, if only I could clench the years into a fist
and rewind them to the infinitive.
Where you resembled no one at all,
like Ashkenazim in central Russia.
Where from the very first word
I understood you entirely in a child's language.
Where summer remained only in Yeysk,
and they never once let us go overseas.
You took in every displaced person
just as once you took in street kittens.
Where the sun shut itself in cashmere,
as if laughing at us that way.
Where you burned as things burn in Siberia,
and stiffened for holy Arkhangelsk.
Where churches and barracks knew you,
and sheets caught on fences.
Where men swallowed you like dogs
and spoiled Smolensk patterns.
Where a nimble knife will catch the fugitive
and return him to the lands of Little Russia.
Where one day a son will still shoot his father,
and the mother will be orphaned forever.
Where I wandered like a foreigner
hoping that one day you would exist.
And where from heart to heart
lie hectares of frozen virgin land.
And where nettles will rush at a crumb,
smashing all her southern rear.
Where of course you loved me,
where of course I loved you.
Where there is no death,
where we are very young,
looking at this sky without refusal.
Where, if we never come to love,
there will be no Crimea or Caucasus left in us.

violetta.title: I FOUND YOU AS A POPPY FIELD
violetta.text:
I found you as a poppy field
at an iron foundry,
far from the epicenter of centuries.
In every city,
on every square ---
the initials of your blossoms.
Even if I don't recognize you by face,
in every name
you resemble that street
with peashrub and mezzanines.
It's a pity: flowers
live beautifully, and then --- summer,
black earth and a plowman.
So do you:
you left home a human being,
you'll return as ashes.
There is nothing special in this!
Very loudly.
Let the elevators and ring roads
stall.
I found you as a red blot,
sending signals
to a rusty sun.
Which clearly means
something hurts
when everything has spilled into dragées,
and therefore someone,
by roughly one love or one death,
has it worse right now
than I do.
You there,
don't die
and don't over-love.
Know
that in this boundless
high-rise December
there is one window
in the middle of the dark
that, like poppies at an iron foundry,
has not fallen asleep
for the fourth year
and burns.

violetta.title: AFTER OUR TIME
violetta.text:
After our time
there will be no archaeology.
It's not about women or history.
There will simply be nothing to dig up.
After everything, graves remain;
after us --- only OnlyFans.
After the twenties will come the thirties;
after us --- only OnlyFans.
And the living will remain to listen
to how a daughter's teeth (a pity it wasn't a son)
came through;
how childhood hanged itself
in the stairwell,
and --- all right ---
how Dad has no
eye
and scars on his body;
how Mom no longer
has a mom;
how God no longer
has paradise.
Though what made him think
those born as angels
don't do webcam shows?
Through radiators,
through pipes, all the way to the heating main,
a couple of words travel like a cradle song:
“Warm me, my angel.
They switched August off yesterday.
It's cold here again.
I seem to be home, but
for some reason I want
to go home so badly.”
Public utilities against Russian chthonic darkness.
Two thousand twenty-something.
The monsters hid under the bed.
Want me to die some next Tuesday
if you let me kiss you?
How about on camera?
Let's make love and shoot ourselves.
Yes, we're the first and the last.
And even if we aren't,
where else can we go?
Beneath masks and outfits...
Just try loving me shameless, conscienceless, and disorderly!
What sorrows of yours are there?
Want to --- take my body,
sell it at market price
somewhere in Baghdad.
I'll warm up there for all of you.
And you will be warmed from the frost
by war.
Remember, my angel,
remember, you died.
And tomorrow --- spring.
And tomorrow --- love.
And tomorrow someone is happy
with flowers on a truck crane.
Assemble me in the grocery store
from a shopping list.
Let them come up one short
at the khach-store.
Please,
tell Mom
everything is fine.
That those men
kissed me purely in a comradely way.
From the word “commodity.”
And when all that's left of me
is an icon on a website ---
write somewhere there in your own hand:
My angel,
even without a little wing,
wrapped in cellophane.
For the last time,
donate
for the repose of the soul.

violetta.title: COME TO ME THROUGH THE PERMAFROST
violetta.text:
Come to me through the permafrost.
My arms grow out of the tundra
and end somewhere in the steppes.
Let's leave for Karaganda?
Otherwise, for about three versts here
I can't reach you.
I kiss the little domes of monasteries.
To me,
there was
something of incense in you.
I remember when they undressed you:
you had spring beneath your shoulder blade.
You had willow curls,
and the water bloomed cornflower-blue.
I lost you and I won't anymore.
Baikonur, Baikonur, come in!
You come toward me --- somehow unfinished,
I come toward you --- through mines and steel.
Between us, distance drafts
into the Baikal-Amur Mainline.
You are my unconquered virgin land.
How many deaths are still there before love?
I love you beast-like and bird-like,
and by now, probably, humanly too.
You are my Russian Atlantis,
guidebooks for lovers
of a monochrome shore.
My hands are covered in blood,
but I am under the protection of the north.
I break down into names,
letters, numbers, and dashes.
In my next life I will become,
perhaps, you,
but more likely my own patronymic.
Walk.
Walk while the sky is still made to grow into,
walk while a titmouse pours,
walk while we haven't been buried.
Don't weep before the willow does.
Think: if God is here
frolicking with us,
then who is there now
with them?

arisha.title: NOON, THE EIGHTH CALL AND THE THIRD COFFEE
arisha.text:
Noon, the eighth call and the third coffee.
My home --- an open-space cubicle, a little cage gnawed by an animal.
My interlocutor --- spam, an AI agent and a robot.
I'd rather speak not to it but to you, only I can't.
I'd hide with you in a cat basket,
take cover in the indie tracks of ringing girls,
rub against you and snort at a bird ---
together we're an unavailable subscriber.
While I'm here, I am all desktop,
an accidental spit in the middle of the screen.
I'm a bookcase, a coach's brochure, a knight ---
F2, G5 --- my move, info-gypsy style.
Six in the evening, another call, spilled coffee.
Life is blocked --- if only I could find the VPN keys,
clear the cache, erase myself and start all over.
Answer. And into the receiver, please,
say nothing.

arisha.title: VERY TENDER ZOOMERS DRINK OVERPRICED COFFEE
arisha.text:
Very tender zoomers drink overpriced coffee
and are afraid to stay at work past six,
so at rush hour they won't run into the city's sadness and drunkenness;
they always choose a taxi.
They're offended by black jokes about women and skin color,
and also by body shaming, abuse, and age underestimation.
With an HQD vape in hand they like to dream of freedom
from the Lord's rough paws.
Anxious zoomers try to surround themselves with comfort:
they keep memes next to photos of dead friends on the desktop,
attach avoidantly to smartphones and people
so they won't attach themselves to a noose.
In a collection of candles, the flame freezes in reaction to the story of an ex,
of youth that followed transparent tracks left by others.
Brave zoomers want so badly to be heard,
but end up in spam.

arisha.title: THE WIND IS ALREADY BLOWING OVER YOU, SKIN --- A PRICKLY SWEATER
arisha.text:
The wind is already blowing over you, skin --- a prickly sweater.
You scrape fibers from your nose as if with someone else's hand.
On a cool summer evening you gather beads from your eyes,
melting into the hot asphalt like viscous amber resin.
Inside, everything boils and foams; freckles replace the burn.
Boiling water is poured into mugs.
It feels as though you'll burn up too.

arisha.title: HOW MUCH OF ME IS LEFT? HOW MUCH CAME UP MISSING?
arisha.text:
How much of me is left? How much came up missing?
Send me a receipt for every whisper of mine.
A beggar in Levi's asks for alms by the station ---
a sign in his hand: “for spiritual bread.”
He reaches a hand toward passersby,
repeating the tattoo sketch from his right leg,
just like Adam, but God doesn't need him ---
he has debts of his own.
Personhood --- a salary:
counting days from advance to payday.
But Up Above they've already found a candidate,
and of course it isn't you.
Digging through yourself, opening graves,
asking the mirror, “Am I human?”
Sitting by the station, watching how others
managed to ask for Levi's and bread.

arisha.title: PRIDE --- A PUDDLE OF BEER, YOU WERE NEVER MEANT TO BECOME A LITTLE GOAT
arisha.text:
Pride --- a puddle of beer, you were never meant to become a little goat.
Being needed by someone --- cinematic milk.
If only to drink from one or the other: dive to the bottom for treasure,
send innocence far, far away with a hand on the heart.
Cry at a drunken house party, dreamily looking out the window:
if only I could grow up, become somebody --- since I was never meant to be a little goat.

arisha.title: WHILE YOU WAIT FOR NEW MEANINGS AND SHARP TEXTS
arisha.text:
While you wait for new meanings and sharp texts,
somewhere a copywriter cries, generating a prompt for pennies.
If artificial intelligence replaced your heart ---
how much more would bomb explosions move you?
While you complain about the bankruptcy of art,
a marketer tries to promote a touring show for next to nothing.
If you were very sad,
how often would you watch films with Kutsenko?
While you talk about the lies of news and priests,
your unbiased journalism is crucified by a thousand characters and sold for thirty little words.
But if they forced you to become an SMM manager,
how many online candles would you light?
While you scream at a broken router,
bare your teeth at my Telegram and go feral,
I drop little tears onto the sticky keys of my laptop
because no one will ever buy this text.

arisha.title: THIS WORD MAKES ME FEEL SO SICK AND CRAMPED
arisha.text:
This word makes me feel so sick and cramped.
I repeat myself. And spit bread crumbs into my palm.
Let a patient winged messenger peck from my hands
and return home to you with a message.
Breaking holes through the blue ceiling,
with a light feather it will deliver --- “I miss you.”
Too little and out of place. As if I were targeting
a student with an invitation to a deserted edge.
“To miss” --- a counting-rhyme word for missed days,
a piggy-bank word for abandoned promises.
Longing will suit the white wedge of cranes,
and adorn only widows and drunks.
Tongue-twister boredom will interfere
with boredom-the-bitch languishing through Januaries, erasing dreams.
I'm not bored, upstairs neighbor,
but, you know...
come by anyway.

arisha.title: IN MY HEAD, INSTEAD OF THOUGHTS, ONLY THE RINGING OF BELL TOWERS
arisha.text:
In my head, instead of thoughts, only the ringing of bell towers.
We don't sleep --- we're playing hide-and-seek with the tired city.
Then comes a quiz about which of us is sicker,
running in circles through courtyards and fences.
Wait for us, we'll probably make it by dinner,
two orphans in our invisibility cloaks.
We're gray-haired children, unwanted.
Help us save ourselves
in prayers.

arisha.title: THE AIR CRUNCHES UNDERFOOT
arisha.text:
The air crunches underfoot.
Seas spread across the cheeks.
My eyes --- a peninsula:
ours or whose, you decide.
The height feels like a childish prank.
If only to catch the smoke of chimneys on the way.
A jump --- and into your arms.
Please, don't catch me.

arisha.title: YOU'RE SO TIRED --- I'LL BECOME A CIGARETTE ON YOUR SMOKE BREAK
arisha.text:
You're so tired --- I'll become a cigarette on your smoke break
between days that froze back in November.
I'll run away from them to the Baltic Sea
so you can find me in amber like a little bug.
In a bath of women's old-and-new things,
dry your wet thoughts on me and put them in order.
In a world where without friends the DJ plays very sadly,
I'll be the faithful shadow of a crowd of fangirls.
Let me remain an awkwardness in the air,
an empty conversation, a ridiculous joke.
When people around you become too loud,
I'll dart like a quiet mouse beneath your heart.

arisha.title: PLEASE, MOM, DON'T SING ME A LULLABY
arisha.text:
Please, Mom, don't sing me a lullaby.
Leave the light on here for at least a couple more minutes.
Yes, the bags under my eyes are burial pits,
but don't give me the chance to fall asleep.
I'm not afraid of nightmares, deadlines, or the magic of morning.
Darkness and the drunk neighbor behind the wall don't scare me.
But now, wrapped in a blanket like a child,
I tremble when I see His silhouette.
Like in children's legends, he lives under the bed,
holds me by the legs so I'll stay beside him,
chooses words, pseudonyms, and dresses,
makes the reflection strange and cruel.
Now he goes to work in my place,
won't let me eat lunch or get up to use the bathroom.
He took my courage, love, and freedom,
even the strength to meet the final dawn.
