It's neither too late nor too early to take pills:
he has woken up; his hands are now on my chest.
Please, Mom, don't sing me a lullaby.
While I'm still here, kiss my forehead and leave quickly.

arisha.title: ON THE BUS THE HANDRAILS LOOK LIKE NOOSES
arisha.text:
On the bus the handrails look like nooses.
Please don't stop at the next one.
We're going to Murino, Pargolovo, or Dybenko...
somewhere with nothing human left.
Two coins: for the eyes or for the fare.
It hardly matters --- payment by card.
There are so many empty seats left here
for all the fare-dodging hares without God or meadow.
My heart beats in time with every bump.
On the ring road the cars lead a waltz.
The validator is a pole; I can barely hold on.
Rate my curtsy to routine.
There is no conductor, if only
so they won't hand me my lucky ticket.
I'll ride past your house, wave from the window,
and say one final hello in farewell.

arisha.title: I WANT TO BE A GOOD AND PROPER PERSON
arisha.text:
I want to be a good and proper person:
graduate from university, find a good job, successfully marry the person I love.
Only I'm a poet. And behind swollen red eyelids
a talentless hack hides under pseudonyms.
Someone hides there who is constantly looking for attention,
like a drug stash, perhaps, or some pompous meaning of life.
Being yourself is like placing a huge bet on graphomania
in a world where every new thought is secondary anyway.
There is no respect. My view of myself is exclusively harsh.
I am my own garden, and my own pest.
In a world where everyone diligently loves themselves,
allow me
to hate
myself.

stas.title: WHAT A RUSH BLEW THE TOPS OFF OIL REFINERIES
stas.text:
what a rush
blew the tops off oil refineries
God is with us, and he claps his hands
the echo swore, spilling through courtyards
like a janitor pouring water into beef Doshirak
and the whole little landscape --- like croutons with smoke
an army of high-rises held the flanks
I held your hand, so what
we're all --- merely material for anxious reports
and ourselves --- anxious little mushrooms
geraniums got all pretty in the central park
while all we need is barefoot through the storm
and to tuck May under the lip like naswar
our little bridge across the century on skinny piles
take a gulp of napalm, like a confused Danko
walk and sing, only beyond the river
there's nothing but a minefield, like an impostor tablecloth
youth, kissel, and milk will all sour
they won't wait for us, because they aren't waiting anyway
you'll shiver, I'll hold you tighter
such a shaky, purely poser-like redoubt
keep calling, siren --- how long do we have left?
the counting rhyme is trash; only one thing is allowed here:
not to let go, to keep holding your hand
and bet on myself
like on zero

stas.title: GLVNG
stas.text:
Such a rancid post-Khrushchev ammonite
and a body stubbornly clinging to sanitary porcelain
(what kind of life --- such are the stagecoaches)
no one will squeeze you out, no one will take your place
inside your spiral shell.
Gloomy and unfit for dopamine,
daily life loses aspiration and form,
and interference flakes over the eyes.
And from behind the wall again someone's crying.
Behind a wall any girl is Melpomene.
All romances are reduced to cheating,
and your love --- overforce and crunch.
Behind another wall: giggling and fooling around,
fussing is fussing, touching and moans,
other people's children, liberties, rom-coms,
and someone digesting tasty pilaf.
The way the building will digest un-tasty you.
The sewer drain rumbles contentedly,
behind walls a league of profanations rustles,
and every kitchen is like a Yury Dud interview.
To leave the room is like coming to after a coma
where you lay around listening in on doctors.
Outside, sparrow-like belonging to no one,
everyone looks suspiciously familiar,
as though there were nothing interspecies about it.
Little snails slide through the flow and the resource,
and every one is, like, not exactly pussy,
but carries its calcium coffin on its back.
Run away from home, but drag it along.
From above --- beyond the belching boiler houses,
nothing but clusters of hermit shells,
and the whole district looks like the seabed...

stas.title: SPRING, LATE AND THOUGHTFUL
stas.text:
spring,
late and thoughtful,
stood before the wayfinding stone.

go right ---
you'll get lost between Chyon and Chersky
(may bristly Kolyma keep and bury you).

go left ---
you'll trip over the Baltic shallows,
tumble head over heels through the calendar;
if only someone would gather your little arms and legs.

and straight ahead
(who even walks straight?)
nothing but mountains and passes.

while she stood there hesitating,
foolish March
climbed out of her bag,
followed a fox's tail,
and no one ever saw him again.

wayward April
pulled out a Nagant,
freaked out,
went off to join the partisans.

only flashy May
twisted like a bright ribbon
(the chief dandy and straight guy):
“what are you doing, mother, dithering?
what directions do you need?
you're everywhere anyway.
just bloom already, for fuck's sake.”

stas.title: FOOL VODKA FIELD
stas.text:
I went out into a field and drank vodka,
arms spread, grinning like an idiot,
fell flat with a swing, and the wheat, like a mother,
rocked me to sleep so I wouldn't get up.

I lay there embracing black earth with my back,
was a prophetic root, a capricious stream.
No one cursed me, no one chopped from the shoulder,
no bot scammed me and Roskomnadzor banned nothing.

And clouds flew above me,
rocket strokes drew dark ages,
stars swung like the mournful ruble exchange rate,
and beyond them vacuum (there was fuck-all left).

No one came for the wheat or for me,
not a single signal into the solid-crow-black cosmos,
only a feeling itched (well, imagine that):
I owed no one in the world anything anymore.

I came back to the city, confused and out of place,
but instead of a city there was only decay and haze.
Prefab blocks stared dumbly with eye sockets at zero,
and not one living thing answered.

A childless black swing creaked.
Moths of ash hung on the wires.
Only on the roof of the madhouse sat a seraph,
smoked black, thinner by six wings.

He told me I was a system bug
and had reliably missed all the content.
Instead of answering, shuffling through the dust,
I held out a little bottle from my stash.

And we sat at the edge of nothing,
melancholy, motionless, and he
only stirred when sunset bled open again,
sucked down the bottle, burped, and whispered:
“Fucking great.”

stas.title: YOU'LL TUMBLE OVER THE FENCE OF DAY, BUT NOT AS THE SAME ONE
stas.text:
you'll tumble over the fence of day, but not as the same one
(as it all tumbled and spun on earlier days).
the day before yesterday I was a swallowtail,
yesterday a volcano.

you were a saffron moon,
then --- the chime of farandole.
today your tender age
is a white kerchief beneath a Merkava tread.

so the final link of evolution
turns into endless grief.
and what will I turn into now?

the wept-out glow,
a mugged sunset spits,
the little body fills with lead,
the field of vision becomes rifled.

fire me, Motherland,
in every destitute direction.
where could your prodigal son be of use?

perhaps
when the haze disperses,
someone will find me
dented into someone's bulletproof vest,
crumbled into years of service,
in birch sap,
where the thicket stood tilted with hazel,
out in the winter-crop expanse
under a robin's trill.

they'll find me, pick me up,
wrap me carefully
in a patched hem,
return me to a warm quiet home.

and the day after tomorrow
I'll be kissed again,
I'll become a child's giggle
on a wind-up horse.

in southern gardens
ripe plums will blush.

and you, I believe,
will come back beautiful too...

stas.title: LET'S MEET SPONTANEOUSLY
stas.text:
let's meet
spontaneously
at the gates to the grounds
of the crematorium
(the unloved leaves groan,
“ari ari ari, black-black”).

statistically,
roads most often
lead somewhere there,
not to some damned
hypothetical Rome.

we'll hang around and watch
human bitter-eyedness
mock
forever-crazy
punk June.

a firstborn poplar shoot
at our feet
will blow up the asphalt like an orphan,
and at once,
without saying a word,
we'll adopt it...

stas.title: TO READ POEMS TO TANK TRACKS
stas.text:
to read poems to tank tracks,
so neither battle caw nor accordion iamb:
boil, earth, let sorrow sprout,
a lily of the valley from each dog tag, an ear of grain from each casing.

(I'd like to, but I skipped it.)

and all through Novembers you kept carrying
the first snow in your palms
like a cradle with a dead infant.

everything around was torn apart and ground down,
and the burned forest stood like soldiers' wives
(or the other way round?).

how long does our vulnerability stretch?
which front is this now?

I'd fill the holds of our shadow fleet
with Cyrillic and Karelian moss.
let foreign border boats
swarm in like mosquitoes;
there will be enough for everyone.

(I'd like to, but what's the point.)

from your palms
spring finished drinking the last thawed drops
(how we lived this long I don't know).
the sky was clear,
clear enough to look under God's toga.

it even seemed for a moment that there were no more
bolts and corporals,
incoming strikes and black eyes,
gender wars or police vans,
brainrot or AI slop,
spies or oaths.

and for a moment
I wanted to read poems again
for no reason at all.

stas.title: I TOOK MADONNAS OFF YOU
stas.text:
I took Madonnas off you
(I was afraid myself; they forgave me),
peeled versts from the most defiant permafrost
(they sang to me in every northern dialect).

about you I broke open like an ice drift,
melted into blueberry juice.
(I look like a baptismal font now --- at least dip your little feet.)

the children of our cathedral spring
are sects waiting for the solstice.

in my cellophane chest
I carried them a stale piece of bread,
but turtle doves and rooks pecked it away.

such is the revolution.

two viscous willows stood in a hurricane,
stroking each other
(what were they thinking?).
all around, things whistled and youth was cut by fragments.

a one-armed evening threw a camouflage smock over your bare shoulders,
bindweed tied stopper knots.

it was so beautiful
and unbearably wounded,
beautiful and painful.

you said you'd cry poems about it,
and I caught cold in the wind.

I wore no crosses so heavenly snipers would have a harder time aiming,
but after you there are through-wounds anyway.

after you, wherever I run,
it's sobbing anyway.

stas.title: WOLF CUBS
stas.text:
Februaries were definitely invented
to be nature's
opposite of gospel.
dose yourself until spring
and hide under a sheet
while the Creator takes the heavenly bodies out of the toaster.

and under snowfall I confess
I've never seen carrion more beautiful than you,
and bodies fell flat into potholes.
I'd take you out of rehab.

Februaries are unbendingly sad,
someone's tenderness withers beneath snowdrifts,
while the two of us, wolf cubs, grew stronger in ravines
and painted our bedrooms with cave drawings.

bare your teeth.
we aren't the first here.
Mengele could have written our prologue with a scalpel.
our diagnosis --- hyperbole.
give us a time machine:
we'd gnaw Adam and Eve to death.

Februaries lick tenaciously and mournfully,
like a she-wolf in her death agony,
against raised fur
and against peace,
only multiplying submission by resilience.

we grew used to losses in advance,
favors no longer reopen wounds,
but still I ask...
when winter packs its things and moves out,
with all your homeless faithfulness
just become my
Palm Sunday.

stas.title: RAZOR
stas.text:
February screamed like a criminal stepfather,
wasted and unasked-for...

“You allow yourself too much, foundling.
Your place is by the powder snow!”

...breathed booze right into my face,
licked my mug raw,
abrasively and indecently...

(and what the fuck can you do to him?
he's a made man,
all the cops answer to him,
and his father is a general.

once I told a sunbeam-bunny
where February touched me;
it shrank
and ran behind the garages
like an illegal immigrant caught misbehaving.)

...followed on my heels, yelled,
shook cigarette butts down my collar,
spat under my feet...

before February I am an eternal little punk,
pressing myself into headphones and an old parka.

in my fist I clenched
a bared-tooth resentment.
if only this time I don't chicken out.
through winter, through winter
I carried a dangerous razor.

(and Nevsky is so dressed up,
even under the trip of coldocracy.)

now we'll turn the corner,
February and I.
(in my headphones, for some reason, Dua Lipa will be singing.)
I'll pull the razor from my sleeve
and, if things go well,
for a couple of days
I'll shorten the fucker.

(someone once managed it.
maybe I'll get away with it too.)

stas.title: ON MOTHS AND ANGELS
stas.text:
I was telling her
about moths,
or rather, how

every year,
at the breaking point of summer,
at the darkest possible timing,
when entomologists are simultaneously distracted
by calls from relatives and girlfriends' nudes,*
moths gather into a single front,
stream toward the stratosphere
on their final crusading flight
to the sun.
(if you've ever watched
one of them beat itself against a light bulb,
that wasn't a seizure,
but exhausting training.)
and there, at the finish line never once promised,
for lack
of fireproofing and nonstick coating,
they, as they should,
in unison
turn to ash...

after some time
the ash returns to the fatherland,
settling immeasurably
on tree branches, shack roofs,
sergeants' caps,
road services caught unprepared,
and foolish people call it snow...

I was telling her
about moths...

but before I finished,
she jokingly fell onto her back
and made a snow angel.

I got almost sincerely angry
at the heartlessness and fooling around,
but meanwhile caught myself thinking
that sometimes death
still
doesn't quite exist...

*I'd like to believe someone
does send entomologists nudes.

stas.title: SN*WY
stas.text:
Snow will come
like a hacked-open wound,
like a bell
fallen from a church in Bolshevik fashion,
and piles of Moishes
and imams' beards
without distinction it will sweep up to the ceiling.

The awkward dog-tailed Ordnung
will bury its snout
in cotton wool with chloroform.
The forward can't carry the match,
and cranberry freezes
across the throat.

(Give the beggar a coin for boiling water.)

You sit gloomily,
a sailor without a boat.
The whole district --- permanent Chukotka.
If only to reload the mortar
with a quarter-bottle of vodka,
and your own fortress
no longer has walls.

December --- a failed storming of the Bastille.
Heroism was abolished with goose down.
In the cold it's so easy
to justify helplessness
and blame disconnects
on the oppression of autocorrect...

(Dig up Tsoi, let him call for changes.)

And snow dove down
like dust onto antiques,
like ones and zeros in a seasonal estimate,
onto every atrium and afterlife.
Imagine cloud cover as blooming asphodel.

Searching for a checkpoint in blizzard hysteria,
like a stray cat
on top of a warm manhole cover.
And let all the saints drown in a shot glass.
Later, about us
as a prayer,
the thaw will ring out.

stas.title: STEPLADDER
stas.text:
Above the little village:
six houses, two hundred crosses.
The forest-steppe was fading out.
An eagle owl hooted, sighed
about the failed winter crop...

And Grandpa Afanasy
dragged a stepladder from the shed,
set it in the middle of the yard,
and, crunching heavily,
like a sack full of stones,
climbed up toward the night
to light the moon.

Sure,
it could light itself,
but Grandma once
told the city grandson
that lighting the moon was Grandpa's duty,
and the little one looked skeptically
as the old man, smiling,
climbed the rungs,
took a flint from his pocket.

Strike!
And a little star flashed...
Strike!
A whole flock scattered...
Strike!
And there you have the moon itself...

Grandpa climbed like that
every dusk except in a couple of downpours...
(Though even in spite of the clouds
his moon still lit up.)
The grandson smiled,
believed,
clapped his hands.
(How long ago was that?)

The years are past counting.
No one brings children's footsteps anymore.
Grandma dozed off, covered herself with goosefoot.
Even the little village
vanished into obscurity,
a tiny wart
on the body of an endless fatherland.

And Grandpa Afanasy,
without age or reproach,
still, again and again,
rises higher than sunset.
Because he's used to it.
Because men keep their word.
Because who, if not him?

Instead of flint,
a stuttering lighter
sounds a little off-key.

Strike!
A spark falls...
Strike!
A spray bursts out,
sticks to the canopy, smolders...
Strike!
...
A brother holds out a light:
“Here, we'll break through.”
And the grandson lies down
in damaged camouflage,
dusted with ground-up granary
and somebody's screams,
his hand pressing poppy petals.

The brother pats his shoulder:
“Remember telling me about your grandpa?
Well, look... you did it.”
(Strike!...)
And the moon lights up
through the half-dark of shelling.
The grandson smiles,
naively, childishly,
and a smile-tear
slides down the trench wall...

stas.title: MSS
stas.text:
I dreamed of a country
with neither devil nor boss,
barefoot youth,
the last papirosa,
and we were there,
bold, unenvious,
dry as oilcake,
taut as hanged men.
In our pockets:
wrappers, sparks.
July melted
like a barberry candy.
July barked,
and you kissed me
over palace roofs,
beneath dump-truck wheels.
Lips measured things in scarlet,
but it wasn't enough.
Then
the frame broke into slalom.
In the next one
we were raising hell, rebelling.
Where --- unknown.
For what --- I don't know.
We fired into the air,
dashing and inaccurate.
Butterflies sliced off
the sun's zest,
and doors flew off hinges,
bunched into flocks
above the dance of Mordovia,
above Severstal plants.
We grew more stately.
No one can scam us now.
The streets glowed red,
shutters were being sewn shut all around.
The streets emptied,
and you kissed me
with the city of Grads,
with Kandahar sunrises.
People traded their cries
for a chorus of cicadas,
and no rumor was dreamed of,
no jihad,
except us.
Nothing human remained,
and even we were only loops,
living handrails...
...
The alarm clock hurled
lightning hands,
loud and prickling,
deafened me like a burglar
climbing in through the vent window.

And carried you away,
I hope,
to another
sleeping me.

And I woke up,
and later I myself was dreamed
by an entirely different
country.

stas.title: PP
stas.text:
Tumbleweed,
roll my pain.

Pick it up, take it away
from the doorstep, the steps,
dodging trips,
over asphalt and directions.

Re-dust, re-mud,
with an untrained crew,
through the skeletal farms,
the pride of high-rises.
Carry my pain
so it belongs neither to ours nor theirs...

Past boundary markers,
introvert checkpoints,
the spit-roast road threads the country
where phoenix-cedars rose from ash,
where people shouted “HELLO?”
and waited for no answer...

Where coltsfoot,
asters,
Venus flytraps,
where they built a church --- and got a warhead,
where loving broadly is easy, pretending --- swampy.
Roll my pain
from flood to furnace.

Past apple-girls
who ripened quickly and spoiled quickly,
bayonet-knife boys
who rang themselves out wastefully.

Where a brave song is about a widow's cry,
icebreakers hope for luck.

The willfulness of rivers
that know no fairway.
Where an anatomist opened Cupid's corpse.
Where grief was asked on a date,
to breathe incense together.
And if it didn't come,
to hell with it --- fine.

Past swag-chicks and senile mumiyo,
across steppes and wormwoods,
explaining the different soils.
Traffic lights in puddles twisted like eels.
It grew dark, dreamed,
fought,
and something
twinged...

Tumbleweed,
roll my pain.
Roll it away,
then bring it back.
What am I worth without it?

stas.title: AUTUMN DROWSINESS, LIKE A DUFFEL BAG
stas.text:
Autumn drowsiness, like a duffel bag.
Getting ready to fall apart, you pack your stuff.
On top of a fifty-ruble hat
lies a bag with a half-eaten belyash.
You dive after it, missing in action yourself,
like a pack of cartridges with no shotgun,
so that by accident someone's practiced hand
might pick up this absurd baggage,
drag it to a warm little communal apartment,
hide it so no one can dig up
the airiness of anxieties or the clamor of an alarm,
only the timid firefly of a roll-up cigarette.

If only to get lost among the folds like a silica-gel bead.
Let Deus Ex Machina work its season,
and through a mouse hole in the corner of the burlap
tumble out naked and sleepy in April.

stas.title: BAD OMENS
stas.text:
*
On a thistle scratch
the seams come apart again.
It bleeds.
(Too pampered
for the dominant species.)

On a daisy
growing beneath the fence
of an abandoned chemical plant,
every petal rustles
that you're a faggot.

The Baltic greets you
with a dropkick to the face,
like a mad old woman hurling
cormorants at the windshield,
blowing Grandpa's medals away.

The farther north,
the closer meekness.
(Judgment Day is shitty enough;
if it's polar too,
we're completely fucked.)

*
And troubles and sorrows
crossed my road,
blackly, independently.
I dared touch one of them;
it stayed in my bed.

And curls spread
like escaped oil.
A dolphin's moan dreamed:
Main herz Brent.
Trawlers threw themselves ashore.

When the Bible ends,
only lovers will survive.
Or they won't,
in the name of propaganda
for a healthy complete family.

Neva waves
turned multicolor
with our chemical homelessness,
waiting for something from above
to thunder in condemnation.

*
The tremor of the information field
hinted either at Eschaton
or an approaching Ragnarok.
Dig like a gudgeon,
or waltz naked with idiocy.

In Yamal a village vanished --- taiga unfolded.
In Cambodia fish broke themselves from the sky on rocks.
Somewhere in Africa again they slaughtered
some unnecessary people.

In other words,
again
nothing happened.

P.S.
Yesterday she asked,
“When is Husky's concert?”
Today: “What's an angel's payload
in TNT equivalent?”
You joked it off:
“For a big boom, demand they add ‘arch-.’
And angels, at most,
can carry booze home from Lenta.”

She looked out the window
at flamingos of port cranes lapping up sunrise.
The city was waking:
a meditation of high-voltage vectors.
“You know, I think I just saw
halos and suicide belts...”

stas.title: RUSSIAN BRIDAL UNKNOWN
stas.text:
1.
And my bride
(is she mine?)
has more rings than can be counted.

a gold ring,
a nickel ring,
a tantalum ring,
an yttrium ring,
a blackened, bottomless ring...

all missing the fingers.
all from whom?

2.
From how many notes could her silence be solved?
From how many no's?

3.
On how many legs
to burst into the fray,
trip at the altar,
shout “Wait!”
tear off the crowns,
search
for new numbers in October(?)

(a little falcon freezes in a drop of amber;
ochre falls onto unruly heads.)

4.
And as bride-price:
a slanting fathom of bravado and a bad temper,
recklessness
(we'll grind everything down, don't chicken out, don't whine),
a handful of Martian soil
hidden behind the back.
(I invented everything,
but she hasn't been there either.)

She looks sternly,
tightening the belt of the Urals,
hands on hips,
as if to say:
I've solved everything,
and it was no use.

(she strokes the hills --- a coal rolls;
cold lace-like water runs over the wreaths.)

5.
Look closer:
cheeks beaten, eyes poured out.
Not made to suffer --- deprived.
Bruises are the most honest heraldry.
For your sadness I'd give
(in Varangian fashion)
both the desert pestilence
and Antarctic stasis.
(and all these are someone's brides too.)

(a snowflake bow, like fleeting flirtation.
thunder will strike --- cross yourself as if for the last time.)

6.
I invented all this,
God knows when,
God knows why,
God knows at whose expense
and on whom I drew the crosshairs.

And I myself lay exhausted
beneath your hem,
half-servant,
half-ronin,

while others took from you
the dress,
tender-leaved, tart-coniferous.

7.
How many more like me,
half-witted,
are buried
nearby...

And the urban world will sour around noon,
melt, ashamed beneath the zenith,
knock neural-domestic algorithms
out of rhythm like a flashbang.

And we'll fall away somewhere far,
where the motherland is deeper and unshaven,
shed armor and slosh through virgin land,
swallow the bitumen of predawn fog.

Slide as dew, lie under an embankment,
like broken rap lines,
on a lakeshore, sedge standing by,
with a full confession, without seal or shiv.

Heat lightning will flash like detectives' beacons,
and you, face buried in a stolen anorak,
will forgive me everything: the spoon, the bong,
perhaps even the fact that I'm an asshole.

Tomorrow will subtract us from the servers.
Dawn will splash us with a pyromaniac's orgasm.
Only two of us will remain on earth,
without scars or a single flaw.

And then again mute ballerinas
of utility poles will spin in dusty leggings.
Every road will reduce to a ring road,
to our private kilometer 404.

stas.title: IMPOSTOR
stas.text:
While stray and rootless dogs
licked Jesus' salt from beneath the cross,
I went out of myself and beyond what was permitted,
piercingly and visa-free.
Went out onto the balcony, saw spears,
saw pitchforks, only a little --- and everyone to the benches.
Saw children returned to storks under warranty,
heard the broken cries of someone's females,
heard the blades of angels entering the market,
someone smacking lips, someone flashing ID,
saw such an anthropomorphic Dead Sea
and those who managed to recognize beauty in it.

Saw, heard,
took it for granted, prayed for no one
so as not to jinx it and not dig through GOST standards.
Hovering centrist over chamomile tea,
whether cropped or tonsured --- still an impostor.
And someone will stare at me the same way
and, naturally, won't pray either.
A pack of mutts leaves for the industrial-zone bogs.
After us “new people will appear.”

And the life-jacket look will never go out of fashion
(it will become more contextual and heavier).
Someone will say the salvation of the drowning
is, after all, the work of hands, not knees.

After death everyone will end up somewhere,
but will there be room there for God's fucking hosts?
Love, rabble; party, rags.
Are we really to hope for an afterparty...

P.S.
A rich kid gets caught with weight and nothing happens.
A deputy's son runs down a victim and keeps driving.
Christ is risen.
Well, of course, with a father like that!

stas.title: BEAUTIFUL AND BEERY
stas.text:
In the north of the city, in an unnamed hypermarket
(unnamed because not a single bastard
has paid me for advertising it),
you and I stood there, accidental visitors, thoughtful and cultured,
beneath the sign “fresh vegetables”
(not all that fresh vegetables).

An assortment of greens beckoned like the jungles of Cambodia,
the jungles of Laos, maybe the Amazon.
(if only to dive in there, then good luck finding us.)
Somewhere around here we silently avoided saying
that if there is a swordfish,
there must also be a shieldfish.

Then we walked, five half-liters each, through the white night,
and I kept silent about
the difference between a bore and a darling,
about a gay milling-machine operator having three members on each hand,
and whether the Sex Pistols had their front sights filed off.

Toward morning, two three-hundreds in,
above the waking Neva,
the rusty hinges of gulls began to creak.
And there I stood, beautiful, beery ---
that is, beautiful because beery,
and beery because opium is banned.

And there you stood, beautiful and beery:
beautiful because always,
beery because “fuck it all.”
Somewhere here (and this will enter the annals of our history)
I finally made a joke about shit out loud.

And somewhere here (worthy of a chronicle),
beneath a sky clear and gilded like pilsner,
you laughed, made a joke back,
and seemed funnier.
I thought, “What a bitch, don't come onto my territory,”
and fell in love...

stas.title: FOOL
stas.text:
If an idea and an ideology are equated with disease,
people will be divided into carriers, spreaders, and miscarriages.
And me, choosing my category, I'd like to carry your blown kisses
in the mesh bag of my lungs past the wastefulness of exhalations
and other sharp things.
If only I knew where to carry them (navigation hasn't been invented,
and mud greets you at least up to the hubs).
Samurai are fine; samurai have a path.
Fools have nothing but rasputitsa.

If hope and faith in anyone besides yourself are treated as half-life,
you'll see around you neither whole people, nor valuable ones, nor virgins,
only Brownian commotion.
And I toss my half-wittedness and unseriousness into a little boat
folded from your palms,
knowing for certain it will never sink.
Let the anxiety of Ladoga or the diuretic Murino stream
spill between Scylla, Godzilla, and the raising of retirement age.
A fool was given “perhaps” precisely so
that against the elements he might at least force an accidental draw.

And if competitiveness and recklessness are explained by animalism,
while they figure out who gored whom and who gave whom the tooth,
I'll flatten myself like a ray across your knees and tear your tights
with my post-chordate spikiness
until I shrink into a parody of balyk.
The earth will tremble for a long time from those who come out onto it
and explain the importance of walking upright,
and from debates over who cooked the primordial soup so rich and thick.
But no evolution can disturb a fool's simplicity.
A fool will remain young forever.

Someday the will will be found to admit
that all amour and tenderness are not synonyms for war.
At that moment the united disarmed forces of all republics, kingdoms, and federations
will pick me up and accept me into their ranks.
Someday I'll stop being a fool.
If you can,
just
wait
a little longer.

stas.title: EAST
stas.text:
Yura, we fucked everything up.
I saw stars only on shoulder boards and infidel flags.
Neither inspires trust.
We simulate honor in slow motion and through input lag.

Space is an illusion, Yura.
Hubble was bullshitting; the sky ends a meter above the bunk.
Don't touch it with wax or torch.
Whatever the knives are like, so is the nudity.

And what's left?

Blue courtyards, counterintelligence pigeons,
heavy jokes like a funeral feast for a tractor driver
(his pig Pyotr stabbed him in the side while taking his wheels,
but it's not halal here either, nor recognized there).

Youth starts with vape exhaust.
(a colleague jinxed the superiority of synthetics.)
An old tram decomposes in the depot,
loved by no one, without lucky tickets.

At the end of the tunnel, light from burning villages.
No more chastushkas or collective-farm punk.
I'd demobilize too, Yura, straight out of Homo sapiens,
sewing aiguillettes on poser-style, and inside out.

Yura, we...
But I believe this is a multi-move operation and part of a cunning plan.
Space is only what is inside us,
and only through nothing can nirvana be understood.

stas.title: THE FREEDOM OF SELF-DESTRUCTION
stas.text:
The freedom of self-destruction
is the only thing they can't take from us.
A crumpled cigarette pack will fall past the bin,
the banner of the most defeated army.
(Get out your hidden cash.
Let's go party
and tell everyone to fuck off.)

On the news again: abusive terraforming.
Someone's mother, bare-breasted,
passionately kissed by artillery fire.
The starving were sent as humanitarian aid
thirty-five tons
of yellow snow.

Every day another cyclone.
The little feathers of the sky got damp and matted.
Apparently the sky isn't made of duck down.
You hide your neck in a scarf, your thoughts in snuff,
remember who you owe which stuff.
You wander like a rowan tree.

Self-love is an ever-growing list of paraphilias.
Fortunately, for necro-... there's still too much alive inside.
When crossing the road, look both ways.
Cool yourself down, but don't loaf around.
Fell down --- two sets on the bench press.

A blizzard is eternal misgendering:
supposedly a bitch, but it howls like a castrato.
Living off the north, you think only
whether the firewood will last until tomorrow.
And all I want
is shamelessly
to unfreeze
in your embrace, cozy
as Evenki national dress,
and touch neither church porches nor funeral wreaths.

stas.title: PLATFORMS
stas.text:
A train going from point “A” to geolocation “Why the Fuck”
unzips the country's fly as if before love.
I spill onto the platform like a pioneer,
ambassador of the outermost flesh.

(my leg went numb.
my de-capitalized little heart throttles.)

Dust in the face, a gaze for some number of yards.
Either peaceful sky or mined palate.
In a repeat-offender land where rye meets rust:
pay debts, just don't lose your shit.

(calendars reported to me about your sadness.
why are you such a crybaby...)

Wheels rattling over sleepers: breakcore.
Taking anamnesis, iron-born arrhythmia.
In the clamoring sweat of the communal car, stop being reserved-seat.
Just don't step into nostalgia.

Along villages (six houses, two hundred crosses)
of conspiratorial happiness the color of public-utility dreams.
Rings of cigarette smoke coiled around the neck like a constrictor.
I switched to feeding on bitten lips.

Orphanage larvae blinked with cataracts.
Dragons were blown from the sleepless volcanoes of power plants.
Aborigines fused with the coordinate system.
(if they knew where to leak away, they'd lose weight.)

Responsibility stared into the forehead with a Mongoloid slant.
(an armored horde of unfinished words.)
Windows smeared pointillist canvases.
A prodigal asshole smoked in rocked sleep.

Like sign language,
flora branched
about your sadness
along the geometries of stations.

A train from the region “Fine” into the zone “Once.”
I spill onto the platform.
“Hello, Mom.”

stas.title: TESTAMENT
stas.text:
When I finally die
(and that definitely won't be for an extremely long time),
I bequeath, so everyone loses their fucking minds,
that my obituary be replaced with a random Krovostok track
and the funeral march with the chatter of mating waxwings.

Don't bury or cremate me; just make a stuffed figure from my little body.
Let it stand in your hallway
as if you stole the lamest exhibit from the Kunstkamera.
Next, I leave all my savings to cats' tails,
and all my ill-wishers to the Jeffrey Dahmer fan club.

Then sneak onto a military base
and scratch my ellipsis onto a thermobaric canister.
That burn will clearly be brighter than any verbal one.
Also, find all my hidden pigeons and release them into the world.
Give the devils an amnesty; care for them and pamper them.

I know you don't like mourning and most likely simply don't know how.
That's for the pliable and fine-boned; in general, not your route.
Therefore I bequeath: smile and sing so that both the Sirens and Alkonost envy you.
Dance everything I never could.
Jump into the deep without a parachute.

Though what kind of wills can there be? You were always headstrong.
Freedom is the most trembling beauty.
So when I finally, super-not-soon,
do whatever you want,
my dear Emptiness.

yanur.title: I LIVED RATHER STUPIDLY IN DECEMBER
yanur.text:
I lived rather stupidly in December:
fruitlessly nostalgic for May,
reaching, straining, sparing no strength,
running headlong (where --- I don't know).
Tired, I'd send it all to hell ---
absent, late, spending,
gave up hopes of finding myself a harbor
and could stay in bed for a week.
I waited for the end --- everything has a limit ---
the way a guillotine falls on a neck.
I suppose I don't know any other way.
January came, but I didn't get any wiser.

yanur.title: YOU'D THINK THAT'S IT: EPILOGUE
yanur.text:
You'd think that's it: epilogue.
But again you don't sleep until morning ---
drilling the ceiling with your eyes
in anticipation of another loss.
I toss and turn, can't sleep either;
and so we press ourselves to the window frame
to catch the predawn hum
of the forest gloom beyond the window.
The sprint turns into a marathon ---
time thickens and slows.
Wrapped in blankets, we go onto the freezing balcony,
like a new Chud and Merya,
and Baudelaire walks together with Vivaldi.
Soon the pussy willow will bloom.
The Saturday sky is dressed
in the morning twilight of former losses.
So into a single “we” was gathered
what had been broken into pieces.
This is the anxious joy of darkness,
my destructive happiness.
This was what I convulsively saved myself with,
diving without fear of depth;
the way the tremor of a living string
submits to sensitive fingers.

yanur.title: AT SUNSET I'LL GO OUT, LIGHTING A CIGARETTE
yanur.text:
At sunset I'll go out, lighting a cigarette,
to the shore where flocks of birds curl:
the bay stands there, resembling a bay,
and gulls circle in the sky like gulls.
Houses stand, resembling houses,
a road spreads out as asphalt.
Centuries pass smoothly, year by year:
a little will pass, then --- a little more.
Round circles of windows shine,
square squares of houses stand,
and it would be silly to expect any others.
I stand, smoke. Then I'll go back.

yanur.title: WHEN SADNESS ITCHES IN THE THROAT
yanur.text:
When sadness itches in the throat
and you feel sorry for everyone in the world,
then the hungry muteness of words
won't express a damn thing.
I catch air with a numb mouth,
but that's not what this is about:
in deathly letters I catch hold of essence
to breathe it into words.
Volapük sticks to the lips like persimmon,
everything falls from the hands.
The tongue tangles itself; the drive is gone.
No reason to open the mouth.

yanur.title: ABOUT HOW WIDE THE COUNTRY IS
yanur.text:
I think about how wide the country is
while standing at the bus stop,
especially when my sneakers are wet
and the bench is painfully cold.
My bus is late again.
It must have caught every red light.
Or perhaps it's plowing across the country's vast spaces?
What could possibly delay it so much?
Let them solve this problem in future ---
where are the city authorities looking?
Can the distances really be such
that it cannot overcome them?
I stare around the corner almost deliriously,
and it seems: just a little more and --- there it is!
But no, it isn't around the corner,
and I stand, and think, and wait.

yanur.title: FOR NOTHING AND FOR NO REASON
yanur.text:
For nothing and for no reason,
just because, and meanwhile,
above the river --- a park. In maple shade,
far from noise and problems,
the sound of an accordion is barely heard.
The sheer-sided Eden is silent.
Not far away, rowing with an oar,
Charon floats on a narrow board
to the rippling song,
and as a reflection in the river
hills and settlements spread out,
swaying slightly in the breeze.
And, divided in two,
reality floats in blue:
two shores, two horizons
merged into a single nature,
and in some white haze
they settle on the grass.

yanur.title: I WILL BE FAITHFUL LIKE A STRAY DOG
yanur.text:
I will be faithful like a stray dog
to everything here that never came true for me.
N. Kiselev

Returning half a stranger,
I gather everything now scattered apart,
and stroke by stroke recreate the picture,
remembering what never came true.
Night has fallen, and I stand by the house
that in a previous life was yours:
the entrance door --- barely familiar now ---
and the bench where we no longer sit.
The stairwell, the window, the playground swing;
weeds multiply in the sandbox.
I pull bookmarks out of memory
and thoughtfully read the diaries.
So in blurred twilight, furtively,
the past appears far away,
what in unstable shifting memory
remained like lipstick on a cheek.

yanur.title: A REMNANT OF SLEEP SLID THROUGH THE WINDOW AS A RAY
yanur.text:
A remnant of sleep slid through the window as a ray
and cheerfully hopped along the frail branches ---
outside, intoxicating spring,
and I took out my dress overshoes.
I'll step into dazzling dirt,
enter enchanting slush:
since the brown script has spread,
it's time to put the ink away and stop crying.
Take out your coat, though it isn't May yet ---
sail with me through the streets like a liner,
and, intoxicated, understand sharply
that life can no longer become any more real.

yanur.title: HELLO, DEAR ASTHENIA
yanur.text:
Hello, dear asthenia,
we've met again in November:
I wither like a flower in shade,
drown in a courtyard-well.
Days fly past the streets ---
the eye cannot keep up with them ---
only my hair stirred
from the speed of their flight.
Day after day I either carry
my body like a burden in circles around the house,
or drill the ceiling with my eyes ---
so much that the neighbors complain about the noise.
And I drive myself to the limit
until all drive is gone ---
there's simply nothing else to do,
and no other way to live.

yanur.title: A PSYCHIATRIC PATIENT STARTED SHOUTING IN THE WARD
yanur.text:
A psychiatric patient started shouting in the ward:
“Please, peace, give me peace,
because I no longer know who I am.
If only peace would come again soon ---
please tell me who I am.
I have never been Napoleon.
I am me. But what is --- I?
Brain and body? An imprint of being?
‘I’ is locked in an unfamiliar space,
and emptiness screams with a piercing ring.”
He pounded on the door --- asked to be left alone,
shouted that he wanted silence,
tried to tear the shirt off his back
and demanded freedom, but hardly
will anyone hear him in this carnival.
He'll exhaust himself and fall face down,
then gather the scraps of consciousness ---
quietly rise, walk to the bars,
and from deep within his eye sockets
catch birds flying beyond the bars.

yanur.title: HOSPICE
yanur.text:
An inconspicuous little house with a narrow path,
sadly gray, crowded,
but music plays there from morning
and gulls circle above it.
It stands alone on the outskirts ---
hidden from ordinary people ---
swarming inside with its wounded entrails,
choking on sobs.
Leaving softness for morning horror,
through haze it sees in the distance
that from burdensome reality
someone has again been taken away.
And the house looks, frozen in horror,
through an empty window at the sight,
while gulls continue circling in the sky
and the music keeps playing.

yanur.title: YOU GO OUTSIDE AND JUMP
yanur.text:
You go outside and jump
into a soft refreshing snowdrift,
and you just lie there and look at the sky:
dignified clouds crawl by.
And ravens fly across the sky,
and snow falls from the sky
to become another snowdrift,
and you don't need anything anymore.
You stretch out on the snowdrift and lie there ---
you could just die here.
And passersby walk around you
and look on disapprovingly.

yanur.title: I THOUGHT DARKNESS WAS NOTHING TO ME
yanur.text:
I thought darkness was nothing to me,
but a wolf pack was set on my side ---
I curled into a wretched little ring,
forced my eyelids open. Thought I was dying.
In a single moment I was out of the game:
the flash made everything swim and flicker.
Twisting, I quietly stood, stepped, sank down ---
a grave appeared vividly before me.
Life hooked a claw into my stomach,
though it had seemed short and pitiful,
and I thought: “It won't heal now” ---
it grabbed and held me in a death grip.
I endured it. But I understood exactly:
sooner or later a period will have to be put down.
I don't shy away from nonbeing,
but I still hope for a postponement.

yanur.title: WHEN NOTHING REMAINS
yanur.text:
When nothing remains
except continuous light,
it will no longer matter
whether it's that light or this one ---
a zone will triumph
of piercing emptiness,
dazzling white ringing,
scorching purity.
The year cannot be named by number:
signs will lose their meaning.
Light will scatter across the world
and disappear into darkness.
The fading hum of discord,
like a ghostly veil,
will settle over naked expanses,
like any other.
There will be no one to repent,
nothing to mourn
amid sleepless chaos
in the eternal harmony of darkness.
The world, neither dead nor alive,
will lose its shell.
The cosmos will contract to a point,
and once again there will be an explosion.

yanur.title: SHE ROSE ABOVE THE RIPPLING WATER
yanur.text:
S. Kh.

She rose above the rippling water
and disappeared into dense fog:
circling somewhere between dream and waking,
and the damp air beckons somewhere.
It will carry her in pieces to the gulf,
mute, wounded, naked,
to where she will howl like an orphan,
to where the winds blow piercingly.
And people catch the body in pieces:
they decided that farther means deeper,
and failed to notice how she flew away
to where a voice is no longer needed.

yanur.title: ACCEPT ME, TAKE ME, MY CITY
yanur.text:
Accept me, take me, my city,
where I have been burned out and ground down,
where I fell after rising and disappeared ---
the canal's water closed above me.
Here everything past is blurred in memory:
images ripple in a frantic swarm ---
but sometimes what was forgotten until now
rushes from the deep onto the shallows.
Have mercy, I already feel bad enough.
I'm forgetting who I am and where I'm from.
Yes, my source is not here --- what is there to blame?
The current will not turn backward.
And I float along center and outskirts,
though exhausted, emptied, wounded:
I search for a gap, passing dirt and vileness ---
I'll find one and feverishly wedge myself in.
But even if you don't need me,
I remain stubbornly a Petersburger ---
take me, as you took others a hundred years ago,
three-eternal Petroburg, Saint-Leningrad.

yanur.title: I LOVED YOU ALL, EVERY SINGLE ONE
yanur.text:
I loved you all, every single one,
and cannot rid myself of you:
now one, now another, like a sharp avalanche,
sometimes crashes into memory.
Old breaks call to one another ---
against my own peace
I rush to flip through albums
and feel that it still aches.
I learned to live without you, but here's the trouble:
I never mastered the skill.
Yet my tongue won't turn
to say I need no others.
You remain something eternal at the edge,
something I can entrust only to a pencil.
For some reason I preserve you inside myself;
perhaps that is why I write.

yanur.title: DEAD CAT
yanur.text:
Once we were nothing but “kitty” to each other,
so simple and sweet, tender-wild.
Every week ended so that, caring about nothing,
we could lie there and you could fall asleep purring,
burying your little face into me from Saturday to Sunday.
Though now none of this matters.
I remember even our positions had different names,
because we weren't dogs but kitties, so --- cat-style.
And in the morning we listened to Tchaikovsky or read Baudelaire.
You said you wanted kittens with me,
you were my black little kitty, and I took it on faith,
though I'm not used to taking everything I'm told on faith.
I dreamed of the smell of the pillow, and with that smell
memory torments me, tugging at my nerves.
And I still find little packets of sugar in my pockets
saved long ago for you.
When it hits me, I dive in with new force,
though it seemed I'd long since had all strength knocked out of me:
I slowly stop distinguishing what I dreamed,
what I actually remembered, and what I invented.
I wandered through echoing courtyards and threw drinks down my throat;
much of it I couldn't remember if you killed me.
At some point I came to hate the city
for how insistently it reminded me of you.
Trying to escape, at first I looked for an excuse,
then said fuck it, booked the tickets, drank until nauseous,
packed, came to the station, but fell asleep there
and missed the train because I was dreaming of you.

yanur.title: PRACTICALLY BY ACCIDENT, AT RANDOM
yanur.text:
Practically by accident, at random,
the way the Mandelstams chose Voronezh,
for some reason you chose the city of Pskov.
So behind your back the bolt slid shut:
gone away, eaten away. You'll catch up ---
and by then you'll be out of place,
and you yourself won't be glad of the meeting.
Only intoxicating memory will jerk,
strike the back of the head like an axe butt ---
all that remains is to smile sadly,
playing the role of a tragic clown,
while backward flash
fragments of years that will never thaw,
until reason cuts in, sobering memory.
Perhaps it's for the best. It's time
to leave the past in its viscous thickness,
not claw at it with your nails,
though there once felt like blood kinship.
Yes, it's empty now, and will be emptier still:
yesterday stayed in yesterday.
Perhaps it's for the best. It's time.

yanur.title: I GATHERED MY OWN CHAOS FROM THE SHARDS
yanur.text:
I gathered my own chaos from the shards
into some clumsy monolith,
fastened it, and now I carve myself from myself
the way marble and granite are carved.
Uneven here, rough there ---
I catch defects and crush them into crumbs:
gripped myself roughly as if by a switch ---
carving the human out of myself.
Here you cannot bend --- you have to break,
break yourself and fuse yourself again.
You'll hardly find the glory of an idler
when you have to labor so zealously.
You cut, break, chase after something,
trying to shovel through everything there is:
cutting away flaws segment by segment
until you use yourself up entirely.

yanur.title: AND TIME IS OVER, AND THERE IS NO MORE ROOM
yanur.text:
And time is over, and there is no more room:
we've been crossed out, we don't exist.
I took off the sheet, I'm folding the blanket ---
the bed will not take my name in vain.
I packed my belongings into a worn suitcase,
look at the stripped space:
how will I repay my mental debt to it?
Clearly not with interior decoration.
Sadness looks kindly from the mirror,
winks at the room: “Best wishes...”
This view froze in my eyes for a long time
and trembled, reflected on the retina.
I went downstairs, left the entrance. Well, forward?
The door closed; it needs no help with that.
The stairwell already doesn't recognize me,
and I think it never will again.

yanur.title: IN TRUTH, I ONLY LIKED MYSELF
yanur.text:
In truth, I only liked myself.
I liked feeling something like happiness.
Now --- amid the sensation of nonbeing ---
I want the world torn apart.
I liked the feeling when there were not one but two.
I liked being cared for, feeling as though I was liked.
And if I had to give something in return,
with a heavy heart I'd pinch off the necessary little bit.
So you wouldn't get bored, I arranged an attraction:
pushed you on swings --- swung your mood, nerves, strength.
Knowing how you loved attention, sometimes I withheld it
so you'd value it more when you got it.
One can love the beauty of the game and
the imitation of passion, the skill of causing a burn.
Even when I stared into your eyes for a long time,
I was really only admiring my own reflection.
In the end, let no one else have you.
After me let nothing grow in the world:
animals, grass, trees --- let all of it fly into darkness,
and you with them, and your future husband and children.

yanur.title: EVERY DAY IS MORE WINTER THAN YESTERDAY
yanur.text:
If only winter would hurry up and come, and cover all this.
I. Brodsky

Every day is more winter than yesterday ---
it has become cold to live in the world.
The icy wind pinches your cheeks
like that relative in a fit of temper,
the one you never missed.
You trudge home on the warmth left over
from embraces that seemed to be yesterday.
Nearby --- some kind of playground ---
why does the ringing shout of “hooray”
make the soul feel so vile?
Apparently everything will be settled soon.
Only a little more to endure.
Whiteness will cover the earthly firmament.
Brodsky waited --- it came. All the more so,
he has already lived his life, and I --- haven't begun.

yanur.title: THROUGH HALF-SLEEP IN THE JOLTING RAILCAR
yanur.text:
Through half-sleep in the jolting railcar
you look tiredly at the trees.
We stop: a night platform,
some snow-covered little station.
White flies fly toward the light,
and beyond a cracked column ---
the entrance to a God-forsaken buffet,
open around the clock by the station.
You no longer even know whom to think about,
and life only throws mines at you ---
so get out for a pastry
and a vitamin salad.
Sit down unhurriedly at a table,
taste the modest food, feel it:
all the salt is in directness,
there is an art of its own in this lightness.
By the assortment of mineral waters,
the gloomy, slightly gray-haired buffet woman
is almost nodding off.
She should just sleep, knowing no fuss.
What if you suddenly address her,
say something vulgar like, what a babe,
and offer to spend some time together ---
who would stop you from simply staying?
Just start a family with her,
go work at the local plant,
live in harmony as in paradise,
sleep calmly and think simply...
Exhaling, you feel: there will be a day.
Life cannot be beaten so easily.
Cast off the mute shadow of doubts
and don't miss the departing train.

yanur.title: ON THE RESCUE OF THE DROWNING
yanur.text:
It was life slipping out from under my claws,
crunching beneath my foot like weak ice,
and while it collapsed faster and faster,
I kept putting everything off until later:
ignored the freezing crack
hinting that everything was splitting at the seams.
Not wanting anyone to climb into my soul,
I declared that it wasn't for them to decide,
and kept living like an idiot,
tripping over every bump,
beating against life like a fish on ice,
deciding that people drown alone.
I thought I was cut to different patterns,
even if you cut me with a knife ---
life, as usual, kept leaking away,
while I grabbed at a sieve.
When I was being carried off, I remembered one thing,
knew a truth belonging to no one:
you can calmly go to the bottom,
you can drift with the current,
but it's better to flounder against
everything in the hateful mess, and
even when people are placing bets
on whether you'll make it to retirement.
And when the time comes, leave
brightly, calmly, without panic ---
the way the musicians probably played
on the sinking Titanic.
Sooner or later everything will end;
I too will certainly end.
So let it be bright if we can't be saved;
no need to play rescuer.

yanur.title: I'VE PUT ON A LITTLE WEIGHT AND I'M ALREADY DRINKING MYSELF AWAY
yanur.text:
I've put on a little weight and I'm already drinking myself away.
Emptiness grows around me.
I dump another bunny:
every one is not you, therefore --- the wrong one.
I'd like something to work out, of course,
I invested myself properly. Then
it became clear that the third is extra.
Didn't escape. Even if I'd wanted to.
That's why I write, though I won't send it.
That's why I started drinking, getting fat:
consider it harassment of the body,
since I can't get rid of myself.
I'd like to squeeze your hand again,
wake up beside you as before.
We haven't forgotten what happened “before”;
I'm afraid we won't manage to forget all the “after.”

yanur.title: RUSTLE OF GREENERY, FIELDS ALL AROUND
yanur.text:
Rustle of greenery, fields all around.
Barely remembered:
poplars thundered loudly,
the poplars thundered.
It was no one's fault,
yet from the earliest morning,
wherever you spit --- geraniums can be seen.
Geraniums can be seen.
The sun burns, fuel oil in the head,
you don't remember the date.
Caterpillars crawl somewhere.
They crawl somewhere.
Petals, injuring the sky,
are steadily carried by the wind.
A caterpillar will crawl across them
and not notice.

yanur.title: CONFESSION
yanur.text:
1.
The only thing that kept me from despair
was that this would definitely pass:
a day is good only because it ends,
the same is true of a month and a year.
But it keeps going, keeps going ---
no end, no edge in sight.
Faces flash through the bustle,
forming a gloomy host
that leads me along the edge,
pushing from behind,
when time after time I discover
that without me things are no worse than with me.

2.
The story, of course, is not new ---
how many times I've seen and imagined
people trying to justify
their claim to mercy with dignity.
But if you look at it another way,
perhaps one should bite the bit:
count your vices as good fortune,
so existence won't be boring,
so you can continue the unequal fight,
changing faces in a circle.
Sometimes it's useless to drag others down;
you can only descend yourself.

3.
Out of great love for everything mortal,
for this heaviness (which is tenderness),
raising a cross, I don't rise from my knees ---
and that's fine, let it be, I'm not the one to carry it.
Darling, for you I'm ready
to sink to the very bottom,
to be the last asshole
no one could ever find.
Nothing remains that I would reject,
and when the route is over,
little bones will fall into the earth,
but they are unlikely to sprout.

4.
If life decides to chew me up
for all the extra things I've done,
I probably won't worry at all,
because I was an asshole for my neighbor's sake.

yanur.title: IN THE VAST EXPANSES
yanur.text:
In the vast expanses
we sometimes remained without those closest to us,
and at times left without saying goodbye,
as if blowing up the powder beneath ourselves,
so as to be neither here nor there
and impossible to trace.

Belatedly
we remember the past with a kind word ---
the pain of loss healed like fractures ---
we step forward as though
nothing had ever happened,
not a trace of the past remains.

Perhaps shadows
will flash somewhere at the edge, but you can't catch them,
and they slide like fingers between keys,
and settle down, hiding the sun from plants ---
darkness spread above them,
but memory did nothing to help us.

yanur.title: WHY DO YOU SEND PEOPLE TO EACH OTHER, GOD
yanur.text:
Why do you send people
to each other, God?
Or don't you know either,
and everything goes in circles:
we seek each other, find each other,
then lose each other ---
how many circles do we find
like this before paradise?
How can one get warm in a frozen world? ---
please, don't lie to me ---
they wondered in Ancient Greece,
in Ancient Rome.
I, so everyone would be stunned,
penetrated into people ---
does it speak about me,
or scream about them?
That happened as easily as hello,
even in passing.
It smells of passion
with a shade of lust.
I arch from the thought:
how fleeting it is, yet
a human needs another human
only temporarily.
Either this is how you punish us ---
for what exactly? ---
or this is how you save us,
but invisibly.
First you bring us together
so the blizzard won't eat us,
then both are saved,
but from each other.

liza.title: I DANCE ON SHARDS OF MEMORY
liza.text:
I dance on shards of memory.
I take them in my palms, smell them,
wash my face.
Scratches remain.
Love is never soft or expired.
And what do I have now?
Here it is, a clean flat mirror.
I look into it,
and there is death.

liza.title: SUCH A SUMMER --- BY DAY IT SITS ON YOUR HEAD
liza.text:
Such a summer --- by day it sits on your head,
by evening it crawls above the pavement.
Such a life --- you couldn't handle it three times over ---
under God, under stuff, under attack.
Let the horses loose, the dogs; let it be
as if all the darkness with you had never come true,
the weakened fist.
I cut this evening out of space.
Hold onto my hand --- I'm a subway handrail.
Let's imagine reverse, start all over,
go backward, rewind to the intro,
to cells, molecules, the foundation.
When we choose how to drown this time,
what will you choose, tell me, knowing what you're doing?
How am I to protect you even from your own eyes
(my helpless youth never knew how).
I hate dreams: there you're healthy and whole,
an inky gaze biting into sunset.
Pin the prescription to the sky with a needle,
and the wheels roll at random.

liza.title: MAYBE I'M DREAMING OF YOU OR WHATEVER
liza.text:
Maybe I'm dreaming of you or whatever.
On the tram you put your head on my shoulder.
The snow fell so hard it plastered over memory.
Now to spam it with stupid conversations.
The wind howled in caps lock, couldn't find peace.
By force and across the bridge, and now with your hand
you wipe mascara from my face, and along with it
erase a layer of death from me.
And there was something about a cause, friends, and a chain,
and a scratch from it on the face,
but for some reason
the heart is bleeding.

liza.title: TEACH MYSELF TO WALK WITH HEADPHONES ON
liza.text:
Teach myself to walk with headphones on,
unafraid of a silent knife.
I was taught to be obedient,
and I'm almost wearing a burqa.
But behind the door there is definitely someone strong,
in the reflection definitely someone frightening,
and I am definitely a hydrophilic little leaf,
growing up in little balls at home.
Someone will come and rip me out by the roots,
simply say hahaha without a bracket.
A useless Midjourney candidate,
an old little iPhone without a box.
And in the headphones all kinds of things are playing
that make me imagine myself a rock idol
for one second between glitch and hang-up,
before I hide from the world.

liza.title: A DRAWBRIDGE, BEYOND IT --- PREFAB ROOFS
liza.text:
A drawbridge, beyond it --- prefab roofs.
Snow merges with the sky, interference, suspension.
A glance at the keys, before my eyes --- Misha.
As if he never left and stayed here.
Center. Snow again. Around the corner --- quieter.
Everyone to work, me --- to gnaw through science.
Out of the wind into the courtyard, and in the courtyard --- Misha.
Smoking something, warming a hand in his pocket.
It snowed in Thailand today, I hear in my head ---
there, trembling and speech break against sand,
and above the wave bright Misha floats,
and everyone God could not keep safe on earth.

liza.title: LONGING FOR THE CITY AND INSIDE IT AT THE SAME TIME
liza.text:
Longing for the city and inside it at the same time.
Frost, Caribbean pools, lighting,
Siberia, infants, nine variables,
one given, but where is the equation here?
And we have to play as different pieces:
you have a pawn, I have the six of clubs,
and somewhere between the lines on a smoke break,
between little clouds of smoke, imagine us together,
while a child's hand searches for an eraser
for pen ink, to redraw borders.
I'm not looking for you, more precisely, a slip of the tongue ---
I don't know what, but it will happen again:
longing not for the past, but for an invented world,
and turbulence of the heart that is so damn annoying.
A child draws dash-dotted lines with a marker,
and the map tears in an inconvenient place.
Tikhvin, Moscow, Frankfurt am Main --- all the same:
everywhere I am not, a flicker lives.
But you'll come --- an arrow or an exam ---
with your hand remove denial from my forehead,
and my Ordnung grows tangled again:
frost and bullets, maps and winds,
work, a line, trauma or slogan,
and everything we talked about until morning.

liza.title: IT'S QUIET HERE, I CAN HEAR MYSELF BREATHE
liza.text:
It's quiet here, I can hear myself breathe.
I thought: what if I exist?
And the heavenly parachute will fold,
harnessed by hand.
And there is no green icon above my head.
The embryo of the future kicks for the first time,
and I am really walking home.
What a sky, look, what a sun.
Cats walk around, press themselves into corners.
I press myself to the earth --- where is the malice, where is the rocket?
And rock a miscarriage in my arms.
Such a sun, look, such a summer.

liza.title: SYMBOL DER FREIHEIT
liza.text:
The symbol of freedom has a specific height, clothes, eye color.
Rides a scooter if the train is delayed.
(Complains about Deutsche Bahn.)
The symbol of freedom speaks every language, but not mine, and that
will never upset us.
*I, Princess Nesmeyana with six years' experience, officially declare that I*
¡laughed on 17.02!
*And I am not the least bit ashamed of being cheerful.*
Bird shadows slide across the facade.
We hid a promise by crossing pinkies.
Only joy is paler than my face, joy.
And now we say goodbye: me and my symbol of freedom.
And I laugh.

liza.title: EVERY SOUND AND EVERY BREATH --- SUCH PRESSURE
liza.text:
Every sound and every breath --- such pressure.
Don't creak and don't ring, don't pull the handle.
There isn't enough cash for the honest and the holy,
but look, just look at what they teach us.
Everyone good around us --- that's different.
There is good money and there is bad money.
He's good if he praises you into ecstasy.
You're bad because being honest --- that's basic.
I'm a little owl, but there isn't enough amplitude
to turn away from everything in one sweep.
My head is like a meat grinder --- pure miracle,
spun up, I'm taking off without instructions.
Every day --- an attempt to fight the boss.
I wake up underleveled with a club.
Every voice --- a scheme for a DDoS.
What do you want, devils, where's the action again?
I can barely drag myself under a thick shell.
I'm going toward grace without healing potions.
But now I can't run, can't stay.
I love him, and that's enough for me.

liza.title: SOMETIME WE ARE STANDING IN A FLOWER OF HOUSES
liza.text:
Sometime we are standing in a flower of houses.
You say you have strength enough for everyone,
strength --- for the world and certainly for my shelter.
I watch the movie and feel no interference.
And we stood there, me and my youth.
You say you'll give me a superpower.
I think life is easy as spitting once,
and twice --- jumping over the grave.
And we stood in the middle of the flower,
at the heart of a courtyard by the sea.
You described how easy life would be,
but spoke as though in adult language.
And why, so many years later,
am I concentrate, powdered drink mix?
By feeling, I don't exist at all.
No one's hand gives me an electric shock.
I don't want to tell you
that I jump through life like a kitten.
You cannot hear about my fate,
and I increasingly just feel sorry for it.
You cannot hear how, ringing behind the wall,
I was establishing contact with a pregnant planet.
You say your strength is for me.
So where are you, and where is all of it now?
Whom do I tell that I'm afraid of freedom,
that a whole boiler of my love
has definitely been drunk, and the water was shut off?
This isn't a demo, it's definitely a spoiler.
And we stood in the middle of the flower,
and youth was leaving forever.
You said there would be enough strength for now.
I gave all of mine away.

liza.title: JOY IS THINNER THAN LACE
liza.text:
Joy is thinner than lace.
The thread snaps in a loop.
Whom will I tell that I have
nowhere else to come?
My youth, blood,
a moth's wing,
searches for a starting point
in time and in hands.
I am pregnant with grief.
It makes me sick.
This is my love story:
cold and beat.
Life is just mold.
Anger is just style.
Flowers made of songs
sprout in the throat from hurt.
A taxi, also a little taxi,
drives me to my own home.
I am extra in this home.
I am a lump in this throat.
I gave my days to everyone.
The evening is longer than the week.
In the world we are all alone.
Whom will I tell that I am more

liza.title: I'M ALL LIKE THE WHINE OF A MOSQUITO
liza.text:
I'm all like the whine of a mosquito,
like hearing after a heavy concert:
to fly upward toward trouble at my own risk
and scatter across fifteen kilometers.
Make something up, lie, let's go looking
for my summer air, my remainder of oxygen.
I seem to be cursed if my home is a bed,
and I don't really have any gender at all.
But two little palms, both with emptiness,
I carry what I have, though there's lots of wind in them.
Why I carry it to you I don't know, but wait,
let's slow our step for the last two meters.
I'm only a whine and I look, look.
My eyes are one huge thermal imager,
and it seems, caught on a hook,
I see the gradient, meaning he is near.
The minute's fragility, the sharpness of a knife wound,
as if you might suddenly disappear from the planet.
And every time summer will not be enough for me.
Again I won't say a single word to you.

liza.title: CYCLE 1530
liza.text:
1.
1530 days without sound.
I bow and scrape before people.
Hello, you can come in without knocking.
The door opens on *mi*.
(I simply remember.)
Conclusion: no pathologies detected.
No Catalonias found.
All your hollows
fit our depressions.
1530 days of nonbeing.
Every evil evening an exam.
Muted me,
waving my arms.

2.
I dream of you again, and I suppose
spring will come (first into dreams) then
all the leaves in the world will gather closer to May,
will speak as if with your mouth.
They'll tell me: you need to live more vividly.
Look at that, see, and over there, that.
I'll listen and I won't believe,
leaving all joy until later.
I dream of you again and I laugh,
squeezing my diaphragm like a sponge from pain.
April air rolls toward zero.
April is in fact a kind of little zero.
Spring will come, forgive, and become okay.
There is something to forgive, since I'm stuck in textures.
My tear will settle on a flower,
then flood the pallor of plaster,
then be cut into several parts
by brown beams of half-timbering.
And I come to you --- over people's heads.
No, I'm not God, I'm just a water strider.
I started rhyming like in that lit workshop;
I suppose they loosened my tongue.
At the dentist it was easy to breathe through my mouth.
At least I breathed; living was another matter.
And sleep is light like a wagtail's tail,
a patch of sand, Gothic Quarter.
For some reason you speak Russian,
but again I didn't understand you.
I dream of you, and in it I'm so pathetic
I told myself: bro, hold on.
A residue will remain for the whole day,
and a scar will remain on me the length of a life.

3.
Toniiight we are younggg
Youth is not a boomerang.
On some sunny day,
does someone think of me?

4.
The scarlet heart will soon become dorblu.
I don't love you ---
God said. You've exceeded your limit.
*Or maybe he does love you, just doesn't say so.*

5.
I quit smoking.
I quit work.
I quit patience.
I quit someone.
I quit being sighted.
I throw my little ball.
My sunny little ball of anxiety.
Well, who will catch it?

1530.
--- What would you do if you knew the summer of '19 would be the last?
--- Nothing.

liza.title: A PITY THE STELLER'S SEA EAGLE IS NO FRIEND TO HUMANS
liza.text:
A pity the Steller's sea eagle is no friend to humans.
Still, it's wonderful that it knows only bird language.
It matched its talons and beak by colors and rivers:
yellow and yellow --- find 25 differences.
Some article talked about foolish adults:
strange people thought they'd managed to become friends,
so they could see how a wing cuts through air.
People carried fish to the shore for the birds.
The birds were simply too lazy to hunt themselves,
ate little fish from silly human hands,
quietly laughed in bird voices,
the wind joined them, bursting into laughter.
Bird, you're a bird, but your claws are almost cat-like.
I'm human, only my little beak seems bird-like.
Jump --- off the bridge, I'm a frightened foster boy,
only I won't become a target, game in the sights.
Jump and off the bridge, finally I hear the air.
Here come the sea eagles, catching the fall.
Now I cnnt be tamed eithr and th soun
d flis I fly my brd sng

liza.title: RETROGRADE LANDSCAPE
liza.text:
I start the text from the end, the thirst for life --- from a pit.
Unable to fit my shoulders into Moscow's latitude,
I am an NPC, a transparent point, the most
sensitive invisible gesture on this strange evening.
But we stand in a shop window; the city --- an advertisement.
Naked on every side, I cover my mind.
But I stand on the counter; my city --- a drama,
a high-voltage nerve, a retrograde phase.
Ride and ride. Graffiti, forest, Khrushchev blocks.
A lullaby knock will say: I'm a friend, don't be afraid.
Here is my life: from Farforovskaya to Sortirovochnaya ---
my personal six minutes before I'm mown down.
A house in indigo-colored lace of sorrow.
Gazes layer like a monster from Elden Ring.
Ride and ride. From muteness and displacement.
Ride with a knife, like the owl from Duolingo.
Check my head as baggage so it won't malfunction.
Hear fear signals like the sound of the Buzzer.
One step and a can of beer short of death;
for life, a voice message and mineral water were enough.
A house in indigo-colored lace of sorrow.
Hands, pu-erh, robe and a jazz selection,
tears and dreams, love, cherry cigarette,
a high-voltage nerve, a retrograde phase.

liza.title: I DON'T REMEMBER MY NAME
liza.text:
I don't remember my name.
I don't know the time.
I am only action, running,
human concentrate.
Talk me into speech.
Snow dies in green.
I die --- snow
plasters over my eyelid.
Talk me into speech.
I don't remember yesterday,
night, year.
I don't see my own hands.
Metonymy.
Light and shadow.
Translation.
Words have turned into sound.
Talk me into speech.
Shake me out of suspended animation.
With a hot hand ignite my eyes.
Catch me (I live on the move).
I traded away color
and grew a shell.
No one told me
whom and what I am waiting for.
Light light.
Crust.
All that remains of us.

liza.title: GHETTO
liza.text:
An extinct ghetto.
A leaf scratches the courtyard.
Branches and silhouettes
the wind braided into a pattern.
I stand and don't bend,
an extra streetlamp
in a calculated row.
And behind my eyes let there be
emptiness and a home
I will not come to.
A frozen-out ghetto
to match my face.
Trunks await summer.
Winter is nearing its end.
It's already sixty-eight.
In my petrification,
either freedom is hiding,
or a voice beneath the body has gone quiet,
or insomnia sleeps there.
The trunks beat out the uneven rhythm
of John Cage's accidents.
Again it seems everything is wrong,
coming in sequence --- faster.
Spin faster, monochrome and dirt,
while I stand here as a boulder
that doesn't want to --- that's one,
two --- cannot find a choice.
An extinct warehouse of boxes
with points made of fire,
walls made of cardboard,
has become more alive than me.
Thinking physically hurts,
so it's not worth thinking about.
The ghetto will fall asleep peacefully.
The cigarette will end.

liza.title: LAST LETTER TO DARYA
liza.text:
I no longer give a damn
who hit whom,
and who started the fight,
because I remember it was me.
I no longer know at all
who loved whom,
who cried and when,
but for some reason I remember it was me.
For many years now I haven't been able to swim up,
crawl beneath your hooks,
get caught, confuse the edges,
because I remember exactly where I was.
Because I remember every bottom of a glass
flying upward beside my face, and all
the essence of substance, the essence of these secrets and scars ---
it was me, I'm telling you, it was me.
Because there is a boundary between the eye and the world;
a planetary sheet cannot fit inside the pupil.
I wished you only good and drew in dotted lines
all the features on you in which there was only me.
I no longer give a damn, I'll tell you again.
I'm not saying goodbye to you and won't put a period,
because after any period two more dots will rise,
and every goodbye is said in longing and at night.
And in your salvation, and in the flow of the calendar,
and in the wish to burst a balloon made of emptiness,
in every anxious nerve --- all of that was me.
But from now on I do not know where you were in all this.

liza.title: NOT FOR HIM
liza.text:
And now everything is solemnly cut by whiteness.
The spring of little boots jumping resonates into the stars,
to later become a sharp sedimentary stripe,
food for the mouths of streetlights vacuuming the air.
And joy from the light will multiply in blue-gray pupils,
and people rejoice in the cold as if it had warmed up around them.
And everyone will begin this day in snow-light leaps
as if the soul had lost five kilograms.
Winter in the neighborhood will snap its bridle from joy,
for everyone out walking, everyone who I don't know what.
I smoke with my left hand and hold a first-aid kit with my right.
He told me this was not for him.

liza.title: LOUDER
liza.text:
I laugh the loudest here.
I'm the last to leave.
I'll be the highlight
of every ridiculous life.
Into the wall of a vast host
they will fire, and triumphant
from behind the wall mine will be,
and cornices will fly.
I drink all truth to the bottom
and in the mornings throw it
from the window at passersby
so they'll finally see.
And my serenades
grew together with veins so tightly
that when you leave
they drill into my head.
I laugh the sweetest here,
the same funny teenager
in the same linen shirt.
To be even a little adult,
they tell me that farther on
it will be dark and harsh.
And I laugh; I'm scared.
What else do I have left?

liza.title: A FIST BEAUTIFULLY
liza.text:
A fist beautifully
merges with the wall.
There it is, red:
direct perspective.
Alone with myself
is even more terrible.
Like someone shot,
I fell, writhed.
That's the kind
of love that happens.
And for weeks
I rode in silence,
stuttering.
Jumped on Friday.
A fist won't
lie --- useless.
Depending on the mood,
step by step --- into battle.
Compared
with me,
iron walls
seem
like women's fabric.

liza.title: BELLFLOWER
liza.text:
As if there is something I cannot say,
hanging my gaze among smiling mouths.
The sorrow of a bellflower, crystal is its seal,
a heavenly drop on a thread, like past progressive.

You forbid me to rejoice in things,
but secretly I rejoiced in the little flowers
that absorb bitterness on an empty stomach,
that are also meaningless, invertebrate.

As if there is something that pricks without end;
you can't pull the leech from the heart without tissue.
The delicacy and light of the bellflower's face
will also be trampled by children and hit with a stone.

As if there are only you and your longing,
your pedestal of sorrow, your exhaustion,
an athletic gesture, an Atlantic hand ---
only you could be seen, or so it seemed to me.

As if there is something I cannot say.
A fragile cap will find an answer in the soil.
The sky looks into your mouth, opening its maw,
and I reflect the sky, losing color.

liza.title: TELLING FORTUNES BY BIRCH TREES
liza.text:
Tell fortunes by birch trees, crossing out three at a time,
against my sky: loves me or not.
And you'll turn toward the glass, saying, look
how black little rivers crack the white color.

And I'll turn toward the palisade of forest trunks
where God mixed some green into monochrome.
And you tossed your nostalgia into my shelter,
and there it sprouted while the shelter decayed.

And there it took root, in this new reality,
pushing out mine, which was long and far away.
Birches like a stencil of lace sorrow,
projections of sky painted milk-white.

And the wind drags us along metal threads.
A train is a trolleybus in reverse.
We'll go into the courtyard, shout everyone come out,
and the ball is already waiting, left by the goal.

liza.title: AUTUMN DIDN'T GO ACCORDING TO PLAN
liza.text:
Autumn didn't go according to plan, moving in quick steps.
We drink and drink, but remain sober.
And with this autumn I grow cold in time with the wind.
If only it would pass completely, pass faster.

Here melancholy flowed into agony.
When I calm you, you calm me.
Across truck roofs, our soles already burning,
and the sky burns more convincingly than September.

It seems to me that growing cold means hardening.
With the years --- less warmth, below minus twenty.
My grown shell no longer squeezes me.
With it, it's easy to say hello and laugh.

And my bulletproof vest made of white cold,
and if something is unclear --- better not.
But beneath it, even in dead calm, something blazes,
something alive --- a heart or a fuse.

And my ice is so terrifying that against it will shatter
the fear of all who fled, the lie of their foreign sun,
everyone hostile to you, even a little.
There is nothing but the heart, you, and God.

There is nothing, only cold around and you.
Strength and truth; your features are in them.
Only after finding morality do you receive a choice.
For everything allotted, I say thank you.

Cold advances on soft white paws.
Cold doesn't care whether you're from east or west.
The burning glow of truth, love, and duty.
There is nothing but the heart, you, and God.

liza.title: THE TEXT STANDS IN A STRAIGHT FORMATION
liza.text:
The text stands in a straight formation where there is nothing to lean on.
Its weight is so great, it can easily replace a foundation,
support, concrete, granite, and my honest heart.
I say mine, meaning yours.
Text is a distortion of life where anything can be embellished.
Doctors cut out what is unnecessary; text is also a scalpel.
Out of the seven known things it will cut out anger and envy,
compressing them into a beautiful song only a couple of drops in volume.
Happiness is freedom. Freedom is synonymous with strength.
Accept: nothing is eternal, and lose what is frightening.
But waking up hurts, and I would ask you,
