but one doesn't ask for such things, especially when they're important.
A word is synonymous with text. Text is a prototype of placebo.
Our foundation is carved in calligraphic handwriting.
There will be no place for me here; you were never anyone here:
support, concrete, granite --- over the years I became them for myself.
You want nothing, having skillfully cut the lines.
You'll step over me like Nevsky, scalpel and iodine in hand.
Your honest heart will die next night.
I say your heart, meaning mine.

liza.title: REMEMBER, THERE WERE GOOD ONES
liza.text:
Remember, there were good ones.
We waited for *love* like dogs.
My ringing past,
my premonition of a fight.
Vacuum, white noise,
a breath cut off at the root.
I smash my fist,
and there is no blood on my hand.

katerina.title: IF YOU'RE ANGRY AND GLOOMY
katerina.text:
If you're angry and gloomy,
if inside you --- war,
I'll braid your Bickford fuse
into a rope,
throw it to you,
seal the breach in the hold.
I'll set out wine --- drink,
set out bread --- eat,
dry you off, shelter you,
etch out the excess noise.
And for my care
I ask only one thing:
don't get used to me,
don't take me away.
You know how many there are ---
those who need me,
those tormented by pain
whom I am destined to save.
I am not always good.
You hugged me --- now let me go.

katerina.title: THE NEVA FLOWS IN MY VEINS
katerina.text:
The Neva flows in my veins.
The bowstring of the bridge has gone taut ---
its span will shoot into the night
a little later.

Into my spine, like the keel of boats,
the cast Peter and Paul spire is sewn.
I am the native daughter
of Palace Square.

Fixed in place --- forever! ---
islands like birthmarks
on my forearms.

I store the cry of your gulls,
every wind-soaked moment
in my liver.

Even the blue-gray, bitter smog,
you, my angel, could never
etch out of my lungs.

Like resin stuck to pines ---
I'm with you even if things
are completely,
outrageously bad.

For three centuries now,
you have been both Piter and Leningrad,
a cord between Rus' and the Baltic.

Like the cannon's noon salvo
I explode into you. You are mine.
I love you,
Petersburg.

katerina.title: TO REMAIN SHADOWS FROM FRIEDRICH'S PAINTINGS
katerina.text:
to remain shadows from Friedrich's paintings,
the unvoiced hope of an exhale
there

on the Gulf of Finland.

an almost perfect embrace,
unable to speak
and confusing concepts,
tripping over boxes of my own inventions.
future minus past equals present.

not to wish for better than good,
because it will come back to haunt us.
let it remain like this.

streetlights night street,
getting ready to go home,
gathering my thoughts on the way.
I'll say: I will, I can, I'll endure.

not make it, not manage,
fall into something difficult,
and ring and ring,
not with blades --- with sheaths.
to speak
not to you but as if to the Gulf.
not to say,
having played too long with far-and-near.
not to say
what was already on the exhale.

look:
this sky
is just like Friedrich's.

katerina.title: I WANT TO WALK OUT TO THE NEVA AND RUN INTO PONTE VECCHIO
katerina.text:
I want to walk out to the Neva and run into Ponte Vecchio,
so the needle of Peter and Paul answers the tower of the Signoria,
so a tired eyelid lowers over the pupil-sun,
cutting the ropes of weights hanging from the heart.

I want to cross the bridge as a weightless tightrope walker,
bend into a bow to the applause of the wind.
Between the Winter Palace and the faceted Palazzo Strozzi,
to live knowing neither totem, taboo, nor veto.

I want to throw myself to my knees right in the square,
seep through marble, soak into the wall.
If this is possible in any universe,
I want to swap worlds --- tell me the price!

But the broker is silent for lack of offers.
Instead of a dome --- apartment-block honeycombs.
Is there anything sadder than the silver backs
of abandoned airplanes frozen motionless?

katerina.title: ELEVATED NOISE LEVEL
katerina.text:
An elevated noise level
will sooner or later cause trouble.
I'll tell you a story
about Gauguin's friendship with Van Gogh.

Gauguin admired Van Gogh.
Van Gogh admired Gauguin.
Walking with a drunken gait,
they bumped into walls

when along the avenues of Paris,
and later --- southern Arles,
having seen an aurora above a roof,
they returned together from a bar.

Together they drank half a liter,
talked in the evenings,
mixing colors on the palette.
And everything was peaceful. But a quarrel

flew down from Olympus like a kite.
One insisted: “Nature
through art!” The other:
“Art through nature!”

They stopped speaking,
wanted to pour out their anger.
One cut off his own ear,
the other flew off to Tahiti.

Was that quarrel important,
who was right --- no one will answer.
The point is that now in the Hermitage
Gauguin and Van Gogh are neighbors.

katerina.title: PERSEPHONE
katerina.text:
I have a migraine and my vision flickers,
eternal twilight triples inside.
spare me, spare me, Hades ---
in your house
I am not queen.

I feel suffocated here; neither diamond throne
nor riches of underground mines flatter me.
I want to be free
from every freedom!
cutting locks and roots,

I want to be like verbena pollen,
carried away by every gust of wind.
inside these walls I'll become quieter than the walls
and cover myself in ash.

only the feeling containing both night and day
will sprout through anxiety like a pomegranate seed,
and someday
I will return to you,
I will return
back.

katerina.title: LIFE IS LIKE ARCHITECT ROSSI STREET
katerina.text:
Life is like Architect Rossi Street ---
smooth and combed,
the color of autumn,
while you have --- mud season, a clearing
somewhere in fields far from civilization.
Though perhaps it only seemed that way to you ---
drunk, in a bar, aged by half a century:
instead of a clearing and mud season ---
a loose woman and prosecco.

Life is like Nevsky Prospect in mid-May ---
you stand there,
speechless from beauty,
look at the bridge, Klodt's quadriga,
choking on love,
but someone
will inevitably come up and say: “Hey, señora,
why are you frozen there, let me through, bro,”
and go inspect the bronze balls
for Napoleon's profile.

Life is like the Fontanka embankment
in the days of the Nameless Erik:
when there were ten years and one tantrum before the stone pavement.
To build something solid, you have to start in a swamp ---
not always, it's true, but that's how it happened here:
one inspired man loses his mind,
and after him the whole country grows flesh.

Life is like an alley you see for the first time ---
the houses seem familiar, the yard grows over with cherry trees,
but something doesn't fit, doesn't catch,
remaining a hole in hungover memory,
chips that appeared from nowhere.

Life is like a street.
And mine hasn't been built yet.

katerina.title: SPLIT APART, LIKE MIRRORS
katerina.text:
split apart, like mirrors,
blue ice on a black river.
maybe it's not a river --- resin
boiling in milk.
so we look --- eye to eye,
brown into blue. the surf roars.
maybe it isn't ice either --- but me,
who hasn't found the way home.

katerina.title: ON MY WINDOWSILL
katerina.text:
on my windowsill
gnats were always dying,
round-the-clock death right before my eyes,
and there was no way to stop it.

*as if I were dropping bombs on them*
*as if I were shooting them at dawn,
as if I were waging this war.*
they did nothing to me,
but kept dying
on their own,
and I watched and watched,
trying to understand
whom they were striving toward so hard.

katerina.title: YOU COME FOR TEN DAYS, BUT YOU USED TO LIVE HERE FOR HALF A YEAR
katerina.text:
you come for ten days, but you used to live here for half a year.
you say the house has grown old and no longer remembers who you are.
the city stamped you like a mountain against once-loved squares.
you say these streets are full of pus, though once there were love and faith.
silently you walk one after another through avenues learned by heart.
you drew halos around every trash bin but never understood where you were.
I remember those eyes of yours, bright clots of happiness.
and the fact you told me nothing back then
is not the city's fault.
and anyway look: the same park, the same bridges and spires,
wind in July, sand on your teeth, glass in the coastal silt.
look, even the Wi-Fi password is the same seven letters and a hash.
the mirror in the bathroom, shampoo, conditioner, the same toothbrush.
the same neighbors, their shaky marriage still doomed.
and the fact you stopped loving me ---
you're the idiot yourself,
and the city has nothing to do with it.

katerina.title: I WAS LOOKING FOR A RHYME
katerina.text:
I was looking for a rhyme
but never found one.
perhaps it's still too early.
perhaps there is no rhyming seed in me
and nothing from which to grow it.
maybe I haven't yet met the right person
(as if I alone were somehow not enough).
maybe we have poetic incompatibility.
or maybe I simply
cannot have
poems.
so I adopt images overheard from others,
adopt as daughters rhymes spotted in books.
I raise them,
cherish them,
buy notebooks and pens with glitter,
but increasingly
they stare with alien cosmic pupils
and whisper:
*you are not our mother.*
*we never wanted you at all.*
*we never asked you to drag us into this miserable home.*
*we'd have been better off staying there*
*where we were,*
*where we belong,*
*and never becoming orphans,*
*because our parents are immortal.*
*and you ---*
*go away.*
*rot in your loneliness,*
*gray and unnecessary.*
so even my poems rejected me.
and I sit on the edge of the bed,
open my fingers,
my lines fly apart like silver Patronuses
into their true universes,
carried by a wind I
cannot even feel.
emptied,
I fall
and become earth
where nothing is grown,
trampled by heels.
hair and eyelashes turned to dust,
bones digested in the world's stomach,
and inside my belly
something kicked.

katerina.title: TALKING TO YOU, LORD, IS HARD
katerina.text:
Talking to you, Lord, is hard.
Like with a father --- I don't know how; I barely breathe.
With a friend most often words aren't needed,
but right now I want there to be --- words.
To talk as with myself is above my station,
and often I don't understand myself anyway.
Only one word has lodged in my mind ---
but it does not submit to the mind.

katerina.title: GRANDMA KEEPS ON LIVING
katerina.text:
Grandma keeps on living,
growing frail darkly, poorly.
Lives like an ordinary little pill
of lint on God's sleeve.
Lives, saves every kopeck
for bread, milk, and beets,
and a simple candle in church ---
but who would save her herself?
Grandma keeps on living ---
a pale bedsheet.
Lord, really, really,
that isn't me,
not me?

katerina.title: LEFT-LUGGAGE LOCKER
katerina.text:
from childhood I remember only dust on the roads,
especially in summer,
the blank wall opposite my window,
and oil-soaked air
you get used to.
I remember them calling home late one evening,
saying Grandma had been hit by a car,
that we urgently had to go somewhere.
I remember not going.
I was thirteen.
I remember hands burned by nettles,
a boy throwing stones at me,
the hospital smell in the clinic,
in the street,
in the bedroom.
I remember bites of jealousy at family holidays,
a notebook with my first poems
flying from the balcony,
the cat Vaska,
who never came back.
I remember the smell of the dump near the playground,
the iron edge of the swing,
the burned remains of the neighbor's house.
that's probably all.
all my luggage,
which I left in a storage locker
at Ufa station
fourteen years ago.
I left everything
in a fireproof box
and wear its claim ticket around my neck
until it becomes a small tag
on the big toe
of my right foot.

katerina.title: LOVE AND SLIPPERS
katerina.text:
what's the point of talking about love
when you can simply make soup,
pour it into your favorite bowl,
add plenty of sour cream,
sprinkle parsley,
*absolutely no cilantro!*
serve fresh black bread with it,
and that spoon, remember, from your childhood.

but as you know I can't cook,
so while you're at work
I spend all day walking around the house in your slippers
so that when you come home
they'll be
warm.

katerina.title: SUMMER SHADOWS FLEW DOWN FROM THE EVENING SKIES
katerina.text:
summer shadows flew down from the evening skies.
lilac branches are gentler than a girl's beads.
if I disappear you won't ask,
and lighter than a tear will be the splash
of Neva waters, the rustle of blue-mouthed twilight.
if I disappear you won't remember my sound or trace,
either the hum of hives or the blooming of cherries.
here are already six, already seven sad lines, but no ---
there is nothing,
and you don't see it either.

katerina.title: ON THE 1ST LINE OF VASILYEVSKY ISLAND
katerina.text:
Here is the street where everything began.
The house yellows with its peeling facade.
It would suit a square or a garden ---
not a line pierced through
by winds from the embankment and the bell
of the old number-forty tram.
Here is the street where nothing is new ---
and there's nothing bad in that.
The café still bakes pies
with cream cheese, herbs, salmon.
Now it doesn't close at eight ---
we could have talked another whole hour
at this little table in a secluded corner.
Who were we arguing about? Pasternak...
How I remember those half-signs,
fluttering like a crane in the hand!
That's how it was --- but that's not the point.
The moment stopped, beautiful and carefree.
And suddenly it seems: now, now I'll meet
if not you, then at least someone ---
but I will meet someone, because V.O. itself
looks after us like strays,
and in window glass is reflected
what can be read only in the eyes.

katerina.title: SOME DAY --- SIMPLE. NOT A DAY --- A LINEN TABLECLOTH
katerina.text:
Some day --- simple. Not a day --- a linen tablecloth.
Trees wait for spring --- it brings to the table
milky grass, short as memory,
while the cauldron still boils with honeyed sleep.
An ordinary day. Not zero, not one ---
roughly five sixths (though the count isn't exact).
And twilight and night sting the nose with mustard,
and tears are in the eyes, and something else there too.

katerina.title: THIS IS FREE VERSE OF POETIC STUBBORNNESS
katerina.text:
this is free verse of poetic stubbornness
in which I claim
that if blood is healed with love
much can change,
that banal rhymes
can have sacred meaning,
be the carbon of poetry,
the resin of a poem.

because rules are obeyed,
but only rebellion is admired.

because besides words,
the voice matters too.

because when the original is lost,
copies become valuable.

because literature contradicts,
it does not nod along.

and even this text,
which not everyone will call poetic,
is exactly that.

katerina.title: THE SUGAR OF STARS GLITTERS ABOVE THE CROWNS
katerina.text:
The sugar of stars glitters above the crowns
only as far as the lake of dawn.
Don't look for long
into my bottomless eyes:
there are no runes or hieroglyphs in them ---
their dungeons are empty,
and a fire without fuel burns
with a bad kind of beauty.
And the mighty are helpless,
and the happy have no happiness ---
they seek a witch's treasure
and find a barren flower.
And find only little things ---
there is no miracle in my land.
Only to you, out of pity,
I tell this truth.
How many tears were shed in vain
instead of rain for the horsetail!
I'll give you my hand, lead you out of the forest,
then wave a handkerchief.
But you don't turn your sad gaze
away from the brown flashes.
Well, look into me --- this bell
is not rung more than once.

katerina.title: FOR ONE SECOND
katerina.text:
1
this year death didn't exactly come often.
it practically moved in with us,
poured itself tea,
took candy from the bowl,
at home, without embarrassment.
people around me melted and burned
like candles in church,
fuel in a gas tank,
furniture in a fire.
and others,
who had been seas,
became the Aral Sea.

2
people around me left,
and I began writing this poem
to stop death.
I know how stupid that is,
but what else can I do?

3
I put down a period,
listened.
no one is singing a requiem,
nowhere does a hearse growl,
all my friends are smiling
living smiles,
not from photographs.
and I thought:
there it is.
it stopped.
it ended.
even if only for one
second.

katerina.title: THE MOON FLOATS IN BRINE
katerina.text:
The moon floats in the brine
of the sky like a clove of garlic.
Spring carried in its hem
March's first puppy.
In the cloudy suspension of dill-like grasses
fountain ice snorts.
On its caviar business
smelt goes into the Neva.
Until April snow ferments in the square
like softened baklava.
It's not a city, but a hangover
with a ringing head.

katerina.title: AT THE DISTANCE OF MEMORY
katerina.text:
1
I turned into sound:
knock
knock
knock.
I turned into a beat,
a sign,
a grain
sprouting in your skin.
you turned too
into light,
gift,
no,
yes,
let,
meaning,
path,
upward.
you turned
entirely,
and I'm already here,
a light suspension,
settling:
dust
on the words
in which you
were,
on the fault line
that you
are,
and on the pain
in which you will remain
from now on.
try
not to look
at me.

2
I'll run back
to the distance of memory,
and sorrow will fly
from my shoulder.
instead of grief,
torn for years toward happiness,
only the sea,
mine equal to yours.
but inside it's as if
the key won't turn.
and our fingers, remember, like Michelangelo's,
and the last words
everyone needs,
the meeting of two seas
far from shore,
and my poems like the
Bering Strait.

katerina.title: THE NEVA BOILED WITH ITS UNCHANGING SMELT
katerina.text:
The Neva boiled with its unchanging smelt.
Cucumber-smelling fish, you wanted children
and flew with delight
toward the little Baltic Sea,
unafraid of snares and nets.
What do you care for the troubles of the present ---
sing of the future, Gamayun!
In the terrible roar of sizzling oil
I promise to hear
your final song.

katerina.title: HONEY
katerina.text:
mow or don't mow,
the flower grows.
pollen ripens in it
into fragrant honey.
bees swoop in,
buzzing their hymns.
you climb into the hive,
take out sweetness
on the tip of a knife.
and when your
unearthly mowing comes,
between the ribs stings
steel frost.
fallen back into the sky,
you look into the mower's eyes.
from whitened lips
pollen rises upward.
there silent angels
cook the final honey.
mow or don't mow,
the flower grows.

katerina.title: IN THE HOLLOW OF MEMORY
katerina.text:
live smile-snails,
starfish of kisses,
fish of words,
seaweed of thoughts,
urchins of hurt,
corals of fears.

I thought
the memory-hollow was bottomless,
Mariana,
inaccessible Martian,
but it turned out
to be a box without a lid,
a shallow hollow:
the armpit.

katerina.title: WE LOVED --- JUST NOT EACH OTHER
katerina.text:
We loved --- just not each other,
but the fear of living alone.
Calling the tremor of fright love,
we went to the bottom.

We went to the bottom, placing a veto
on the right to avoid measures.
Love does not exist without an answer ---
and you answered me
that you no longer loved me.

katerina.title: MATERIALITY
katerina.text:
materiality
reduces the flickering world
to a school globe,
as if a laughing boy
had been walled into a checked suit,
sat at a desk,
obliged
to provide exact data
on the coastline,
while he himself
thinks about a wave,
light,
in a transparent dress,
running over sand
and knowing better than anyone where
right now
France ends.

katerina.title: FOR EVERY SICKLY LITTLE POEM
katerina.text:
for every sickly little poem
the Lord lays a stitch across my mouth.
sharp as shame is his needle,
so that from now on I cannot in vain
say, sing, think aloud,
so I remember the gift of servants ---
silence.

katerina.title: DOT DOT COMMA
katerina.text:
dot dot comma,
night night, that other one.
bridge over the little river like a dash,
you and I beside the bridge.
the world is opposed to us.
hocus-pocus, krible-krable,
our story is like a river,
we are the paragraph line in it.
we are hero and heroine.
cut off
on the inhale
the name.
read it --- from the page.

katerina.title: TWO STREETS AND FOUR SQUARES
katerina.text:
*someone else's storm outside the window.
I'll watch it
until I get wet.*

1.
*dedicated to Roma Rakitin*
I read your poems
for lack of anything else to do,
out of necessity,
for pleasure,
to the point of disgust,
and I dream
of other people's backs of heads,
and every time I know
it isn't you.

2.
*dedicated to Olya Olkhovskaya*
you live in a house with an oven,
never go farther from it
than to buy mayonnaise,
bake stupid pies
with your favorite filling,
devour them and don't gain weight.
and once
you used to inspect the bar
at yet another station,
wondering
how many glasses of alcohol
they'd sell to one person,
whether that's still a digit or already a number.
and aprons
with puppies suit you so well.

3.
~~dedicated~~

4.
it's either Sheremetyevo Airport
or poems by Boris Kutenkov.
I can't tell,
but I wander from train to plane,
living on sugar from vending machines
with endless poetry selections,
and text
Roma Rakitin,
waiting
for him to answer.

5.
Roma Rakitin
and Olya Olkhovskaya
got married,
got Max for the dog,
started living
as if the world were two streets and four squares
and they --- understood it.
but then why
does Olya Olkhovskaya increasingly
pause in O'Key
by the Martini shelves,
and Roma Rakitin
finally answered me?

katerina.title: WINE IS KIN TO NEITHER LOVE NOR FRIENDSHIP
katerina.text:
wine is kin to neither love nor friendship,
and the only thing I ever played well with was my own happiness,
so that my bone would shudder and crack,
because bliss will be proportional to torture,
as if happiness without blood and sweat were tasteless,
as if it had been issued to me by mistake.

katerina.title: DON'T MIND THAT SOON WE'LL BE GONE
katerina.text:
don't mind that soon we'll be gone.
your poems, like some zoomer contraption,
will have their turn, oh believe Marina.
having believed, I ask: repeat the spell to me,
so I too can taste that hope.
that's how we'll go, exchanging strength.
that's how we'll walk the road to the hill,
not looking back, so it won't hurt so much.

katerina.title: LET'S MEET BY THE GRASS
katerina.text:
let's meet by the grass,
where a dead cat
is already rotting from the head,
tripping the gaze.
tomorrow the poor thing will be removed,
the capital will shake itself off,
our fates will change route,
our meeting won't happen.
so let's, while the cat is dead,
while the bier-grass withers,
while death --- is our servant,
kiss by the emptiness
where flowers haven't broken through yet,
because we love each other.

katerina.title: BIRDS FALL OUTSIDE THE WINDOWS
katerina.text:
birds fall outside the windows,
but they think they're flying,
like soaked autumns,
like a handful of kittens.
the bird-like turned rabbit-like,
painted feathers into fur,
and then the winds playfully
toss the birds upward,
and sensing their former strength,
gaining altitude,
newly grown wings
spread in flight.

katerina.title: AS IF I'M GUARDING TIME
katerina.text:
as if I'm guarding time,
I tremble through streets, wander
in circles of courtyard garages.
and time? it already
fluttered with the wind out of the gate,
slid upward,
dropping a feather
into the cold meaningless sky,
dimly murky like ice
before winter,
ice that will not melt.
a five-story block looks like a nanny
at a Mowgli lost between
the liquor department and bread.
and if I must search,
then for hope,
at least for that.
your happiness is far beyond me.
I peer at the suits of little leaves,
but don't recognize my forest ones.
hello, I shout, hello, I whisper, hello,
and linden yellows on the ice.
one more little step and I'll find it, find it.

katerina.title: TOWARD EVENING, INVISIBLE DOG DREAMS
katerina.text:
Toward evening, invisible dog dreams
float around the room,
small talk meaning nothing
thickens into “remember when?”

A candle burns and reflects
in pupils widened by Shiraz.
A drunken crab-like Friday
pulls metastases into Saturday.

And something between a child's tear
on skin red from anxiety,
and a fragrant drop of wax, and
my own uncried thing --- too.

And the gaze slides, sorting through
objects, names, visions.
Words and voice stay mermaid-silent,
while movements speak:

involuntary movements of lashes and muscles,
clenching the teeth harder.
And the crust of indifference cracked ---
living tenderness! But where

did it come from? It died long ago.
The kaleidoscope aligned differently...
Happy and foolish,
unseen dog dreams wander on.

katerina.title: SNOW IS FALLING, AN ADMIRAL'S BEARING
katerina.text:
snow is falling, an admiral's bearing.
it's winter saying goodbye as it dies
in March slush as if in luxury.
snow falls, unhurried --- it's slippery after all.
asking nothing, knowing nothing,
I catch a snowflake. it is the last one.

kris.title: FIRST GRADE
kris.text:
first grade
Nikita and Stas
fight for a long time over
which one of them I'm the wife of
and then
I grow up alone
no time for tears here ---
only gratitude
I was neither obedience
nor mediocrity
I climbed trees
carried backpacks, not handbags
maybe it's all because nobody asked for my hand
still, first grade ---
what if I'd given in
and the limit of my dreams
would have become a wedding waltz
I would have learned to keep quiet and nod
for the sake of that wedding
very lucky that the boys back then
were occupied by the first shop class lesson in time

kris.title: THEY WANT FROM ME
kris.text:
they want from me:
a smile, a flying step,
piloting an airship,
ADHD-style editing,
children
(a wish from strangers),
to manage to keep spinning,
not to wander around after dark,
to be quieter, to be modest,
to be experienced in bed
(another wish from strangers),
not to stick my nose everywhere, not to speak without being asked,
to grow my braids back immediately.
I swallow bitter beer,
play songs and cry a lot
over a good film
or a book about happiness or war.
if you have advice
on how one should live differently,
don't give it to me.

kris.title: ROLL A SHADOW ACROSS THE HEART
kris.text:
Roll a shadow across the heart
Across the face --- a smirk
Tomorrow there will be a new day
I should fix the shelf
What do you sense in the dark
With the back of your head gone cold?
I should pick up in the room
The crumpled T-shirt
Here's one boom, here's another
Here's the prickly smoke
We'll go along the edge of the ditch
To feed the cats
If you lie without moving
It probably won't get better
I'll rehang the shelf, pick up the T-shirt
Feed the kittens, watch the sunset
All more useful than the poison
Of lying emptiness

kris.title: AROUND AND EVERYTHING AT ONCE, AND NOTHING
kris.text:
around and everything at once, and nothing
and for so long that the speech skill
built up over other years goes deaf
and the sun over Moscow has fallen sideways
and smeared shadows through the corridors
balconies, like tiny boats ---
that's how clouds covered the high-rises
of which there is an endless number
and all of them are rowing God knows where
my temples hum, the wires chirr
and I'm stuck in the middle of July
and it is such a slow bullet
in idiotic cartoon slow-mo ---
you keep waiting for it to explode
and still it doesn't. the sun froze above.
not summer, just some kind of shit.

kris.title: I WAS ALMOST ASLEEP AND THEN CLICK AGAIN
kris.text:
I was almost asleep and then click again
an unfastened rib hook
I have to look out the window at the trams
the trams go ding and the heart goes ding with them
and it's summer, and what dreams there are in summer
be glad, look at that, you're alive
and the wind tastes carbonated
and by the water the dew pearls the slope
as though nothing were booming half a meter away
and it's quiet, as though everyone exhaled
and I with them, up to the crown of my head in dew
to the very bottom of my lungs in wind

kris.title: THE DOWNPOUR IS QUIETER. AND YOU CAN HEAR CLEARLY
kris.text:
The downpour is quieter. And you can hear clearly
How in the alleys --- one-two-three, one-two-three --- a waltz.
I freeze like a cat on a smooth roof,
A little closer to the sky --- one-two-three, one-two-three --- to you.
Cats run silently through the cold square,
Only their --- one-two-three, one-two-three --- pulse gives them away.
Don't lock the big doors in fear:
I'm only --- one-two-three, one-two-three --- a dream you dream.

kris.title: THEY SAY TO LIVE WITHOUT LETTING GO OF EACH OTHER'S HANDS
kris.text:
They say to live without letting go of each other's hands
And it sounds almost like a friend
But we didn't let go of our hands around each other's throats
And boasted --- look, I'm breathing
And the noise in our ears --- it was the usual noise
We saw no trouble, laughed proudly
But I remember the first time as if it were yesterday
I say, this isn't a game
And you keep squeezing my wrist, as if joking
And maybe not. What kind of friends are we?
And I said quietly: you can't do this
And then you didn't, but the horror remained
I remember how you wanted to hit
And I wanted to love, neither was enough for us
What a pity you didn't break my arm
At least I'd be angry, but this way it's barely there
And only words keep building up in my throat
And I can no longer spit them onto the gym floor
One-two-one-two
See, I said it
Jump-hit-see I
One-two

kris.title: HIDDEN IN THE DOORWAY
kris.text:
hidden in the doorway
say whatever you want, however much you want
going is no joy at all, as though
I'm wearing shoes one size too small
and the wind reaches out tentacles like an octopus
leave the comfort --- it'll drag you across the yard
just imagine it and you'll put down roots
into the doormat pressed against your leg
Moscow spring is such a bitch
what if the stupid leaves freeze ---
they came out in this bitter cold...
why are you looking into my eyes like a book
can I just not go anywhere?
and you answer laughing, “yes”

kris.title: AN ACQUAINTANCE GENTLY REMINDS ME
kris.text:
an acquaintance gently reminds me:
joke more quietly, what if someone hears the joke
some idle uncle, somebody's drunk stepfather
it only makes me joke louder
and afterward I dream of my mother
sitting on the corner of the bed, dead
and how can I fear those who are stupid and rough
when even a pale corpse isn't frightening
staring disappointedly into the dark
I wait for dawn, pretending to sleep
and arrange the letters the wrong way
sliding along the silly little edge

kris.title: SOMETHING GOES DING, AN APRIL TUNING FORK
kris.text:
Something goes ding, an April tuning fork
Probably worth retuning the plans
The metro will lick me up with its enormous mouth
And fling open its squinting lamps
Run, run, strange beasts,
The bored guard whistles under his breath
But as for my heart being stolen,
Did anyone even look for it? Yeah, right, same old story

kris.title: LIKE ANY DAY THAT STARTED FROM THE END
kris.text:
Like any day that started from the end,
Insomnia devours Sunday.
Go on, frighten the general merriment
With the ambiguous pallor of your face.
Where were you going? To hide along the way,
To turn the world inside out with dreams:
To interpret every possible sign
That might happen at all,
To teach yourself not to cry over things
That are bound to happen ---
Here is a cloud. Here is snow. Here is change.
Your city waits, having promised spring,
For you to return, meek and simple,
Softened with age like grandmother's yarn ---
And for a long time it looks for what is missing
In the empty hands of trains.

kris.title: THIS COLD INSIDE --- NOT BECAUSE IT'S WINTER
kris.text:
this cold inside --- not because it's winter
it's just that fears are building houses in me again
chilling out the echoing foundations for them
and that's why my legs are ice and my palms are ice
and the thermometer lies and the mirror lies too
and hope has the shape of a hot bath
you won't get me, bastards, what else did you expect
there's a gray little wolf growling beside me
clawed demons are dozing in my arms
and my eyes have gone dark --- that's not forever
there are snowdrifts now --- there will be water again
where there are ruins now --- rain will kiss the earth
and spill into the eyes, wash out the bruises
the heavy whale-fish will lead with its fins
shake the occupying little town from its spine
there are things that won't heal even in April
only the mirror lies, and the thermometer lies too
everything is moving toward spring
toward spring, how else could it be

kris.title: ON THE WASTELAND, WORMWOOD PLUS DARKNESS
kris.text:
on the wasteland, wormwood plus darkness
stare wide-eyed, cut corners
fatigue blossoms in the body
as bitter as wormwood
you run, shuffling books in bags,
somewhere where no one is ---
but twilight will catch you anyway
and its angry inhabitants
you keep breathing out of curiosity
until they tell you “don't breathe”
and the wind tastes of iron
and lies that there isn't a soul nearby
wormwood sways beneath the sun
despair burns in the chest
and not a fucking thing will work itself out
and I love you, damn it

kris.title: I'M THIRTY-SIX. MY BROTHER DOESN'T LOVE ME
kris.text:
I'm thirty-six. My brother doesn't love me.
I took off the ring --- I wore it for so long.
I'm selling my camera
To spite the way everyone around me is beautiful.
I say:
--- Everyone around me is beautiful!
And I'm not lying. I'm wildly in love with everything.
How wonderful --- one day I will die,
And beauty will remain, just look.

kris.title: A COLD DAY, ALMOST BURNT OUT
kris.text:
A cold day, already almost burnt out,
Shaken from the shining digit on the clock,
I'm drinking in the kitchen with the white queen
And she has pulsars in her hair.
I feel the Neglinka swelling red
And stirring, full, ---
But we speak quietly about different things
And the war seems one drop farther away,
And the storm beneath my rib almost subsides,
And fingers stroke the cat's sides,
And handsome Yuri can be seen from the window ---
And he even smiles a little.

kris.title: LOOKING INTO THE ABYSSES OF WORK
kris.text:
looking into the abysses of work
into a pocket's mouth, the bottom of a heart
come on, come on, what's stopping you
tell me everything is shit
that under the white snow --- a puddle
women are monsters, marriage is prison
and it won't even get worse:
the same darkness
you'll yell at the door, the kettle
the courier, VK
and again it won't feel better
only make you angrier for sure
and outside --- the ringing of trams
the pain of farewells, somebody's laughter
go on and have a proper cry already
and forgive yourself and everyone

kris.title: I SMELL OF INCENSE
kris.text:
I smell of incense.
my witch friend
gave me a potion. it usually costs
crazy money, I just got lucky.
people use it to change their fate,
find a wealthy match, raise their status,
bewitch a handsome man, become a queen,
curse someone, hide somebody's tracks.
I just like the way it smells.
a day ago
I get into a taxi --- and the driver smiles:
--- you went to church today!
I laugh
and shake my head:
--- I just like the way it smells.
and then
all the way to the station
we ride in silence.

kris.title: MAKE A PISTOL WITH YOUR FINGERS
kris.text:
Make a pistol with your fingers,
Make it and aim
At November, long as a hundred years,
At the dreary Celsius.
At empty sticky eyes
And the whistle from a car.
At that sickening “you can't”
Take aim as well.
And the carousel will start to spin
Of every kind of trash,
And there'll be enough of a shot for everyone,
And the shot will thunder.
And the guitar pick will spark,
Pinched between the fingers.
And then? Then one-two-three.
Something like a waltz.

kris.title: I REALLY WANT IT TO SMELL LIKE MAY AGAIN
kris.text:
I really want it to smell like May again:
An overcrowded city thirsting for revolutions,
Black bread, sunflower oil in a deep saucer,
A clean new album, a jolting big tram,
Grated apple, clouds twisting into spirals,
Someone's warm nape, a scrap of paper in a cat's paws.
I really want them to finally stop lying to us ---
It terribly spoils the magical smell of spring.

kris.title: HERE IS THE HOUSE. OLD SMITH BUILT IT
kris.text:
Here is the house. Old Smith built it.
Now he is sick in mind and sick with flu.
And having forgotten that he used to be angry,
He only breathes the air out with a wheeze
And gathers broken props.
Here is Smith's dog. It has been dead for five years,
Buried by the garages. But the gray ghost
Lies down at his feet, refracting light,
And waits for a hand, commands and barberry candies,
Chases rats and guards the meal.
Here are windows in a web of emptiness,
A bridge over the river, stairways, paintings.
Here Smith, captive to sweet drowsiness,
Watches reflections cool in puddles.
And to the dog's ghost, as if to a son,
He whispers not to fear the dark.

kris.title: I WANT LONG, LONG
kris.text:
I want long, long
long fingernails
to cut through the viscous darkness with them
to pry open with them the valve
of hardened chicken hearts
of armchair warriors
the edge of foundation that over the years
has grown mortally into the skin
I want something to gasp
and start beating under them
but I can't because of the strings.
so there's no need to be afraid of me

kris.title: I DREAMED A DREAM: THEY DON'T TURN ON THE LIGHTS THERE
kris.text:
I dreamed a dream: they don't turn on the lights there
And put out the lamps by the entrance to the house.
Writers with stern shoulders
Are met beside rusted cars,
Savoring endless filterless cigarettes.
And vials of medicine smell of poison,
And the stiletto heel squeals in surprise
On the shoes of sculptures coming alive.
Look there: in the kitchen, sitting cross-legged,
A memorable Jew has settled into the corner.
And Lermontov is almost Lensky now
With his famous pallor.
No snow, inhospitable and chilly.
In the hallway, taking off their shoes one by one,
Drowned women pull off their hats
And hand out cheap wine.
As a condition of mocking chic,
Driving the age of holograms mad,
A typewriter bangs,
A sacred mountain appears in visions.
Cry out among the shadows of your shrine,
Try to gather scraps of phrases...
But the dead disdain the living
And notice them only every other time.
The teapot hums with iron sides
And remembers a gaze for a long time --- in the stream of faces,
Smiling, Nabokov is talking
With one of the young suicides.

kris.title: THE TRAVELING CIRCUS DOZES
kris.text:
the traveling circus dozes.
the houses sleep in their places.
a train to the back of beyond.
pills for going fucking crazy.
books about nonsense.
films full of horror.
where are we really...
well, here we are:
“chanson” snores
in the bellies of empty taxis,
the pain of our youth
is dreaming its tenth dream,
a thunderstorm sleeps in the clouds,
warmth dozes in the cat.
only my eyes
glow in the dark.

kris.title: OCTOBER, AND WATER, AND THE SCRATCH OF A MATCH
kris.text:
October, and water, and the scratch of a match
the houses stand with their bricks puffed up
kilometers fly up from under the wheels
and everyone grumbles about gloom and acute respiratory infections
but the train driver stopped the train
and is glad to be back, smoking into the wind
and in the clouds, familiar things: cats
hearts, that familiar symbol from above
a cheerful little god lets them loose and laughs
and we're quite alive, even with the flu
and the whole city is like a kind old music video
for a song that turned out to be “very”

kris.title: IN THE TRAUMATOLOGIST'S OFFICE
kris.text:
in the traumatologist's office
they put me back together piece by piece
I'm generally a klutz ---
always forgetting myself somewhere: a leg, an arm
I'll tear off a piece of my heart and leave it with a friend
I cut off my long hair too and gave it away
it seems even my own skin is too small for me
I want to crawl out of it
become myself, only taller and a little stronger
too bad my traumatologist doesn't treat that at all
he only gave me something for the heart, like a corset
nodded with satisfaction:
--- they broke you but didn't break you
but this
put this on and take it off less often from now on
how long am I supposed to keep stitching you up
and led me by the elbow
out into the corridor, where the lamps softly clink
I stand there fiddling with the laces
so I can take it off an hour later, courier it back here
and remain with my heart showing through my chest

kris.title: WITH A COBWEB, LIKE A THIN TRANSPARENT BANDAGE
kris.text:
With a cobweb, like a thin transparent bandage,
The stairwell flight is bound
No one smokes on the concrete balconies
And no one lives in the apartments
A birch has leaned over and its shadow froze
The yard belongs to no one and is loved by no one
And like a tiny airplane
A snow-white seagull hangs above it
Windows slam loudly to the delight of the winds
Glass scatters with a ring
And the teardrops of shards glitter in the mornings
And in the evenings too, if there is light
Look into these windows as if into eyes
So that, holding your breath, you can read in them
Something important that lived years ago
And leave, leaving everything as it is

kris.title: HOW SERGEY YEROFEICH FROM THE FIFTH FLOOR
kris.text:
how Sergey Yerofeich from the fifth floor
invented himself a daughter from a river pearl
started rocking her, saying:
--- now --- it's night
in the sky --- the Dipper. and milk runs from that Dipper
and under every floorboard there are five mice
and every mouse has a pair of funny ears
and the youngest mouse twitches an ear in surprise
why, she says, is everyone asleep --- only you aren't sleeping?
how in the morning Sergey Yerofeich gave away what was his
whatever he had, for a cradle for his daughter and some linen
bought some porridge, bought some more milk
everyone agreed: the old man's head isn't right
but as soon as the moon-ball rolls down from the clouds
from behind the windows --- every now and then, a child's cry can be heard
Yerofeich rocks her, and his shoulders are proud
and both their eyes are the color of river water

kris.title: THE GREAT NIGHT NODS ITS HEAD
kris.text:
the great night nods its head
some get to doze, some sit up like owls
counting losses, rejoicing that they're smaller

the pale lamps' stubs smoke in the pupils
toward morning you can hear the hop of furry paws
and the ghosts of women looking through the window

squeeze your temples, freeze over the table
blind mirrors breathe from the walls
and film photographs laugh out loud

back then we held hands, but now
lie face down, your belly ripped open
stroke it as if it were some poor creature

catch a tear, hang it from a star
one day you'll get used to being everywhere
treasure the fragments of memory and sound

insomnia will pass, but trust the temple
prophetically humming before the throw
ballistics is a stubborn science

kris.title: YOU HEARD THE RINGING, DIDN'T YOU?
kris.text:
you heard the ringing, didn't you?
that's in my chest
little stones, broken pieces of glass
copper pennies spilling from my shirt
hold out both palms, come closer
take this, otherwise
they'll bind it with a bandage
a thin vein, a feeble little spring
lie down and stay there, God's mistake
they'll say afterward
but that's not what I'm telling them
I'm saying: I really don't mind at all
here, take it, you know where to press
nice souvenirs for loved ones to remember me by
the little sun looks on, sinking very, very low
while from inside, stubbornly, against all odds
little poems lash out, dog-earing their corners
ugly little sad demons
what else could come out of me

kris.title: I CARRY A CATCHER OF EARTHLY BEAUTY WITH ME
kris.text:
I carry a catcher of earthly beauty with me
but use it less and less, as though beauty were foreign to me
my dear passerby, I probably won't find out who you are
and why, if everyone leaves --- and you leave too
today I am not sight, only coolness and hearing
only the smell of rain --- that's enough of everything else, please
October is dying, and the crowd of its gloomy servants
(myself among them) silently keeps watch by the black bed

kris.title: A SIMPLE SHOT: IT'S COLD. I'M WALKING
kris.text:
a simple shot: it's cold. I'm walking.
high-rises climb into the dark,
the asphalt has furrowed its painted folds.
all around, they stubbornly lie that everything is fine.
and the air smells of coming winter,
anyone who's not a fool hurries home.
almost no stars can be seen, only headlights.
God bless the effects of pharmaceuticals ---
October spares me a little, though it might not.
here's a table, here's a reflection in the window.
how good that they exist, and coffee,
the warmth of the café, the waitress's profile,
and news not only about the war.

kris.title: IF YOU PAY NO ATTENTION AT ALL
kris.text:
if you pay no attention at all
to the color of the clouds or patches of daylight
splashed through branches onto the ground in the park
then what can have any meaning at all
texts made up of landscapes
aren't valued much if they're contemporary
that sort of thing is forgiven only in dead classics
everyone needs a human story
here is my human story
for a very long time I couldn't see anything at all
my eyes swelled up, got filled with all kinds of filth
and ash the wind brought, and sand
now little by little all that crap has been cried out
here is my human story
I listen to my step, I see the sky and leaves
and funny apartment blocks, pink as fruit paste
and if they tell me I need to watch my step
and nowhere else at all, and walk more carefully
there are still eye drops at the bottom of my backpack
and I don't mind sharing them at all

kris.title: WHO COULD I PAY TO MAKE IT EASIER
kris.text:
Who could I pay to make it easier
What a pity they frightened us with Satan for nothing
I want to wake up drunk in a cheburek café
And let Maksim laugh at me
The poor souls stretched out their necks
Taking full-face photos for a magazine on a phone
Bakhyt Shukurullayevich Kenzheyev
In a dream toward morning shared a beer with me
Bring me back, vinyl record,
Enchanting the hoarse yawning run
Where Herzen got his boots polished
And tore toward you with impunity
Scold me, frighten me with cheap vodka
Hammer ink into a crooked tattoo
Anything is better than, with a dancing gait,
Walking now into the great emptiness

kris.title: IN A COUPLE --- A COUPLE OF DECADES
kris.text:
in a couple --- a couple of decades
having decomposed into letters, steam, and a little grave trace
I'll disappear, as everyone will disappear --- that's how it goes
amid prisons, denunciations, hatred, coffins
there is so pitifully little time for love
make it in time, love, I beg you, choose love
every moment the remnants of the body still allow

alena.title: TO ESCAPE THE LAND OF RENTED APARTMENTS,
alena.text:
to escape the land of rented apartments,
trading cigarettes for campfire smoke.
we lie in the snow, already undressed,
and a seraph cooks porridge over the fire.
snow has clung to his broad wings,
like mittens, they have grown heavy
and stretched downward, to the foot of the spruce,
but his gaze is fixed on the heavens.
with a sleepless, tender longing for home
and an aluminum ladle in his hands,
he understood that he was already failing,
and there was no hope of returning to that blue again.
blowing on the porridge so as not to burn his tongue,
he tasted it, and his eyelashes closed:
the trap-paws of the northern capital
grabbed poor wretches into their embrace like that.
and we are among them, undressed in the snow,
on the endless white field,
and touring performers no longer cut us in ---
now our life is on the Neva bank.
first cold, cold, then heat,
such heat that its force melts bones.
we tear our clothes off on the platform,
taking off the inconvenient scalp at the same time.
falling from the sky, white ash
will settle and melt on the lips.
we are in a cradle in the seven winds,
and here even God won't notice us.
only the seraph, his wing sagging to the ground,
burns his palms on a dented pot.
here the sky is a solid blue ceiling
that casts a glance at the thin meadow,
where we lie
beneath a cross that was never put up...

alena.title: THE INEVITABILITY OF CRUCIFIXION HIDES IN THE WRISTS ---
alena.text:
the inevitability of crucifixion hides in the wrists ---
so crucify me already, for fuck's sake!
hands --- with self-tapping screws to the “main road”,
legs --- to a post with a nylon cable tie,
on my head --- a crown of wires,
beneath the pseudo-cross --- artificial flowers.
having left my eyes in a glass-and-rebar sky,
I spread like mold over bread ---
for your good luck and to spite the city,
turning on my dreary music
and fertilizing the starving bottom
until they take me down at dawn.

alena.title: THE SPINELESSNESS OF A WINDING STREET IN A SOUTHERN CITY
alena.text:
the spinelessness of a winding street in a southern city
flowed into multi-stranded ribbons of aluminum.
the belly of the snotty-jellyfish sea is tenderly slit open ---
through its torn reflections, shore, look at me,
distorted in a mirror with crumbs of sand along the bottom,
reflected in the shifting waves of air.
as if paying tribute to quiet, formidable Chronos,
throw me pieces of glass colored with sun-juice.
embrace me with burning, crumbling paws,
strike my nostrils with the smell of fish and sweetness,
run onto your wet brother in yellow cliffs,
stick out your breast-like slopes at crooked angles.
I will draw myself into this mass as a triceratops skeleton
and freeze as a piece of amalgam in the hole of the bay,
king of mud-crabs (from the creation of Steve Jobs?) ---
an unmarked quest on the map of gray-haired Skyrim.
this land will remember my gray-burnt hair
and ink in the layers of a chilled, pale torso.
I will bring back from it pale stripes on my skin
and cheap knockoff Air Forces that are too small,
and also a couple of photo-booth pictures as keepsakes,
a white hotel soap remnant gone translucent against the light,
several days spent without sleep or rest,
sea water imprisoned in glass bottles,
and poems. and a picture of how I stand
like Vladimir Vysotsky in Moscow on Strastnoy Boulevard,
while water and sand embrace my skin ---
and then I wake up. in Petersburg. crucified by May.

alena.title: WE COME FROM MUNICIPAL COMPETITIONS
alena.text:
we come from municipal competitions
with cardboard crowns on our foreheads,
residents of a threshold topos and chronos,
mired in everyday affairs.
the dog of daily life gnaws out the heart,
a worm made of alcohol will turn the liver to dust.
we are torn into scraps like towels,
we sag like trousers at the crotch.
we are unsightly, with sandpaper faces,
we smell of Nevsky cucumber cream
and mothballs, apple gum,
and something warm --- the way home smells.
in the exhausted blue beneath the eyes,
in the iron grip of hardened hands,
confessions hide in silence
and a fierce heartbeat close to rupture.
all problems will stick like garlic skins
to damp blackened fingers.
death in a communal apartment by choking on shawarma
you would choose over hotel guests,
and let them suffer, let them hurt,
let them bite from inside into the essence
of their own piss-soaked morality:
“wherever you may be, be human.”
but afterward you'll sit down by the hearth,
bury your face in someone's chest (you wanted your mother's),
lower your eyes, fall asleep, and in the morning,
cursing the suffocating summer heat,
go back to the same old things.

alena.title: I WANTED TO SLIT MYSELF OPEN, BUT JESUS WOULDN'T LET ME;
alena.text:
I wanted to slit myself open, but Jesus wouldn't let me;
I chased vodka with ibuprofen,
lay down on the couch and thought: I'll ascend
to the angels, somewhere like a bullet into the sky.
and then a pistol shot rang out,
my hopeful gaze fixed on the ceiling,
but I fell; the bullet's song was over,
it crumbled into somebody's temple,
while I flew, flew toward the floor, I am a casing,
a spent empty cartridge.
above my head is somebody's funeral feast,
and I lie alone, dust on every side,
in the darkness beneath the couch,
in contact with an expensive Persian carpet.
I am a casing, a casing, deprived from birth
of fate and treachery by the machine that fathered me!
I am a wordless hypocrite-witness,
I am a useless man-made element,
a savior of necks from bruises and nooses,
or rather their lawful issuer.
I opened my eyes. my pulse thundered in my ears
like bombs somewhere in nearby countries.
I am a casing, a casing, a piece of rebar in trousers,
whose life and death merged into existence
under the couch.

alena.title: LIKE A BEGGAR ON SENNAYA WITH AN OUTSTRETCHED STUMP,
alena.text:
like a beggar on Sennaya with an outstretched stump,
I raise my gaze to the golden dome.
the Lord will guffaw mercilessly through a rusty horn ---
it seems he is laughing at me,
at the meagerness of my fragmentary judgments
and at the maximalism of youth.
my flag is a torn, faded blanket,
patched with pieces of dreams,
and I'll wrap myself in it like a shroud
to hide from prickly eyes.
and if he exists, then for some reason he created us,
and afterward betrayed us, but didn't cry at all.
Judas's sin is not as terrible as his:
he traded us for posthumous nirvana,
but his lack of love, like a bleeding wound,
cuts the heart open with branches of the metro.
my flag slips from my eyes as though someone pulls it
by its decrepit, crumbling edge.
and I hope I will see my panel-block paradise,
which despises every society reception,
where warm yellow light from the windows
caresses the blue of the snow with its reflection,
where that same one lets people under his roof
without lies, self-interest, or implication.
somewhere in Khrushchev-era kitchens
fingers give birth to echoes of a guitar,
someone there will mock all anthems and fanfares
and jump until the floor collapses.
and there is a corner where God hides
in a cracked, oxidized icon setting,
and it is clear what life was conceived for,
and that he too would like to live, but couldn't.
but the glow only burns brighter,
the light burns out my naive gaze;
I am destined to return to the cage of the Ring Road,
where it is like hell, only hotter.
and the golden dome, mocking me,
stares after me for a long, stubborn time.
oh, darling, there is no God here at all,
I swear to it, and even repent.
my city devours you, me, and our dreams,
my city does not accept silence,
and the whisper of the sky in the corners of the Neva
will be drowned out by the smell of exhaust and sulfur.
we remain here to live with a rudiment of faith,
hiding our eyes behind steel scleras
with handouts from bastard fate.

alena.title: THE COUNTLESS SPACES BEYOND THE RING ROAD
alena.text:
the countless spaces beyond the Ring Road
are covered with hail in July.
welcome to the abode of puritanism,
countless pagan rites,
petty-bourgeois consciousness and daily life,
simple words, not ornate ones.
we have all settled tightly around the trough
nailed to the shelter of the shores,
and we look into it, searching for truth,
of which we criminally get too little
under conditions of uneven terrain
and extremely left-right views.
what is the zombie box broadcasting to us today?
whose faces does it spray into pixels?
someone there ends up in Kashchenko not by accident,
but surely our host couldn't be mistaken?
someone's house is burning there, and the flame
smokes up the sky as if tempering steel.
there, by the Boris and Gleb monastery,
an old sexton reads the Psalter.
there the learned cat plays chess,
there schoolchildren rape dogs.
there snow fell on the pines and does not melt,
someone died there --- no fucking point in botching the ink.
you reach for the remote. switch it off.
silence hangs in the apartment.
without truth you won't last long, fuck,
and there's no fucking way you'll ride out the withdrawal,
but the supplies aren't being replenished ---
the old women scraped everything from the bins,
divers pulled every pearl from the bottom,
shamans enchanted a talisman,
but what's the use? there's nothing to catch
while everything immutable smolders.
and we stayed here to love or jerk off,
pressed against an old dusty radiator.
and breathing Moscow's stuffy air through the screen,
we dream of good news,
read manuscripts of old GOST standards,
giving ourselves over to nostalgia on social networks.
the trough will crack and sink,
although, you'd think, a log doesn't sink.
the space beyond the Ring Road quietly moans,
a face cracks into a smile, cutting the silence,
and under the rib longing will whine or howl like a dog.
sit there bored. and wait for your
spring.

alena.title: LIE DOWN WITH ME IN MY COLD BED
alena.text:
lie down with me in my cold bed
with a bloody stain from a razor cut.
let my leg rest on your thigh ---
the cut hurts, heal it with a prayer,
stroke my skin the way a seasoned warrior
lovingly strokes his medals with his fingers.
kiss me “not on the lips, but on the mouth,”
kiss me until I cough and scream with pain,
and then heal me again with your hands,
slide along the threads of nerve endings,
warm my ribs with your warm sides
and avoid words of farewell like typhus.
when you leave, don't lock the door,
and then come back silently,
shake out, wash, and make my bed with me,
nuzzling your nose into my palm like a wolf.
the half-dark wraps us softly,
an amber light disperses it
like from a campfire, but it's still somehow disgusting
that we exist on only one of all the planets,
that on Pluto there are no one's beds
and that on TOI-700 e there will be no night,
and that on Mars there is no one to cherish,
that no one on exoplanets is writhing.
but we exist, so let's
talk until our throats are hoarse;
whoever stops first --- chain them up in the shed,
so please, don't go deaf.
throw the phone from the fifteenth floor,
let it fly into the wrecked asphalt,
then Charon can wait for us a hundred years,
we won't be sent to the damned Buchenwald,
won't be sprayed into atoms for every extra breath,
won't say the words, if on your knees
I survive every storm and the last Croc,
all the crises of future generations.
come on, my universal and cramped love,
deconstruct yourself while holding hands with me.
we will flare up, tearing through the earth's cover,
killing the whole phenomenon of boredom at the root.
and that means none of this is in vain,
and that means even if the sun suddenly goes out
we'll pull it from November's belly
and set it on fire at the bottom of a sacred well.
lie down with me in my cold bed.
it smells of juniper and mint there,
now it smells of you too.
I send fate to play the fool
with a marked card.

alena.title: WAKE UP IN A LONELY APARTMENT
alena.text:
wake up in a lonely apartment
feel like somebody else
in this enormous world
you are surely someone's sworn brother
in cracked old boots
in white socks with hearts
in service records never served to the end
with your buckshot grown into the flesh
you come into this world alone
from your mother's womb
surrounded by white featherbeds
with the outlines of shafts
in your low drafty window
with lipsticks in a cigarette case
you see the world in tomorrow's day
in a stash of rusty steel
you'll break your first ten
like five thousand at a broken cash register
from other people's generous bribes
you need to get a transponder for the highway
a Zhiguli with no power steering
so the wheel turns hard
an expensive but poor viewer
in salt-stained, trampled Uggs
instant euphoria
from changes in life
trips through the Russian world
straight up to the funeral feast
blue Baltic pines
the golden gut of the gulf
Kuban grape clusters
and a bottle of pale beer
so that when you yourself wake up
in your strangely familiar apartment
you would turn to the heavens
the heavens of subpolar Palmyra
buy a ticket for the nearest open sleeper carriage
definitely for berth thirty-three
watch the sunset on the move
erupting in your native speech
there's no need to go anywhere
or maybe there is, but later
the reflection of a tired gaze
on a walk alone at night
and unclear new images
form a kaleidoscope
it's unusual when you're apart
but at the same time there is a little icon
into the quiet hum of your consciousness
someone else's song seeps
a song of your torment
a song from childhood itself
and when you suddenly come to
in the middle of a lonely apartment
give me your word, my dear friend,
to draw the curtains open forever

alena.title: IMAGINE YOURSELF A CAREER WOMAN, SLEEP FOUR HOURS,
alena.text:
imagine yourself a career woman, sleep four hours,
work 7/0 for a better standard of living ---
accidentally mix up the poles,
crawl between puddles like a slug.
the city is stuck in anticipation of something awful,
metro trains freeze between stations.
you choose your move --- either the cross (Krestovsky), or cross yourself after all,
anything to tumble out of the carriage or out of the stupor.
Kamennoostrovsky is habitually eternal,
the TV tower still stabs God with its bayonet.
better to count clouds or sheep
in an empty Petrograd underground passage?
you can't find gum in your bag, or even yourself,
rummaging fruitlessly through a ton of your own things.
what if a pawn eats its own queen ---
would that be the most ridiculous of deaths?
the trolleybus shakes as if after a stroke,
the left half of its body has failed.
the passengers --- founders of a seated cult,
or a prison one after all?
pass the fare in ringing copper,
spread across checked fabric,
or a cage, or get whipped after all?
to be pursued by packs of Russian Style
or by graphomania after all?
and it is as if I am not me
and the city is no longer a city
and the path has collapsed into a point
and the rain, pity it isn't snow
and transport now goes nowhere
stop: “Bolshoy Prospekt”
(Petrograd Side)

alena.title: FORGIVE YOURSELF
alena.text:
forgive yourself
forgive forgive forgive
the alarm bell of words drowns out the sounds
you pulled it taut and now you're cutting the thread again
whether for a reason or just from boredom
along the little thread you run, cardboard you
sliding on cardboard legs
away from cardboard, not-picture-perfect emptiness
polygamy is stepping on your heels
and the thread dodges your feet
the tension instantly weakens
something distant whistles straight into the gentle lure
while the cardboard hand, exhausted,
with its last strength grabs the thread
so nimble that, truly, it's frightening
to fall in one moment like a stone into an abyss
but does it really matter that much
when guilt and fear gnaw at you
when you hear their thick wheezing
when the only light looms in your eyes
when there is a path to leave the archetypes
to break the taut chain of wild events
sticking your head out of the whirlpool
breaking the boards of every template and floor
shaking from adrenaline or cold
but the thread doesn't give a damn about all hopes
or some imagined dim light
between it and you, present and former,
there are no dealings or agreements at all
the final symphony of fibers
sounds like a dying swan
you cut it --- let it be a lesson
don't bury something with your own hands
everything instantly falls onto its glass shelves
everything is clear as a baby's first cry
forgive yourself
forgive, and no longer be afraid
open your palm, fall into nothing and at last
get warm

alena.title: I BLOOM AS THE NEPRYADVA
alena.text:
I bloom as the Nepryadva
a bloody river stain
a steel, white-hot harvest
beneath a broken polar window
the sky bleeds aurora
houses bare their roofs like teeth
one spark more of me in you
to crawl to you over glaciers
in pieces of aluminum
covered with insulation
just love me
under the howl of thunderous inflation
just hold me with your fingers
while the night cuts me
crucify me with bone embroidery hoops
as though I were a subscript sign
burnt caramel hardens
into an ugly copy of a human being
trams travel to the capital
and have done so for a quarter century now
to be a dot on Google Maps
a suitcase with a set of limbs
before the final collapse
I'll tear you away from eternity
while your bone hoops
prick between my ribs
I'll pack you into a backpack
don't cry in there, don't twitch
my sweet girl
you shouldn't be afraid
pagan prayers
you were born lucky
though naked would have been better
because you're much more beautiful
than a simple soup set
only terribly arrogant
the collector will light like a match
an elevator is not a lift
we're unlikely to meet anyone
if anything, I'll wall you up in Dzift
the stars spit fragments
of HE grenades from CS:GO
licked over by misinterpretations
but still with you
frayed all the way to the roadside
of a country road to the CHP plant
marked by everyone else
as a dilettante and fool
I'll do anything for you
even if you don't believe me
raise your hands, we're in the sights
at a depth of two hundred thousand leagues
paired parallels
set perpendicular
split, not whole
torn apart by the paws of larvae
when your old two-room apartment
becomes like a world for us
we'll dream of something bigger
once we get out of the apartments
just don't cry, my girl
I'm not your executioner
it's just that my faithful love
was never taught not to punish
take my hand without fear
don't waste time
and close your little eyes
it's time to sleep

alena.title: I WANT TO BE WRITTEN INTO YOUR INTERTEXT,
alena.text:
I want to be written into your intertext,
because I am useless in any other one.
a freight train will block the railway crossing,
whiskey with ice will rise like a lump in the throat.
the first January snow will caress you damply
and at once melt on the shell of your jacket.
the kings in this life are all made of paper,
among them I am a minute-boy.
take my undivided faith,
divide it in half, and once more --- quarter it,
dissect it for research purposes.
the stairwell is disgustingly smoky,
the bag has dislocated my shoulder,
and my shoulder blade, like a wing, has pressed against the whitewashed wall.
we play hot and cold,
you and I, and the fragments of the system.
you are so beautiful that I want to cry ---
I kiss your dirty hem.
you take off my bogatyr helmet and bast shoes ---
I keep silent at your mercy.
behind the neon of Ligovsky 50
you can't see the starry spits.
your house on the Pryazhka is somewhere near Kirovsky,
but it consists entirely of words.
and you smile at me with tenderness and pity,
softly stroke me with your hand
beside your height I am insignificantly small,
but at least alive in every sense.
I sink again beneath your knees,
there is tarpaulin leather on your feet again ---
my homeland smashes my face into the ground,
but kisses me with the gaze of Christ.

alena.title: MANIFESTO OF PLATONIC LOVE
alena.text:
the mutual permeation
of air and you,
Cuban independence
and a colon (and I)
instead of periods chopping sentences
the most important and intimate ones,
something like “where would you be without me”
or “I feel so damn good with you.”
the simplicity of words,
practically their discreteness,
degradation to the basics,
but the constancy
of the fact that time slows down
in your silent presence.
when our fingers finally intertwine,
I don't think about the percussion
beating an alarm bell in my head.
only somewhere around the center of the chest,
perhaps a little to the left,
a muttering of “wait”
as an attempt to stop the moment.
not to go to sleep, and
while lungs divide the air of one apartment,
one bed,
warm each other like a fakir's fire.
I am not bones, not muscles, not skin,
not eyeballs and not a waist,
it is not me who one day will be laid
in the earth somewhere beneath an epitaph.
I will live under the skin without a residence stamp,
draw a zigzag of tenderness on the bones,
send a network of roots into spinal discs,
replace anxiety and fear with myself.
I am everywhere, in every atom,
at every point
and I sound the same, like a heart-beat-ing
that very night,
when we hugged each
other in our sleep.
let the damned circle of life
unwind us into some nth spring,
I still steal
every movement of your left eyebrow,
your blind wandering in sleep,
a gaze catching ships
(or somebody else's bullets?
pines?
springs?
kisses?).
I get stuck like a shard in the liver
for good, freeze myself
into a sore throat, fly
into the lungs as smoke and remain.
remain.
remain.
a part
of you. with a lost connection
you occupy my
emptinesses,
sharpnesses,
banknotes,
boycotts,
days.
at least with the rustle of an anti-drug advertisement
amid the bustle of the city
in the most vicious rains
give me a hint,
where
are you?

alena.title: I WON'T ESCAPE THE LAND OF RENTED APARTMENTS
alena.text:
I won't escape the land of rented apartments
and I won't trade cigarettes for anything.
my two-winged seraph lies in bed,
his eyes closed by somebody else's hand.
trap-paws? who said that?
those paws are hundreds of times more tender
than the crooked fingers of southern cliffs,
the wrists of northern ice formations.
concrete is my friend. in it there is air --- for a moment,
and then suffocation begins.
emptiness is crowned not by silence but by a scream,
blows with all one's strength into an innocent pillow.
my autistic overload is a blind tremor,
my nervous breakdown has spilled into a Petersburg sunset,
and only the white night listens to my bullshit
and doesn't complain about the way I swear.
my city is gentle, the city is wild and frightening,
ready to pounce at any moment
so that I remain here a two-dimensional character
crumbled from its foundations.
and angels stopped flying here long ago,
there is no field to lie in,
snow here melts as soon as it falls,
and downpours will flood the Kupchino host
of high-rises and rotten industrial zones,
abandoned buildings with hollows of empty windows.
I've already been turned a hundred times into cardboard
and batches of aerated concrete blocks.
and where is the long-suffering cross that was never put up?
my Petersburg has long been marked with crosses,
it was smashed in two weeks, like Brest,
it failed the entrance exam.
there is no us, no longing --- there is no one to lie there.
only mortal cold remains,
but I hurry to sell it for a penny ---
nobody needs it, since it's no longer young.
days pass. I remain standing
under hail that crushes eye sockets.
I give up: lash me with your belt, my thief-city,
and keep appearing in my dreams every night.

alena.title: LET ME OUT INTO THE WORLD
alena.text:
let me out into the world
into freedom
to a rockers' crash pad
like a gadfly
rummaging under the city's skin
in its nasopharynx
take pictures
before I die of the cold
expensive?
well, everything is expensive these days,
yes, in money
in bruises
in voices
and not letters from the internet
every song has already been sung by someone
but that doesn't make you love dancing to other people's beats any less
fear
has healed into me so tightly
healed under skin
resembling
a shriveled accordion
so what if twenty is practically a year away?
clothes
knockoff, but nobody asks for an explanation
gray hair
or something has curled up in my hair
its fragments
school A's
what was that you said about Mossad?
when you get yourself into a mess
don't forget to sink lower
into the dirt underfoot
it's fucking better
when you knead it with your heels?
closer
and someone laughs over us
because we took out
mortgages for three thousand years
putting down as the first payment a blanket
and half a pack of my cigarettes
with red and green
when I become angry and completely impossible to lift
better bury me in the snow
it's freer there
quieter
I'm a sausage sandwich
under a whitening cheese roof
with my head bitten off
when driving me home
don't forget to lock all the windows
check the overhead cupboards and niches
quiet
quiet
little one, quiet
I'm not taking you into my
existential binge
you cry here in your spare time
others are already going to write about me there
and I'll take them with me

alena.title: SHELLING AND THE HOWL OF SIRENS CANNOT SILENCE THE LILACS
alena.text:
shelling and the howl of sirens cannot silence the lilacs
Yuri Voronov

shelling and the howl of sirens
cannot silence the lilacs,
and even behind a pile of bodies
in the heat there is enough shade
not to melt in hellish flame,
not to glaze over like a brick.
we'll cover ourselves from above with a banner
with Jesus's kind little face,
he'll protect us from asps,
from all the filthy devils.
well yes, it's a little dangerous here,
but life is more fun that way!
it never rains ---
that means the sky isn't crying.
and boats sail along the Styx ---
I haven't been to the other side.
it's almost always like a bathhouse here:
it smells of smoke and the viscosity of tar.
stay with us forever:
here the sun won't blind your eyes,
there will never be winter,
ice will never freeze.
want to play snowballs again?
you'll stop wanting to, that too will pass.
everything will pass, the main thing is to believe.
everyone in hell is destined to forget
that once an enormous swan
was a duckling and knew the word death.
you'll forget the imperial standards,
anarchist shouts and anthems,
and eyes flooded with pepper,
and the one among them who went to prison first.
you'll forget your village childhood,
your father's shouting (he's with us too),
the eternal lump freezing in your throat,
the mandatory quiet hour.
you'll forget how the biggest heartthrob in class
pulled your braids.
you'll forget collar tabs, lapel mics,
the discontent of the masses.
you'll forget your loneliness.
you'll forget what home smells like.
if you're here, then it's all over ---
God has already signed the sentence.
there are gentlemen here in Rolls-Royces ---
don't look into their empty eyes.
the main thing is don't be afraid,
I won't let anyone hurt you.
we're simple people, we don't need much ---
just some shade and the face of Christ.
stay with us forever,
the bolt on the door is already shut.
no one stands above us here,
freedom is branded on the skin here.
stuff dynamite inside yourself,
blow it up --- but it won't help.
there's no way for us to get out of here,
but in the lull of basalt walls
the whole meaning of the universe rests:
history is written only in blood,
now you're a person, not a number.
you became a person, but you were --- loose change.

alena.title: DO YOU REMEMBER HOW THE SUN PEELED OUR SHOULDERS,
alena.text:
do you remember how the sun peeled our shoulders,
do you remember how your hair turned to straw there,
your dad drank cold Krušovice
smelled of triple cologne from Napoleon.
sand in your underwear, fruit ice on a stick,
watermelons, apricots, feijoa.
horses walked in the city park there
and Roma kids stole from the table.
the air conditioner worked without stopping,
and the draft chilled you right down to a runny nose,
but you wouldn't admit it to your mother,
chasing pigeons almost until night.
the embankment smelled of something fresh,
an old man loudly offered corn,
and rustling waters attacked the breakwaters,
little boats searched for their berth.
you ate shashlik and salads in the cafeteria,
at the hotel breakfast you choked down semolina porridge,
but you loved lemon-colored sunsets
and the girl who was older.
all of it was as if in some movie,
and in the gray city nostalgia devours you:
how in the south, criminally long ago,
you once were. for the last time.
for the first time.

alena.title: TO Y.
alena.text:
from the woman in me --- the eyes and the boots.
both reflect red.
and beeps will run down the receiver ---
determination is pretty womanly too, after all!
to call you, to want to hear your voice,
and gather pieces of my feelings:
go on, throw me away like dirty socks
onto the floor, and kick me under the couch.

a boot to the kidneys, adrenochrome ---
I'll look into you like a wild beast.
you stand there with an excessively gentle face:
“we'll work through this, trust me.”
and I'm like apples in chicken broth ---
I'm a sign of poverty, an abomination in the flesh.
you're too soy, too self-aware, too innocent.
I'll wipe myself with your nth “sorry” ---
I have too many disappointments
and too much hatred for the woman in myself,
because the feminine in me wounds me harder
than the lack of masculinity in your pink self.

the sunset descends like a balding Furby,
(it looks like he and I came from the same dumpster)
I am bluish smoke expelled from lungs,
I'm leaving, close the window behind me.

alena.title: LIFE IS AN ENDLESS SEARCH FOR SOMEONE'S TRAUMAS
alena.text:
life is an endless search for someone's traumas
sit, smoke, don't count the cigarette butts
every action is one continuous haram
some kind of idiots scurry around
Allah can't see if you're under a roof
Jesus can't see because he has gone blind
only red-haired Borya sits with me
and he is as red as the streetlight
I pick at sores with a nail file
I think and want to scream
all of life is some fucking Colosseum
a game you can't finish playing
checkpoints plot branches
a kaleidoscope of quests NPCs
the ending is a little coffin somewhere under an aspen
and a profile picture with a ribbon online
get up from the pavement, hunch your shoulders again
and a cigarette smolders between your fingers
nothing here heals, nothing maims
earthly lodgers scurry back and forth
someone else's grief is gray hair at the temples
your own grief is tar somewhere in the lungs
throw away cigarette butts, drown in words
I'll make it, I only need to---

alena.title: RUSSIAN DREAM
alena.text:
Russian dream is a minimum wage of three hundred thousand,
and not having to suck dick for it.
Russian dream --- to carve on the shards of empires
that any government is a whore.
Russian dream --- vodka for free,
Russian dream --- sleeping until noon,
Russian dream --- for her feat of arms
the Motherland is flexing like crazy.
Russian dream --- lightweight combat boots,
Russian dream --- killing cops.
Russian dream --- crucifying your own heart
and heating the stove with it instead of firewood.
Russian dream --- Land Cruisers and Porsches,
Russian dream --- cut the bullshit.
life is worse for us without a dream.
Russian dream --- not lying down under a tram.
Russian dream --- pills without a prescription,
Russian dream --- a house on Rublyovka.
Russian dream --- unlimited cigarettes,
Russian dream --- indulgences from priests.
Russian God looks down at us from above
and, too lazy to send everyone to hell,
sprinkles dandruff down from his head:
here's your snow --- that's what we call it.
Russian life is survival,
Russian life is a low-budget horror.
Russian God, in Russian life grant us
something that drives out the cold.
Russian God hears no one:
Russian God switched on the boombox,
Russian God parties in Paris,
Russian God --- a second tuning fork.
Russian death waits in the alleys,
forges the hammer and sharpens the sickle.
Russian death --- the twenty-fifth hour in the knocking,
Russian death --- heroin and mephedrone.
Russian dream, Russian life, Russian God, Russian death ---
everything is pierced by a single motif:
to escape reality, hide your cybertrace,
fly away in spirit and leave the body behind.

alena.title: LITTLE SPARROW
alena.text:
I breathe stolen air
and walk on a dead man's earth
shrink to a point from my father's indifference
and look for him in a crumpled sheet
a ragged and homeless sparrow, hungry, not chirping,
sniffling with weed smokers somewhere on Lenina
temporary, all of it is temporary
but there is nothing more permanent than an alarm clock beeping
than the feeling of abandonment following you through life
than the fear of not being chosen and crushed by it.
hounded
I roar like a great beast somewhere at the feet of the fatherland
a schema-monk without the schema, dead but not given the funeral rite
dressed up according to fashion
sort of
having punched someone in the face
left until rightness, right until leftness, to
the very chord of radicalism
suffered out by meta- and postmodernism
belched out by realism
breaking into pain for the sake of these lines
not an idol not a monument not a prophet
a human being alone from birth
but a sparrow can't, it dies
under cold or rain
without a flock
hardly
will I find a flock here
I'll melt
like the first snow at the beginning of summer
not quite reaching the maternal prefix meta
and the light
at the end of the tunnel of a stretched ear
not reaching the hearing
in waves of ultrasound
heard only by dogs
who will they cry for now
who will they tear apart now
who will they pity and warm with their belly
it's fine
it's fine
the wings have simply grown under the skin like shaved hairs
temples into a vise
trepanation
crunch
I'm here mom
I'm still here mom
just a little tired
I'll lie down on the crusted snow
ballast
