falls, sinks into the thickness
covers itself with a piece of canva-
s and falls asleep
and melts
together with it
fros-
t falls
as frost
and becomes the line
of a steady pulse
silent
silent forever
with the word amen

alena.title: THE ARCHITECTURE OF A BRAND OR A NAIL
alena.text:
the architecture of a brand or a nail
the face is archetypally depersonalized
to dry up like a fish without water
to stick to the computer and the desk
to the chirp of a metronome (like cicadas)
with a floor lamp instead of a jungle tree
the cubic nature of the room, its flaws
the fractures of air inside
it is thick and smells of spotted apples
ripples with the shade of a pigeon's neck
I look out the window and can't tell
whether those are streams outside or trenches
a car alarm, the sound of warning
all bomb shelters are flooded in spring
draw roads with the cursor in Paint
so that at least one leads home
fawn like a dog over opening doors
go feral when you see the courier there
sleep by day and howl like a wolf at night
hear a hyena's laughter in the metronome
the moon will grin with heavenly meanness
the half-dark in the apartment with an obscene joke
give me back some semblance of a face
let it appear in dotted lines
endure violence in silence
pray for the architecture of relationships
stay awake and wait until someone commands “home”
and bury wasted time every day

alena.title: TO Y. 2
alena.text:
urban patchwork, a golden-domed trill ---
and I lived here, choking on cold porridge.
a farewell diesel-locomotive horn, and now
I'll inevitably have to grow older.
Soviet tables, and I'm standing,
and I'm drenched in burgundy tears.
my nightmarish sick déjà vu:
his leg feels like stone.
shadows from candles will dance over the lace of a skirt,
the rustle of a depersonalized crowd.
so much, so much in this interval,
what prayers could there be?
the blindfold creeps over the eyes,
living green over loosened earth.
details bake into a crust:
the same vodka
has fogged up on the table.
eyes lowered unbearably meekly,
a cold kiss on a white forehead.
I'm not dead I'm not dead I'm not dead
linen whitens on red velvet:
no, this is definitely not the end,
and somewhere backstage he is waiting.
where could beauty be born here,
in the ugliness of lopsided buildings,
in the awkward silence of a cemetery?
that's the kind of life exam it is.
to stay in a two-room apartment with the ghost of a family,
to stay like basement kittens.
something from the shadows looked at me,
perhaps this is the point of no return.
pull myself together, return myself to myself,
try to build a castle from fragments.
the story is banal and old ---
but why does silence
beat against my eardrums, and the reflection in the glass
is distorted by familiar features.
I'm frightened; there is so much of this in me
that hands cannot calm it.
bottles in the refrigerator bared their teeth,
two black ribbons, shot glasses, bread.
I want to fold myself into suitcases under the couch;
the burning light scorches the retina.
I've shriveled up, I'm smaller, I'm holding on.
let the outward polish fool passersby.
the same domes, urban patchwork,
and a cat beside an orphaned shoe.

alena.title: HUNCH OVER, MAKE YOURSELF SMALLER
alena.text:
hunch over, make yourself smaller
there already isn't enough of you
will it get worse?
a residual
phenomenon after a cold
your nose is blocked, sensitivity atrophied
try, wave your claw-grabbers
“your optics are invalid”
learn to be liked. that will be enough at first
until doubts
smash whatever is left of your skull
over Murino asphalt
in a world where Vivaldi still exists
Bottega Veneta
documentary films
you're still just as shapeless, atrophied
ashamed to watch TikTok clips
ashamed that all you can do is communicate, and only in person
thank them for at least not lynching you
they accept you
and while you hammer nails into your own box,
they still often sit beside you
smile, say you're still significant
(you think: not enough)
twist your mouth into a smile --- you can see it's forced
tears on apples
apples on a plate
plate on a tablecloth
tablecloth on three whales
on turtles
that have nothing to do with turtles ---
oops, I have birdies too --- self-repetition
isn't justified by its banality
when speeding up, don't stick your hands into the motor
or look, your fingers have already been chopped off
“I told you so”
grab the pitchforks
burn books in a fit of fear of God
(God is everyone who read them)
if you understood anything at all,
you'd be making cash,
not doing badly.
run out of breath. sit by the window
ignore the doubts
listen to the silence
it prophesies a rise and another fall
atrophy of the face
muscles
tendons
your fat could be rendered into soap
then nitroglycerin, like in a pop thriller
hardly any greater use
been there, know it
and sleep
sleep while you can sleep
sleep while you can change nothing
and whine
whine again about your poverty of words
while this dozen heads
listens to you and even bursts into applause
theatrical pause
meager water from the eyes
nicely done, brother
intermission
you drown in a text as long as life
in childhood grievances
but we could have
oh how much more we could have done here
knock back a shot
they'll survive

alena.title: A CRAMPED BODY
alena.text:
a cramped body
a body far too cramped
roared
hunched over
though it imagined
“I'm so good, people love me so much”
what is the value of that love
“help”
every step like a latent cry for help
well, seriously...
better go away, have a cry
maybe at least the roar will turn out
worthwhile
